    <h1>SC1000 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1000">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h1
id="-is-not-used-specially-and-should-therefore-be-escaped"><code>$</code>
is not used specially and should therefore be escaped.</h1>
<p><em>Note: Removed in <a
href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/blob/2e5c56b27034492134be1538c1e1e6a533ca791a/CHANGELOG.md#removed-1">v0.3.3
- 2014-05-29</a></em></p>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;$&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="dt">\$</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p><code>$</code> is special in double quotes, but there are some cases
where it's interpreted literally:</p>
<ol>
<li>Following a backslash: <code>echo "\$"</code></li>
<li>In a context where the shell can't make sense of it, such as at the
end of the string, (<code>"foo$"</code>) or before some constructs
(<code>"$'foo'"</code>).</li>
</ol>
<p>To avoid relying on strange and shell-specific behavior, any
<code>$</code> intended to be literal should be escaped with a
backslash.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>
</html>

    <h1>SC1001 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1001">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="this-o-will-be-a-regular-o-in-this-context">This <code>\o</code>
will be a regular 'o' in this context.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Want literal backslash</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> Yay <span class="dt">\o</span>/</span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Want other characters</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">bell</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="dt">\a</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&#39;Yay \o/&#39;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">bell</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="bu">printf</span> <span class="st">&#39;\a&#39;</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You have escaped something that has no special meaning when escaped.
The backslash will be simply be ignored.</p>
<p>If the backslash was supposed to be literal, single quote or escape
it.</p>
<p>If you wanted it to expand to something, rewrite the expression to
use <code>printf</code> (or in bash, <code>$'\t'</code>). If the
sequence in question is <code>\n</code>, <code>\t</code> or
<code>\r</code>, you instead get a <a href="SC1012">SC1012</a> that
describes this.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>None. ShellCheck (as of <a
href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/commit/31bb02d6b794f248f732643d744f63bec615b1f7">2017-07-03</a>,
commit <a
href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/commit/31bb02d6b794f248f732643d744f63bec615b1f7"><code>31bb02d6</code></a>)
will not warn when the first letter of a command is unnecessarily
escaped, as this is frequently used to suppress aliases
interactively.</p>

<ul>
<li><a
href="https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Aliases.html"
class="uri">https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Aliases.html</a></li>
<li><a
href="https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Quoting.html"
class="uri">https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Quoting.html</a></li>
<li><a href="https://tiswww.case.edu/php/chet/bash/bash.html"
class="uri">https://tiswww.case.edu/php/chet/bash/bash.html</a></li>
</ul>

    <h2 id="want-to-escape-a-single-quote-echo-this-is-how-its-done">Want to
escape a single quote?
<code>echo 'This is how it'\''s done'</code>.</h2>
<p>(Note: in v0.4.6, the error message was accidentally missing the
backslash)</p>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&#39;This is not how it\&#39;</span>s done<span class="st">&#39;.</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&#39;This is how it&#39;</span><span class="dt">\&#39;</span><span class="st">&#39;s done&#39;</span>.</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale</h3>
<p>In POSIX shell, the shell cares about nothing but another
single-quote to terminate the quoted segment. Not even backslashes are
interpreted.</p>
<p><a
href="http://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/utilities/V3_chap02.html#tag_18_02_02">POSIX.1
Shell Command Language § 2.2.2 Single Quotes</a>:</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Enclosing characters in single-quotes ( <code>''</code> ) shall
preserve the literal value of each character within the single-quotes. A
single-quote cannot occur within single-quotes.</p>
</blockquote>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>If you want your single-quoted string to end in a backslash, you can
rewrite as <code>'string'\\</code> or <a href="ignore">ignore</a> this
warning.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>
</html>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1004 – This backslash+linefeed is literal. Break outside single quotes if you just want to break the line.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1004 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1004">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="this-backslashlinefeed-is-literal-break-outside-single-quotes-if-you-just-want-to-break-the-line">This
backslash+linefeed is literal. Break outside single quotes if you just
want to break the line.</h2>
<p>(This warning was retired after v0.7.2 due to low signal-to-noise
ratio)</p>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&#39;This is long \</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">piece of text&#39;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&#39;This is a long &#39;</span><span class="dt">\</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">&#39;piece of text&#39;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You have a single-quoted string containing a backslash followed by a
linefeed (newline). Unlike double-quotes or unquoted strings, this has
no special meaning. The string will contain a literal backslash and a
linefeed.</p>
<p>If you wanted to break the line but not add a linefeed to the string,
stop the single quote, break the line, and reopen it. This is
demonstrated in the correct code.</p>
<p>If you wanted to break the line and also include the linefeed as a
literal, you don't need a backslash:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&#39;This is a multi-line string</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">with an embedded linefeed&#39;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you do want a string containing a literal backslash+linefeed
combo, such as with <code>sed</code>, you can <a
href="ignore">ignore</a> this warning.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1007 – Remove space after `=` if trying to assign a value (or for empty string, use `var=""` ... ).</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1007 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1007">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h1
id="remove-space-after--if-trying-to-assign-a-value-or-for-empty-string-use-var--">Remove
space after <code>=</code> if trying to assign a value (or for empty
string, use <code>var=""</code> ... ).</h1>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># I want programs to show text in Dutch!</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">LANGUAGE</span><span class="op">=</span> <span class="fu">nl</span></span></code></pre></div>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># I want to run the nl command with English error messages!</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">LANGUAGE</span><span class="op">=</span> <span class="fu">nl</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># I want programs to show text in Dutch!</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">LANGUAGE</span><span class="op">=</span>nl</span></code></pre></div>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># I want to run the nl command with English error messages!</span></span>
<span id="cb4-2"><a href="#cb4-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">LANGUAGE</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&#39;&#39;</span> <span class="fu">nl</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>It's easy to think that <code>LANGUAGE= nl</code> would assign
<code>"nl"</code> to the variable <code>LANGUAGE</code>. It doesn't.</p>
<p>Instead, it runs <code>nl</code> (the "number lines" command) and
sets <code>LANGUAGE</code> to an empty string in its environment.</p>
<p>Since trying to assign values this way is a common mistake,
ShellCheck warns about it and asks you to be explicit when assigning
empty strings (except for <code>IFS</code>, due to the common
<code>IFS= read ..</code> idiom).</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>If you're familiar with this behavior and feel that the explicit
version is unnecessary, you can <a href="ignore">ignore</a> it.</p>

<ul>

class="uri">https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Shell-Parameters.html</a></li>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1008 – This shebang was unrecognized. ShellCheck only supports sh/bash/dash/ksh. Add a 'shell' directive to specify.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />

  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1008 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1008">See this page on GitHub</a>

    <hr />
    <h2
id="this-shebang-was-unrecognized-shellcheck-only-supports-shbashdashksh-add-a-shell-directive-to-specify">This
shebang was unrecognized. ShellCheck only supports sh/bash/dash/ksh. Add
a 'shell' directive to specify.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/mywrapper</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/mywrapper</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># shellcheck shell=bash</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You have specified a shebang that ShellCheck doesn't recognize. This
can be due to invoking the script via a wrapper, specifying a dummy like
<code>#!/bin/false</code> to prevent execution, or trying to check a
script for a non-Bourne shell or tool.</p>
<p>If this really is a sh/bash/dash/ksh script, please add a
<code>shell</code> directive after the shebang to tell ShellCheck how to
interpret the script, as in the example. You can also specify the shell
with the <code>-s</code> flag.</p>
<p>If this is a script in some other language, like
<code>#!/bin/sed</code> for a <code>sed</code> script, then sorry --
ShellCheck does not support <code>sed</code>, <code>awk</code>,
<code>expect</code> scripts. It only supports Bourne style shell
scripts.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>

href="https://mywiki.wooledge.org/BashProgramming?highlight=%28shebang%29#Shebang"

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC1010 – Use semicolon or linefeed before `done` (or quote to make it literal).</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1010 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1010">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="use-semicolon-or-linefeed-before-done-or-quote-to-make-it-literal">Use
semicolon or linefeed before <code>done</code> (or quote to make it
literal).</h2>
<p>(or <code>do</code> <code>then</code>, <code>fi</code>,
<code>esac</code>)</p>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> f <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="pp">*</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">do</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$f</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> done</span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="va">$f</span> is done</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> f <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="pp">*</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">do</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$f</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$f</span><span class="st"> is done&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a keyword like <code>done</code>, <code>then</code>,
<code>fi</code>, <code>esac</code>, etc used as the argument of a
command. This means that the shell will interpret it as a literal string
rather than a shell keyword. To be interpreted as a keyword, it must be
the first word in the line (i.e. after <code>;</code>,
<code>&amp;</code> or a linefeed).</p>
<p>In the example, <code>echo "$f" done</code> is the same as
<code>echo "$f" "done"</code>, and the <code>done</code> does not
terminate the loop. This is fixed by terminating the <code>echo</code>
command with a <code>;</code> so that the <code>done</code> is the first
word in the next line.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>If you're intentionally using <code>done</code> as a literal, you can
quote it to make this clear to ShellCheck (and also human readers), e.g.
instead of <code>echo Task is done</code>, use
<code>echo "Task is done"</code>. This makes no difference to the shell,
but it will silence this warning.</p>
<p>From POSIX-2018, section "C.2.10 Shell Grammar," regarding the
syntax, <code>if (false) then (echo x) else (echo y) fi</code>: <a
href="https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/xrat/V4_xcu_chap02.html#tag_23_02_10"
class="uri">https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/xrat/V4_xcu_chap02.html#tag_23_02_10</a></p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>
</html>

    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />

  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1011 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1011">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="this-apostrophe-terminated-the-single-quoted-string">This
apostrophe terminated the single quoted string!</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&#39;Nothing so needs reforming as other peoples&#39;</span> habits.<span class="st">&#39;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&#39;Nothing so needs reforming as other peoples&#39;</span><span class="dt">\&#39;</span><span class="st">&#39; habits.&#39;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Nothing so needs reforming as other peoples&#39; habits.&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>When writing a string in single-quotes, you have to make sure that
any apostrophes in the text don't accidentally terminate the
single-quoted string prematurely.</p>
<p>Escape them properly (see the correct code) or switch quotes to avoid
the problem.</p>
<h3 id="additional-options">Additional options:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&#39;...peoples\ habits.&#39;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-2"><a href="#cb4-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">...peoples\ habits.</span></span></code></pre></div>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb5"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb5-1"><a href="#cb5-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> echo <span class="st">$&#39;...peoples</span><span class="dt">\x27</span><span class="st"> habits.&#39;</span></span>
<span id="cb5-2"><a href="#cb5-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">...peoples</span><span class="st">&#39; habits.</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>

class="uri">https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Quoting.html</a></p>

    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC1012 – `\t` is just literal `t` here. For tab, use `"$(printf '\t')"` instead.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1012 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1012">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="t-is-just-literal-t-here-for-tab-use-printf-t-instead"><code>\t</code>
is just literal <code>t</code> here. For tab, use
<code>"$(printf '\t')"</code> instead.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Want tab</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> var=foo<span class="dt">\t</span>bar</span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> printf <span class="st">&#39;&lt;%s&gt;\n&#39;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">&lt;</span>footbar<span class="op">&gt;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb1-6"><a href="#cb1-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> var=foo<span class="dt">\\</span>tbar</span>
<span id="cb1-7"><a href="#cb1-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> printf <span class="st">&#39;&lt;%s&gt;\n&#39;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-8"><a href="#cb1-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">&lt;</span>foo\tbar<span class="op">&gt;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Want newline</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> var=foo<span class="dt">\n</span>bar</span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> printf <span class="st">&#39;&lt;%s&gt;\n&#39;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">&lt;</span>foonbar<span class="op">&gt;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> var=foo<span class="dt">\\</span>nbar</span>
<span id="cb2-7"><a href="#cb2-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> printf <span class="st">&#39;&lt;%s&gt;\n&#39;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-8"><a href="#cb2-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">&lt;</span>foo\nbar<span class="op">&gt;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> var=<span class="st">&quot;foo</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="bu">printf</span> <span class="st">&#39;\t&#39;</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st">bar&quot;</span>  <span class="co"># As suggested in warning</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> printf <span class="st">&#39;&lt;%s&gt;\n&#39;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">&lt;</span>foo    <span class="ex">bar</span><span class="op">&gt;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb3-5"><a href="#cb3-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> var=<span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="bu">printf</span> <span class="st">&#39;foo\tbar&#39;</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st">&quot;</span>  <span class="co"># Equivalent alternative</span></span>
<span id="cb3-6"><a href="#cb3-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> printf <span class="st">&#39;&lt;%s&gt;\n&#39;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-7"><a href="#cb3-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">&lt;</span>foo    <span class="ex">bar</span><span class="op">&gt;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> <span class="co"># Literal, quoted newline</span></span>
<span id="cb4-2"><a href="#cb4-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> line=<span class="st">&quot;foo</span></span>
<span id="cb4-3"><a href="#cb4-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">&gt; bar&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-4"><a href="#cb4-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> printf <span class="st">&#39;&lt;%s&gt;\n&#39;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$line</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-5"><a href="#cb4-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">&lt;</span>foo</span>
<span id="cb4-6"><a href="#cb4-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">bar</span><span class="op">&gt;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb5"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb5-1"><a href="#cb5-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> <span class="co"># Newline using ANSI-C quoting</span></span>
<span id="cb5-2"><a href="#cb5-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> line=<span class="st">$&#39;foo</span><span class="dt">\n</span><span class="st">bar&#39;</span></span>
<span id="cb5-3"><a href="#cb5-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> printf <span class="st">&#39;&lt;%s&gt;\n&#39;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$line</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb5-4"><a href="#cb5-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">&lt;</span>foo</span>
<span id="cb5-5"><a href="#cb5-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">bar</span><span class="op">&gt;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck has found a <code>\t</code>, <code>\n</code> or
<code>\r</code> in a context where they just become regular letters
<code>t</code>, <code>n</code> or <code>r</code>. Most likely, it was
intended as a tab, newline or carriage return.</p>
<p>To generate such characters (plus other less common ones including
<code>\a</code>, <code>\f</code> and octal escapes) , use
<code>printf</code> as in the example. The exception is for newliness
that would be stripped by command substitution; in these cases, use a
literal quoted newline instead.</p>
<p>Other characters like <code>\z</code> generate a <a
href="SC1001">SC1001</a> info message, as the intent is less
certain.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>

href="https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Bash-Builtins.html#index-printf"

<a

  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1014 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1014">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="use-if-cmd-then--to-check-exit-code-or-if--cmd----to-check-output">Use
<code>if cmd; then ..</code> to check exit code, or
<code>if [ "$(cmd)" = .. ]</code> to check output.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># WRONG</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> grep -q pattern <span class="er">file</span> <span class="ex">]</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Found a match&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># WRONG</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="ot">! </span><span class="kw">[[</span> logname <span class="ot">==</span> <span class="va">$LOGNAME</span> <span class="kw">]]</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Possible </span><span class="kw">`</span><span class="fu">su</span><span class="kw">`</span><span class="st"> shell&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="fu">grep</span> <span class="at">-q</span> pattern file</span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Found a match&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="ot">! </span><span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">logname</span><span class="va">)</span> <span class="ot">==</span> <span class="va">$LOGNAME</span> <span class="kw">]]</span></span>
<span id="cb4-2"><a href="#cb4-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb4-3"><a href="#cb4-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Possible </span><span class="kw">`</span><span class="fu">su</span><span class="kw">`</span><span class="st"> shell&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-4"><a href="#cb4-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p><code>[ ... ]</code> as shell syntax is a simple command that tests
for whether certain conditions are true or false, such as whether the
value assigned to a variable has a non-zero length
(<code>[ -n "${foo}" ]</code>) or whether a file system object is a
directory (<code>[ -d "${dir}" ]</code>).
<code>If-then-(elif-then)-else-fi</code> statements are logical
constructs which themselves contain lists of commands which can include
simple commands.</p>
<p><code>[</code> is just regular command, like <code>whoami</code> or
<code>grep</code>, but with a funny name (see
<code>ls -l /bin/[</code>). It's a shorthand for <code>test</code>.
<code>[[</code> is similar to both <code>[</code> and <code>test</code>,
but <code>[[</code> offers some additional unary operators, such as '=~'
the regular expression comparison operator. It allows one to use
extglobs such as <code>@(foo|bar)</code> (a "bashism"), among some other
less commonly used features.</p>
<p><code>[[</code>, <code>[</code> and <code>test</code> are often used
within <code>if...fi</code> constructs in the conditional commands
position: which is between the 'if' and the 'then.'</p>
<p>There are certain shell syntaxes which can be wrapped
<strong>directly</strong> around simple commands, in particular:</p>
<ul>
<li>(1) <code>{ ...;}</code>, group commands,</li>
<li>(2) <code>$( ... )</code>, command substitutions,</li>
<li>(3) <code>&lt;( ... )</code> and <code>&gt;( ... )</code>, process
substitutions,</li>
<li>(4) <code>( ... )</code>, subshells, and</li>
<li>(5) <code>$(( ... ))</code> and <code>(( ... ))</code>, arithmetic
evaluations.</li>
</ul>
<p>Some examples include:</p>
<ul>
<li>(1) <code>{ echo {a..z}; echo {0..9};} &gt; ~/f</code>,</li>
<li>(2) <code>[[ $(logname) == $LOGNAME ]]</code>,</li>
<li>(3) <code>readarray -t files &lt; &lt;( find ...)</code>,</li>
<li>(4) <code>(cd /foo || exit 1; tar ...)</code>, and</li>
<li>(5)
<code>dd bs=$((2**12)) count=1 if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/zeroed-block</code>,
respectively.</li>
</ul>
<p>Note how in example (2) <code>logname</code> is enclosed
<strong>directly</strong> within a command substitution, which is itself
enclosed within a <code>[[</code> reserved word / conditional expression
/ compound command.</p>
<p>If you want to check the exit status of a certain command, use that
command directly as demonstrated in the correct code, above.</p>
<p>If you want to check the output of a command, use
<code>"$(..)"</code> to get its output, and then use
<code>test</code>/<code>[</code> or <code>[[</code> to do a string
comparison:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb5"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb5-1"><a href="#cb5-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Check output of `whoami` against the string `root`</span></span>
<span id="cb5-2"><a href="#cb5-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">whoami</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;root&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb5-3"><a href="#cb5-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb5-4"><a href="#cb5-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Running as root&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb5-5"><a href="#cb5-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related Resources:</h3>
<p>For more information, see <a
href="http://mywiki.wooledge.org/BashPitfalls#if_.5Bgrep_foo_myfile.5D">this
problem in the Bash Pitfall</a> list, or generally <a
href="http://mywiki.wooledge.org/BashGuide/TestsAndConditionals">Tests
and Conditionals</a> in the wooledge.org BashGuide</p>
<ul>
<li><a
href="https://stackoverflow.com/questions/2480584/how-do-i-use-a-file-grep-comparison-inside-a-bash-if-else-statement">How
do I use a file grep comparison inside a bash if/else

<li><a
href="https://mywiki.wooledge.org/BashPitfalls#if_.5Bgrep_foo_myfile.5D">Bash
Pitfalls: <code>if [grep foo myfile]</code></a></li>

  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1015 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1015">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="this-is-a-unicode-double-quote-delete-and-retype-it">This is a
Unicode double quote. Delete and retype it.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> “hello world”</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;hello world&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Blog software and word processors frequently replaces ASCII quotes
<code>""</code> with fancy Unicode quotes, <code>“”</code>. To Bash,
Unicode quotes are considered regular literals and not quotes at
all.</p>
<p>Simply delete them and retype them in your editor.</p>
<h3 id="status">Status:</h3>
<p>This error was retired after 0.4.5. In this version and earlier,
ShellCheck parsed slanted quotes as a valid double quote. This meant
that the warning could not simply be ignored. It has since been replaced
by <a href="SC1110">SC1110</a> (outside quotes) and <a
href="SC1111">SC1111</a> (inside double-quotes).</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>If you really want literal Unicode double quotes, you can put them in
single-quotes (or Unicode single-quotes in double-quotes) to make
ShellCheck ignore them, e.g.,</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">printf</span> <span class="st">&#39;Warning: “wakeonlan” is not installed.\n&#39;</span></span></code></pre></div>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1016 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1016">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="this-is-a-unicode-single-quote-delete-and-retype-it">This is a
Unicode single quote. Delete and retype it.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> ‘hello world’</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&#39;hello world&#39;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Some software, like macOS, Microsoft Word, and WordPress, may
automatically replace your regular quotes with slanted Unicode quotes.
Try deleting and retyping them, and/or disable “smart quotes” in your
editor or OS.</p>
<h3 id="status">Status:</h3>
<p>This error was retired after 0.4.5. In this version and earlier,
ShellCheck parsed slanted quotes as a valid double-quote. This meant
that the warning could not simply be ignored. It has since been replaced
by <a href="SC1110">SC1110</a> (outside quotes) and <a
href="SC1112">SC1112</a> (inside single-quotes).</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>If you want to use typographic single-quotes, you can put them in
double-quotes (or typographic double-quotes in single-quotes) to make
ShellCheck ignore them, e.g.,</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">printf</span> <span class="st">&quot;Warning: ‘wakeonlan’ is not installed.\n&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1017 – Literal carriage return. Run script through `tr -d '\r'` .</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1017 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1017">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="literal-carriage-return-run-script-through-tr--d-r-">Literal
carriage return. Run script through <code>tr -d '\r'</code> .</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<pre class="console"><code>$ cat -v myscript
#!/bin/sh^M
echo &quot;Hello World&quot;^M</code></pre>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<pre class="console"><code>$ cat -v myscript
#!/bin/sh
echo &quot;Hello World&quot;</code></pre>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>The script uses Windows/MS-DOS style <code>\r\n</code> line
terminators instead of Unix-style <code>\n</code> terminators. The
additional <code>\r</code> aka <code>^M</code> aka carriage return
characters will be treated literally, and results in all sorts strange
bugs and messages.</p>
<p>You can verify this with <code>cat -v yourfile</code> and see whether
or not each line ends with a <code>^M</code>. To delete them, open the
file in your editor and save the file as "Unix", "Unix/macOS Format",
<code>:set ff=unix</code> or similar if it supports it.</p>
<p>If you don't know how to get your editor to save a file with Unix
line terminators, you can use <code>tr</code>:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">tr</span> <span class="at">-d</span> <span class="st">&#39;\r&#39;</span> <span class="op">&lt;</span> badscript <span class="op">&gt;</span> goodscript</span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">or</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">dos2unix</span> badscript</span></code></pre></div>
<p>This will read a script <code>badscript</code> with possible carriage
returns, and write <code>goodscript</code> without them.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://mywiki.wooledge.org/BashFAQ/052">BashFaq: How do I
convert a file from MS-DOS format to Unix format (remove CRs from CR-LF
line terminators)?</a></li>
<li><a
href="https://stackoverflow.com/questions/39527571/are-shell-scripts-sensitive-to-encoding-and-line-endings">StackOverflow:
Are shell-scripts sensitive to encoding and line-endings?</a></li>
</ul>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1018 – This is a Unicode non-breaking space. Delete it and retype as space.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1018 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1018">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h1
id="this-is-a-unicode-non-breaking-space-delete-it-and-retype-as-space">This
is a Unicode non-breaking space. Delete it and retype as space.</h1>
<p>You copy-pasted some code, probably from a blog or web site, which
for formatting reasons contained Unicode no-break spaces or Unicode
zero-width spaces instead of regular spaces or in words.</p>
<p>To humans, a zero-width space is invisible and a non-breaking space
is indistinguishable from a regular space, but the shell does not
agree.</p>
<p>If you have just a few, delete the indicated space/word and retype
it. If you have tons, do a search-and-replace in your editor (copy-paste
an offending space into the search field, and type a regular space into
the replace field), or use the following command to remove them:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">sed</span> <span class="at">-e</span> <span class="st">$&#39;s/</span><span class="dt">\xC2\xA0</span><span class="st">/ /g&#39;</span> <span class="at">-e</span> <span class="st">$&#39;s/</span><span class="dt">\xE2\x80\x8b</span><span class="st">//g&#39;</span> <span class="at">-i</span> yourfile</span></code></pre></div>
<p>On macOS, a non-breaking space can be inserted into most programs by
holding <kbd>⌥ Option</kbd>+<kbd>Space</kbd>.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>

    <h2 id="expected-this-to-be-an-argument-to-the-unary-condition">Expected

<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-x</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-x</span> <span class="st">&quot;myfile&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span></code></pre></div>

    <hr />
    <h2 id="you-need-a-space-before-the--or-">You need a space before the
<code>]</code> or <code>]]</code></h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$STUFF</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;&quot;</span>]<span class="er">;</span> <span class="er">then</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$STUFF</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">then</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Bourne shells are very whitespace sensitive. Adding or removing
spaces can drastically alter the meaning of a script. In these cases,
ShellCheck has noticed that you're missing a space at the position
indicated.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>None.</p>
<h3 id="ignore">Ignore</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># shellcheck disable=SC1020</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$STUFF</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;&quot;</span>]<span class="er">;</span> <span class="er">then</span></span></code></pre></div>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1026 – If grouping expressions inside `[[..]]`, use `( .. )`.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1026 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1026">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="if-grouping-expressions-inside--use---">If grouping expressions
inside <code>[..](..)</code>, use <code>( .. )</code>.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> [ a <span class="kw">||</span> b ] <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> c <span class="kw">]]</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> [ a -o <span class="er">b</span> <span class="ex">]</span> <span class="at">-a</span> c ]]</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="op">(</span> a <span class="kw">||</span> b <span class="op">)</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> c <span class="kw">]]</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="dt">\(</span> a -o <span class="er">b</span> <span class="ex">\)</span> <span class="at">-a</span> c ]]  <span class="co"># or  { [ a ] || [ b ]; } &amp;&amp; [ c ]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p><code>[ .. ]</code> should not be used to group subexpressions inside
<code>[[ .. ]]</code> or <code>[ .. ]</code> statements.</p>
<p>For <code>[[ .. ]]</code>, use regular parentheses.</p>
<p>For <code>[ .. ]</code>, either use escaped parentheses, or
preferably rewrite the expression into multiple <code>[ .. ]</code>
joined with <code>&amp;&amp;</code>, <code>||</code> and
<code>{ ..; }</code> groups. The latter is preferred because
<code>[ .. ]</code> is undefined for more than 4 arguments in POSIX.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://mywiki.wooledge.org/BashPitfalls#pf11">Bash
Pitfalls:
<code>if [ [ a = b ] &amp;&amp; [ c = d ] ]; then ...</code></a></li>
<li><a
href="http://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/utilities/test.html">POSIX
<code>test</code></a></li>
</ul>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC1028 – In `[..]` you have to escape `\( \)` or preferably combine `[..]` expressions.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1028 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1028">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="in--you-have-to-escape---or-preferably-combine--expressions">In
<code>[..]</code> you have to escape <code>\( \)</code> or preferably
combine <code>[..]</code> expressions.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-e</span> ~/.bashrc <span class="ot">-a</span> <span class="er">(</span> -x /bin/dash <span class="ot">-o</span> <span class="ot">-x</span> /bin/ash <span class="er">)</span> <span class="ex">]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<p>In POSIX:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-e</span> ~/.bashrc <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span>  <span class="kw">{</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-x</span> /bin/dash <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="kw">||</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-x</span> /bin/ash <span class="bu">]</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="kw">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Obsolete XSI syntax:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-e</span> ~/.bashrc <span class="ot">-a</span> <span class="dt">\(</span> -x /bin/dash <span class="ot">-o</span> <span class="ot">-x</span> /bin/ash <span class="er">\)</span> <span class="ex">]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p><code>[</code> is implemented as a regular command, so <code>(</code>
is not special.</p>
<p>The preferred way is not to group inside <code>[ .. ]</code> and
instead compose multiple <code>[ .. ]</code> statements using the
shell's <code>&amp;&amp;</code>, <code>||</code> and
<code>{ ..; }</code> syntax, since this is well defined by POSIX.</p>
<p>Some shells, such as Bash, support grouping with
<code>\( .. \)</code>, but this is an obsolete XSI-only extension.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1029 – In `[[..]]` you shouldn't escape `(` or `)`.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1029 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1029">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="in--you-shouldnt-escape--or-">In <code>[..](..)</code> you
shouldn't escape <code>(</code> or <code>)</code>.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="ot">-e</span> ~/.bashrc <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="dt">\(</span> -x /bin/dash <span class="kw">||</span> <span class="ot">-x</span> /bin/ash <span class="dt">\)</span> <span class="kw">]]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="ot">-e</span> ~/.bashrc <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="op">(</span> <span class="ot">-x</span> /bin/dash <span class="kw">||</span> <span class="ot">-x</span> /bin/ash <span class="op">)</span> <span class="kw">]]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You don't have to -- and can't -- escape <code>(</code> or
<code>)</code> inside a <code>[[ .. ]]</code> expression like you do in
<code>[ .. ]</code>. Just remove the escaping.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1033 – Test expression was opened with double `[[` but closed with single `]`. Make sure they match.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1033 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1033">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="test-expression-was-opened-with-double--but-closed-with-single--make-sure-they-match">Test
expression was opened with double <code>[[</code> but closed with single
<code>]</code>. Make sure they match.</h2>
<p>(or <a href="SC1034">SC1034</a> for vice versa)</p>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="ot">-z</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> ]</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="ot">-z</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="kw">]]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a test expression <code>[ ... ]</code> (POSIX) or
<code>[[ ... ]]</code> (ksh/bash), but where the opening and closing
brackets did not match (i.e. <code>[[ .. ]</code> or
<code>[ .. ]]</code>). The brackets need to match up to work.</p>
<p>Note in particular that <code>[..]</code> do <em>not</em> work like
parentheses in other languages. You can not do:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Invalid</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> x ] <span class="kw">||</span> [ y <span class="kw">]]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>You would instead use two separate test expressions joined by
<code>||</code>:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Valid basic test expressions (sh/bash/ksh)</span></span>
<span id="cb4-2"><a href="#cb4-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> x <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="kw">||</span> <span class="bu">[</span> y <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb4-3"><a href="#cb4-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb4-4"><a href="#cb4-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Valid extended test expressions (bash/ksh)</span></span>
<span id="cb4-5"><a href="#cb4-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> x <span class="kw">]]</span> <span class="kw">||</span> <span class="kw">[[</span> y <span class="kw">]]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

id="test-expression-was-opened-with-single--but-closed-with-double--make-sure-they-match">Test

  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC1035 – You need a space here</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1035 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1035">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="you-need-a-space-here">You need a space here</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="ex">![-z</span> foo ]<span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">then</span> <span class="fu">true</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">fi</span> <span class="co"># if command `[-z&#39; w/ args `foo&#39;, `]&#39; fails..</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="ot">! </span><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-z</span> foo <span class="bu">]</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">then</span> <span class="fu">true</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">fi</span> <span class="co"># if command `[&#39; w/ args `-z&#39;, `foo&#39;, `]&#39; fails..</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Bourne shells are very whitespace sensitive. Adding or removing
spaces can drastically alter the meaning of a script. In these cases,
ShellCheck has noticed that you're missing a space at the position
indicated.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>ShellCheck does not understand <a
href="https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/History-Interaction.html">Bash
History Expansion</a>, an interactive shell feature also using
<code>!</code> (such as <code>!!</code> to expand to the previous
command).</p>
<p>These features are disabled by default in shells and very rarely used
in scripts, but may occasionally be found in interactively sourced files
like <code>.bashrc</code>. Please ignore the error in these cases.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC1036 – `(` is invalid here. Did you forget to escape it?</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1036 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1036">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="-is-invalid-here-did-you-forget-to-escape-it"><code>(</code> is
invalid here. Did you forget to escape it?</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="er">(</span><span class="ex">foo</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="ex">bar</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<p>Depends on your intention:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;(foo) bar&quot;</span>  <span class="co"># Literal parentheses</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="ex">foo</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st"> bar&quot;</span> <span class="co"># Command expansion</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;foo bar&quot;</span>    <span class="co"># Tried to use parentheses for grouping or function invocation</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck expected an ordinary shell word but found an opening
parenthesis instead.</p>
<p>Determine what you intended the parenthesis to do and rewrite
accordingly. Common issues include:</p>
<ul>
<li>Wanting them to be literal, as in
<code>echo (FAIL) Some tests failed</code>. In this case, it requires
quoting.</li>
<li>Wanting command expansion, as in <code>echo Today is (date)</code>.
Add the missing <code>$</code>:
<code>echo "Today is $(date)"</code></li>
<li>Adding parentheses because other languages need them in that
context, such as <code>foo (bar, 42)</code> to call a function. This
should be <code>foo bar 42</code>. Also, shells do not support tuples or
passing arrays as single parameters.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>Bash allows some parentheses as part of assignment-like tokens to
certain commands, including <code>export</code> and <code>eval</code>.
This is a workaround in Bash to allow commands that normally would not
be valid:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">eval</span> foo=<span class="er">(</span><span class="ex">bar</span><span class="kw">)</span>       <span class="co"># Valid command</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> foo=<span class="er">(</span><span class="ex">bar</span><span class="kw">)</span>       <span class="co"># Invalid syntax</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">f</span><span class="op">=</span>foo<span class="kw">;</span> <span class="bu">eval</span> <span class="va">$f</span>=<span class="er">(</span><span class="ex">bar</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="co"># Also invalid</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>In these cases, please quote the command, such as
<code>eval "foo=(bar)"</code>. This does not change the behavior, but
stops relying on Bash-specific parsing quirks.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC1037 – Braces are required for positionals over 9, e.g. `${10}`.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1037 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1037">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="braces-are-required-for-positionals-over-9-eg-10">Braces are
required for positionals over 9, e.g. <code>${10}</code>.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Ninth parameter: </span><span class="va">$9</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Tenth parameter: </span><span class="va">$1</span><span class="st">0&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Ninth parameter: </span><span class="va">$9</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Tenth parameter: </span><span class="va">${10}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>For legacy reasons, <code>$10</code> is interpreted as the variable
<code>$1</code> followed by the literal string <code>0</code>.</p>
<p>Curly braces are needed to tell the shell that both digits are part
of the parameter expansion.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>If you wanted the trailing digits to be literal, <code>${1}0</code>
will make this clear to both humans and ShellCheck.</p>
<p>In <code>dash</code>, <code>$10</code> is (<a
href="https://gnu.org/s/autoconf/manual/html_node/Shell-Substitutions.html">wrongly</a>)
interpreted as <code>${10}</code>, so some 'reversed' care should also
be taken:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">bash</span> <span class="at">-c</span> <span class="st">&#39;set a b c d e f g h i j; echo $10 ${1}0&#39;</span> <span class="co"># POSIX: a0 a0</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">dash</span> <span class="at">-c</span> <span class="st">&#39;set a b c d e f g h i j; echo $10 ${1}0&#39;</span> <span class="co"># WRONG: j a0</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://mywiki.wooledge.org/BashFAQ/025">BashFaq: How can I
access positional parameters after $9?</a></li>
<li><a href="https://stackoverflow.com/q/4912733">StackOverflow: How to
handle more than 10 parameters in shell</a></li>
<li><a
href="https://www.gnu.org/savannah-checkouts/gnu/autoconf/manual/html_node/Shell-Substitutions.html">Autoconf
Manual: Shell Substitutions</a> - documents some non-POSIX older shells
too</li>
</ul>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC1038 – Shells are space sensitive. Use `< <(cmd)`, not `<<(cmd)`.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1038 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1038">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="shells-are-space-sensitive-use--cmd-not-cmd">Shells are space
sensitive. Use <code>&lt; &lt;(cmd)</code>, not
<code>&lt;&lt;(cmd)</code>.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">while</span> <span class="va">IFS</span><span class="op">=</span> <span class="bu">read</span> <span class="at">-r</span> <span class="va">line</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">printf</span> <span class="st">&quot;%q\n&quot;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$line</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span> <span class="op">&lt;&lt;</span><span class="kw">(</span><span class="ex">curl</span> <span class="at">-s</span> http://example.com<span class="kw">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">while</span> <span class="va">IFS</span><span class="op">=</span> <span class="bu">read</span> <span class="at">-r</span> <span class="va">line</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">printf</span> <span class="st">&quot;%q\n&quot;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$line</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span> <span class="op">&lt;</span>  <span class="op">&lt;(</span><span class="ex">curl</span> <span class="at">-s</span> http://example.com<span class="op">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You are using <code>&lt;&lt;(</code> which is an invalid
construct.</p>
<p>You probably meant to redirect <code>&lt;</code> from process
substitution <code>&lt;(..)</code> instead. To do this, a space is
needed between the <code>&lt;</code> and <code>&lt;(..)</code>, i.e.
<code>&lt; &lt;(cmd)</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
