    <title>ShellCheck: SC1081 – Scripts are case-sensitive. Use `if`, not `If`.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1081 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1081">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="scripts-are-case-sensitive-use-if-not-if">Scripts are
case-sensitive. Use <code>if</code>, not <code>If</code>.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">If</span> true</span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">Then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;hello&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">Fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="fu">true</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;hello&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Shells are case sensitive and do not accept <code>If</code> or
<code>IF</code> in place of lowercase <code>if</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>If you're aware of this and insist on naming a function
<code>WHILE</code>, you can quote the name to prevent shellcheck from
thinking you meant <code>while</code>. Or if you really want the names,
add things like <code>alias If=if IF=if</code> to replace those keywords
and ask shellcheck to ignore them.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1082 – This file has a UTF-8 BOM. Remove it with: `LC_CTYPE=C sed '1s/^...//' < yourscript`.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1082 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1082">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="this-file-has-a-utf-8-bom-remove-it-with-lc_ctypec-sed-1s--yourscript">This
file has a UTF-8 BOM. Remove it with:
<code>LC_CTYPE=C sed '1s/^...//' &lt; yourscript</code>.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<p>This is an encoding error that can't be seen in the script itself,
but <code>cat -v</code> will show three bytes of garbage at the start of
the file:</p>
<pre class="console"><code>$ cat -v file
M-oM-;M-?#!/bin/bash
echo &quot;hello world&quot;</code></pre>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<p>The code is correct when this garbage does not appear.</p>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Some editors may save a file with a <a
href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Byte_order_mark">Byte Order Mark</a>
to mark the file as UTF-8. Shells do not understand this and will give
errors on the first line:</p>
<pre class="console"><code>$ bash myscript
myscript: line 1: #!/bin/sh: No such file or directory

$ dash myscript
myscript: 1: myscript: #!/bin/sh: not found</code></pre>
<p>To fix it, remove the byte order mark. One way of doing this is
<code>LC_CTYPE=C sed '1s/^...//' &lt; yourscript</code>. Verify that
it's not there with <code>cat -v</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>

  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC1083 – This `{`/`}` is literal. Check if `;` is missing or quote the expression.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1083 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1083">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="this--is-literal-check-if--is-missing-or-quote-the-expression">This
<code>{</code>/<code>}</code> is literal. Check if <code>;</code> is
missing or quote the expression.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">rmf()</span> <span class="kw">{</span> <span class="fu">rm</span> <span class="at">-f</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$@</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> }</span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">eval</span> echo <span class="dt">\$</span>{foo}</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">rmf()</span> <span class="kw">{</span> <span class="fu">rm</span> <span class="at">-f</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$@</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="kw">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>and</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">eval</span> <span class="st">&quot;echo </span><span class="dt">\$</span><span class="st">{foo}&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Curly brackets are normally used as syntax in parameter expansion,
command grouping and brace expansion.</p>
<p>However, if they don't appear alone at the start of an expression or
as part of a parameter or brace expansion, the shell silently treats
them as literals. This frequently indicates a bug, so ShellCheck warns
about it.</p>
<p>In the example function, the <code>}</code> is literal because it's
not at the start of an expression. We fix it by adding a <code>;</code>
before it.</p>
<p>In the example eval, the code works fine. However, we can quiet the
warning and follow good practice by adding quotes around the literal
data.</p>
<p>ShellCheck does not warn about <code>{}</code>, since this is
frequently used with <code>find</code> and rarely indicates a bug.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>This error is harmless when the curly brackets are supposed to be
literal, in e.g. <code>awk {'print $1'}</code>. However, it's cleaner
and less error prone to simply include them inside the quotes:
<code>awk '{print $1}'</code>.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>

    <h2 id="use--not--for-the-shebang">Use <code>#!</code>, not
<code>!#</code>, for the shebang.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">!#/bin/sh</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/sh</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>The shebang has been accidentally swapped. The <code>#</code> should

<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>None.</p>

    <h2 id="did-you-forget-to-move-the--after-extending-this-case-item">Did

<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre
class="sourceCode bash"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">case</span> <span class="va">$options</span> <span class="kw">in</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="ss">foobar</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> foo <span class="cf">;;</span> <span class="ss">echo</span> <span class="ss">bar;;</span></span>

<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="ss">foobar</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> foo <span class="kw">;</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> bar<span class="cf">;;</span></span>

<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>There should be no statements between <code>;;</code> and the next

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1086 – Don't use `$` on the iterator name in for loops.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1086 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1086">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="dont-use--on-the-iterator-name-in-for-loops">Don't use
<code>$</code> on the iterator name in for loops.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> <span class="va">$var</span> in <span class="pp">*</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> var <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="pp">*</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>The variable is named <code>var</code>, and can be expanded to its
value with <code>$var</code>.</p>
<p>The <code>for</code> loop expects the variable's name, not its value
(and the name can not be specified indirectly).</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>None.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1087 – Use braces when expanding arrays, e.g. `${array[idx]}` (or `${var}[..` to quiet).</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1087 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1087">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="use-braces-when-expanding-arrays-eg-arrayidx-or-var-to-quiet">Use
braces when expanding arrays, e.g. <code>${array[idx]}</code> (or
<code>${var}[..</code> to quiet).</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$array</span><span class="st">[@]&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${array</span><span class="op">[@]</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Some languages use the syntax <code>$array[index]</code> to access an
index of an arrays, but a shell will interpret this as
<code>$array</code> followed by the unrelated literal string (or glob)
<code>[index]</code>.</p>
<p>Curly braces are needed to tell the shell that the square brackets
are part of the expansion.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>If you want the square brackets to be treated literally or as a glob,
use <code>${var}[idx]</code> to prevent this warning.</p>
<p>This does not change how the script works, but clarifies your intent
to ShellCheck as well as other programmers.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC1088 – Parsing stopped here. Invalid use of parentheses?</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1088 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1088">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="parsing-stopped-here-invalid-use-of-parentheses">Parsing stopped
here. Invalid use of parentheses?</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">grep</span> ^<span class="er">(</span><span class="bu">.</span><span class="pp">*</span><span class="kw">)</span><span class="ex">\1$</span> file</span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span>myfunction<span class="kw">(</span><span class="ex">value</span><span class="kw">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">grep</span> <span class="st">&#39;^(.*)\1$&#39;</span> file</span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="ex">myfunction</span> value<span class="va">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Parentheses are shell syntax and must be used correctly.</p>
<p>For commands that expect literal parentheses, such as
<code>grep</code> or <code>find</code>, the parentheses need to be
quoted or escaped so the shell does not interpret them, but instead
passes them to the command.</p>
<p>For shell syntax, the shell does not use them the way most other
languages do, so avoid guessing at syntax based on previous experience.
In particular:</p>
<ul>
<li><p>Parentheses are NOT used to call functions.</p></li>
<li><p>Parentheses are NOT used to group expressions, except in
arithmetic contexts.</p></li>
<li><p>Parentheses are NOT used in conditional statements or
loops.</p></li>
<li><p>Parentheses are used differently in different contexts.
<code>( .. )</code>, <code>$( .. )</code>, <code>$(( .. ))</code> and
<code>var=(..)</code> are completely separate and independent structures
with different meanings, and can not be broken down into operations on
expressions in parentheses.</p>
<p>In C-like languages, <code>++</code> can't be broken down into two
<code>+</code> operations, so you can't e.g. use <code>+ +</code> or
<code>+(+)</code>. In the same way, all of the above are completely
unrelated so that you can't do <code>$(1+1)</code> or
<code>$( (1+1) )</code> in place of <code>$(( 1+1 ))</code>.</p></li>
</ul>
<p>If you are trying to use parentheses for shell syntax, look up the
actual syntax of the statement you are trying to use.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>
</html>

  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1089 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1089">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="parsing-stopped-here-is-this-keyword-correctly-matched-up">Parsing
stopped here. Is this keyword correctly matched up?</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="fu">true</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> hello</span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="fu">true</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> hello</span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>This error is typically seen when there are too many <code>fi</code>,
<code>done</code> or <code>esac</code>s, or when there's a
<code>do</code> or <code>then</code> without a corresponding
<code>while</code>, <code>for</code> or <code>if</code>. This is often
due to deleting a loop or conditional statement but not its
terminator.</p>
<p>In some cases, it can even be caused by bad quoting:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;foo</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">if [[ </span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st"> = &quot;</span>bar <span class="ex">]</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> true</span>
<span id="cb3-5"><a href="#cb3-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>In this case, the <code>if</code> ends up inside the double quotes,
leaving the <code>then</code> dangling.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1090 – Can't follow non-constant source. Use a directive to specify location</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1090 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1090">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="cant-follow-non-constant-source-use-a-directive-to-specify-location">Can't
follow non-constant source. Use a directive to specify location</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">.</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${util_path}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># shellcheck source=src/util.sh</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">.</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${util_path}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale</h3>
<p>ShellCheck is not able to include sourced files from paths that are
determined at runtime. The file will not be read, potentially resulting
in warnings about unassigned variables and similar.</p>
<p>Use a <a href="Directive">Directive</a> to point shellcheck to a
fixed location it can read instead.</p>
<p>ShellCheck v0.7.2+ will strip a single expansion followed by a slash,
e.g. <code>${var}/util.sh</code> or
<code>$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/util.sh</code>, and treat them as
<code>./util.sh</code>. This allows the use of <code>source-path</code>
directives or <code>-P</code> flags to specify the location.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>If you don't care that ShellCheck is unable to account for the file,
specify <code># shellcheck source=/dev/null</code>.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>
</html>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1091 – Not following: (error message here)</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1091 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1091">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="not-following-error-message-here">Not following: (error message
here)</h2>
<p>Reasons include: file not found, no permissions, not included on the
command line, not allowing <code>shellcheck</code> to follow files with
<code>-x</code>, etc.</p>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">source</span> somefile</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<p>In case you have access to the file, e.g. if it is included in your
source code repository:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># shellcheck source=somefile</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">source</span> somefile</span></code></pre></div>
<p>In case you do not have access to the file:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># shellcheck source=/dev/null</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">source</span> somefile</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck, for whichever reason, is not able to access the source
file.</p>
<p>This could be because:</p>
<ul>
<li>you did not include it on the command line,</li>
<li>did not use <code>shellcheck -x</code> (or specified
<code>external-sources=true</code> in the <a
href="Directive#external-sources">.shellcheckrc</a>) to allow following
other files</li>
<li>don't have permissions, or</li>
<li>a variety of other problems.</li>
</ul>
<p>Feel free to ignore the error with a <a
href="directive">directive</a>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck is unable to follow dynamic paths, such as
<code>source "$somedir/file"</code>. For these cases, see <a
href="SC1090">SC1090: Can't follow non-constant source. Use a directive
to specify location</a> instead. You may be seeing SC1091 because
ShellCheck tried to be helpful and strip a leading dynamic path element
as described on that page.</p>
<p>If you're fine with it, ignore the message with a <a
href="directive">directive</a>.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <h2
id="you-need-a-space-or-linefeed-between-the-function-name-and-body">You
need a space or linefeed between the function name and body.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span><span class="fu"> foo</span><span class="kw">{</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;hello world&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<p>Prefer POSIX syntax:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">foo()</span> <span class="kw">{</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;hello world&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Alternatively, add the missing space between function name and
opening <code>{</code>:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#           v-- Here</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span><span class="fu"> foo</span> <span class="kw">{</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;hello world&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>When using <code>function</code> keyword function definitions without
<code>()</code>, a space is required between the function name and the
opening <code>{</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1097 – Unexpected `==`. For assignment, use `=`. For comparison, use `[`/`[[`.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1097 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1097">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="unexpected--for-assignment-use--for-comparison-use-">Unexpected
<code>==</code>. For assignment, use <code>=</code>. For comparison, use
<code>[</code>/<code>[[</code>.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span>=value</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<p>Assignment:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span>value</span></code></pre></div>
<p>Comparison:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> value <span class="bu">]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck has noticed that you're using <code>==</code> in an
unexpected way. The two most common reasons for this is:</p>
<ul>
<li><p>You wanted to assign a value but accidentally used
<code>==</code> instead of <code>=</code>.</p></li>
<li><p>You wanted to compare two values, but neglected to use
<code>[ .. ]</code> or <code>[[ .. ]]</code>.</p></li>
</ul>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you wanted to assign a literal equals sign, use quotes to make
this clear:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;=sum(A1:A10)&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC1098 – Quote/escape special characters when using `eval`, e.g. `eval "a=(b)"`.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1098 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1098">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="quoteescape-special-characters-when-using-eval-eg-eval-ab">Quote/escape
special characters when using <code>eval</code>, e.g.
<code>eval "a=(b)"</code>.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">eval</span> <span class="va">$var</span>=<span class="er">(</span><span class="ex">a</span> b<span class="kw">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">eval</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">=(a b)&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Shells differ widely in how they handle unescaped parentheses in
<code>eval</code> expressions.</p>
<ul>
<li><code>eval foo=bar</code> is allowed by dash, bash and ksh.</li>
<li><code>eval foo=(bar)</code> is allowed by bash and ksh, but not
dash.</li>
<li><code>eval $var=(bar)</code> is allowed by ksh, but not bash or
dash.</li>
<li><code>eval foo() ( echo bar; )</code> is not allowed by any
shell.</li>
</ul>
<p>Since the expression is evaluated as shell script code anyways, it
should be passed in as a literal string without relying on special case
parsing rules in the target shell. Quote/escape the characters
accordingly.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>

    <hr />
    <h2 id="you-need-a-space-before-the-">You need a space before the
<code>#</code>.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">while</span> <span class="fu">sleep</span> 1</span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">do#</span> show time</span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">date</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">while</span> <span class="fu">sleep</span> 1</span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span> <span class="co"># show time</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">date</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck has noticed that you have a keyword immediately followed
by a <code>#</code>. In order for the <code>#</code> to start a comment,
it needs to come after a word boundary such as a space.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1100 – This is a Unicode dash. Delete and retype as ASCII minus.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1100 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1100">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="this-is-a-unicode-dash-delete-and-retype-as-ascii-minus">This is
a Unicode dash. Delete and retype as ASCII minus.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> 3 –gt 2 <span class="kw">]]</span> <span class="co"># Uses unicode en-dash character</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> 3 <span class="ot">-gt</span> 2 <span class="kw">]]</span> <span class="co"># Uses regular ASCII hyphen-minus character</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>A character that looks similar to <code>-</code> has made its way
into your code. This is usually due to copy-pasting from blogs and other
websites that formatted code as text, replacing the ASCII hyphen-minus
with a Unicode dash character.</p>
<p>To fix it, simply delete and retype it.</p>
<p>For a large script, you can use your editor's Search&amp;Replace by
copy-pasting the bad dash.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None. If you want a literal Unicode dash character, just quote
it.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC1101 – Delete trailing spaces after `\` to break line (or use quotes for literal space).</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1101 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1101">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="delete-trailing-spaces-after--to-break-line-or-use-quotes-for-literal-space">Delete
trailing spaces after <code>\</code> to break line (or use quotes for
literal space).</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># There are spaces after the backslash:</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> hello <span class="dt">\ </span> </span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>     <span class="ex">world</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># No spaces after the backslash:</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> hello <span class="dt">\</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>     world</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>To break a line you can use <code>\</code> before the line break.
However, if there are spaces after the backslash, the escape will apply
to them instead of the line break, and the command will not continue on
the next line.</p>
<p>Delete the trailing spaces to make the line break work correctly.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you do want a literal escaped space at the end of a line you can
ignore this error, but please reconsider and use quotes instead.
Trailing whitespace is invisible and frequently stripped on purpose (by
editor settings / precommits) or accident (copy-paste), and so should
not be relied upon for correctness.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1102 – Shells disambiguate `$((` differently or not at all. For `$(command substitution)`, add space after `$(` . For `$((arithmetics))`, fix parsing errors.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1102 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1102">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="shells-disambiguate--differently-or-not-at-all-for-command-substitution-add-space-after---for-arithmetics-fix-parsing-errors">Shells
disambiguate <code>$((</code> differently or not at all. For
<code>$(command substitution)</code>, add space after <code>$(</code> .
For <code>$((arithmetics))</code>, fix parsing errors.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="kw">(</span><span class="ex">cmd</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$@</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="dv">2</span><span class="op">&gt;&amp;</span><span class="dv">1</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$(</span> <span class="kw">(</span><span class="ex">cmd</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$@</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="dv">2</span><span class="op">&gt;&amp;</span><span class="dv">1</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You appear to be using <code>$((</code> with two (or more)
parentheses in a row, where the first <code>$(</code> should open a
subshell.</p>
<p>This is an ill-defined structure that is parsed differently between
different shells and shell versions. Prefer adding spaces to make it
unambiguous, both to shells and humans.</p>
<p>Consider the <code>$(((</code> in <code>$(((1)) )</code>:</p>
<p>Ash, dash and Bash 1 parses it as <code>$(( (</code> and subsequently
fail to find the matching <code>))</code>. Zsh and Bash 2+ looks ahead
and parses it as <code>$( ((</code>. Ksh parses it as
<code>$( ( (</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p><strong>Alternatively</strong>, you may indeed have correctly spaced
your parentheses, but ShellCheck failed to parse <code>$((</code> as an
arithmetic expression while accidentally succeeding in parsing it as
<code>$(</code> + <code>(</code>.</p>
<p>In these cases, double check the syntax to ensure ShellCheck can
parse the <code>$((</code>, or ignore this error and hope that it won't
affect analysis too severely.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>

    <h2 id="this-shell-type-is-unknown-use-eg-sh-or-bash">This shell type is
unknown. Use e.g. <code>sh</code> or <code>bash</code>.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># shellcheck shell=zsh</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">export</span> <span class="va">PAGER</span><span class="op">=</span>less</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<p>Any supported shell on the shebang or the <code>-s</code> option</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># shellcheck shell=sh</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">export</span> <span class="va">PAGER</span><span class="op">=</span>less</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Shellcheck only supports a specific range of shell dialects, there
are many more applications providing shell like experiences and some of
them look and feel like POSIX shell or bash but does not support the
same commands.</p>
<p>One notable unsupported shell type is zsh, see issue <a
href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/issues/809">#809</a> about
supporting zsh - some efforts have been done in the past.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>The supported shell types are listed in the help context, at the
moment these are</p>
<ul>
<li>sh</li>
<li>bash</li>
<li>dash</li>
<li>ksh</li>
</ul>

    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1104 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1104">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="use--not-just--for-the-shebang">Use <code>#!</code>, not just
<code>!</code>, for the shebang.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">!/bin/sh</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/sh</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You appear to be specifying an interpreter in a shebang, but it's
missing the hash part. The shebang must always start with
<code>#!</code>.</p>
<p>Even the name "shebang" itself comes from "hash" (<code>#</code>) +
"bang" (<code>!</code>).</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC1106 – In arithmetic contexts, use `<` instead of `-lt`</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1106 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1106">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="in-arithmetic-contexts-use--instead-of--lt">In arithmetic
contexts, use <code>&lt;</code> instead of <code>-lt</code></h2>
<p>Similarly, <code>&gt;</code> instead of <code>-gt</code>,
<code>&lt;=</code> instead of <code>-le</code>, <code>&gt;=</code>
instead of <code>-ge</code>, <code>==</code> instead of
<code>-eq</code>, <code>!=</code> instead of <code>-ne</code>.</p>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="kw">((</span> <span class="dv">2</span> <span class="op">-</span><span class="va">lt</span> <span class="dv">3</span> <span class="kw">))</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;True&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="kw">((</span> <span class="dv">2</span> <span class="op">&lt;</span> <span class="dv">3</span> <span class="kw">))</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;True&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>The comparators <code>-lt</code>, <code>-ge</code>, <code>-eq</code>
and friends are flags for the <code>test</code> command aka
<code>[</code>. You are instead using it in an arithmetic context, such
as <code>(( .. ))</code> or <code>$(( .. ))</code>, where you should be
using <code>&lt;</code>, <code>&gt;=</code>, <code>==</code> etc
instead.</p>
<p>In arithmetic contexts, <code>-lt</code> is simply interpreted as
"subtract the value of <code>$lt</code>", which is clearly not the
intention.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you do want to subtract <code>$lt</code> you can add a space to
make this clear to ShellCheck: <code>echo $((3 - lt))</code></p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1107 – This directive is unknown. It will be ignored.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1107 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1107">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="this-directive-is-unknown-it-will-be-ignored">This directive is
unknown. It will be ignored.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># shellcheck foobar=baz</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<p>Depends on your intention.</p>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck doesn't recognize the <a href="directive">directive</a>
you're trying to use in a <code># shellcheck</code> comment. See the <a
href="Directive">Directive</a>s page for supported directives.</p>
<p>It could be misspelled, or you could be using an older version of
shellcheck that doesn't support it yet.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None. If you wish to ignore this warning and continue without it, you
need version 0.4.5 (commit 88c56ec) or later and a command grouping:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Ignore an unrecognized directive in 0.4.5 or later:</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># shellcheck disable=SC1107</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">{</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="co"># shellcheck unrecognized=directive</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Before 0.4.5, unrecognized directives are considered parse
errors.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1108 – You need a space before and after the `=` .</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1108 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1108">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="you-need-a-space-before-and-after-the--">You need a space before
and after the <code>=</code> .</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span>= 2 <span class="bu">]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> 2 <span class="bu">]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You appear to be missing the space on the left side of the operator.
Shell in general, and <code>[</code> in particular, is space sensitive.
Operators and operands must be separate tokens.</p>
<p>Please ensure that the operator, like the <code>=</code> in the
example, has a space both before and after it.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None. If you're comparing values in C style reverse order like
<code>[ -eq == $1 ]</code>, use quotes: <code>[ "-eq" == "$1" ]</code>.
Also, it's pointless since <code>[ a = b ]</code> doesn't assign.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>
</html>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1109 – This is an unquoted HTML entity. Replace with corresponding character.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1109 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1109">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="this-is-an-unquoted-html-entity-replace-with-corresponding-character">This
is an unquoted HTML entity. Replace with corresponding character.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">foo</span> <span class="kw">&amp;</span><span class="ex">amp</span><span class="kw">;&amp;</span><span class="ex">amp</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="ex">bar</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">foo</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="ex">bar</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>There is an unquoted HTML entity, such as <code>&amp;amp;</code>,
<code>&amp;gt;</code> or <code>&amp;lt;</code> (instead of
<code>&amp;</code>, <code>&gt;</code> and <code>&lt;</code>) in your
code. This usually happens when copy-pasting from a web site that has
mismanaged its code formatting.</p>
<p>You should go through the entire script and replace HTML entities
with their corresponding characters.</p>
<p>Don't rely on ShellCheck to detect all of them. ShellCheck only warns
about certain cases in certain contexts, while this issue tends to
affect the entire script.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you want to run a command called <code>amp</code> after
backgrounding another command, add a space:
<code>foo &amp; amp;</code>.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>
</html>

  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1110 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1110">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="this-is-a-unicode-quote-delete-and-retype-it-or-quote-to-make-literal">This
is a Unicode quote. Delete and retype it (or quote to make
literal).</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> ‘hello world’</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&#39;hello world&#39;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Some software, like OS X, Word and WordPress, may automatically
replace your regular quotes with slanted Unicode quotes. Try deleting
and retyping them, and/or disable “smart quotes” in your editor or
OS.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>If you want to use typographic single quotes, you can put them in
double quotes (or typographic double quotes in single quotes) to make
shellcheck ignore them, e.g.,</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">printf</span> <span class="st">&quot;Warning: ‘wakeonlan’ is not installed.\n&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1111 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1111">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="this-is-a-unicode-quote-delete-and-retype-it-or-ignoresinglequote-for-literal">This
is a Unicode quote. Delete and retype it (or ignore/singlequote for
literal).</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;hello world”</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;hello world&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Some software, like OS X, Word and WordPress, may automatically
replace your regular quotes with slanted Unicode quotes. The shell does
not recognize these quotes and will not respect them.</p>
<p>In this case, you have slanted double quotes in a double quoted
string. Try deleting and retyping them, and/or disable “smart quotes” in
your editor or OS.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>If you want to use literal slanted double quotes for typographic
reasons, you can put them in single quotes to make ShellCheck ignore
them:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">printf</span> <span class="st">&#39;Warning: “wakeonlan” is not installed.\n&#39;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Alternatively, use single slanted Unicode quotes like so:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">printf</span> <span class="st">&quot;Warning: ‘wakeonlan’ is not installed.\n&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>You can also just <a href="ignore">ignore</a> this warning.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="use--not-just--for-the-shebang">Use <code>#!</code>, not just
<code>#</code>, for the shebang.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># /bin/bash</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#! /bin/bash</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You appear to be specifying a shebang, but missing the bang (i.e.
<code>!</code>). The shebang should always be on the form
<code>#!/path/shell</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>

    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="remove-leading-spaces-before-the-shebang">Remove leading spaces
before the shebang.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="co">#!/bin/sh</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello world&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/sh</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>The script has leading spaces before the shebang (<code>#!</code>).
This is not allowed.</p>
<p>The <code>#!</code> should be the first two bytes in the file, as
they're used as a file signature by the OS to determine whether a file
is a script.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <h2 id="remove-spaces-between--and--in-the-shebang">Remove spaces
between <code>#</code> and <code>!</code> in the shebang.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># !/bin/sh</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/sh</span></span>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1116 – Missing `$` on a `$((..))` expression? (or use `( (` for arrays).</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1116 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1116">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="missing--on-a--expression-or-use---for-arrays">Missing
<code>$</code> on a <code>$((..))</code> expression? (or use
<code>( (</code> for arrays).</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span><span class="er">(</span>foo+1<span class="va">)</span><span class="er">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$((foo</span><span class="op">+</span><span class="dv">1</span><span class="va">))</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You appear to be missing the <code>$</code> on an assignment from an
arithmetic expression <code>var=$((..))</code> .</p>
<p>Without the <code>$</code>, this is an array expression which is
either nested (ksh) or invalid (bash).</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you are trying to define a multidimensional Ksh array, add spaces
between the <code>( (</code> to clarify:</p>
<pre><code>var=( (1 2 3) (4 5 6) )</code></pre>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1117 – Backslash is literal in `"\n"`. Prefer explicit escaping: `"\\n"`.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1117 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1117">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="backslash-is-literal-in-n-prefer-explicit-escaping-n">Backslash
is literal in <code>"\n"</code>. Prefer explicit escaping:
<code>"\\n"</code>.</h2>
<p><em>Note: this warning has been retired due to being too pedantic.
Removed in <a
href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/commit/d8a32da07f36748986e4e34988f5cc50d7f80faa">v0.6.0
- 2018-12-03</a></em></p>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">printf</span> <span class="st">&quot;%s\n&quot;</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">printf</span> <span class="st">&quot;%s</span><span class="dt">\\</span><span class="st">n&quot;</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or alternatively, with single quotes:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">printf</span> <span class="st">&#39;%s\n&#39;</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>In a double quoted string, you have escaped a character that has no
special behavior when escaped. Instead, it's invoking the fallback
behavior of being interpreted literally.</p>
<p>Instead of relying on this implicit fallback, you should escape the
backslash explicitly. This makes it clear that it's meant to be passed
as a literal backslash in the string parameter.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None. This is a stylistic issue which can be <a
href="ignored">ignored</a>. But can you name the 5 characters that
<em>are</em> special when escaped in double quotes?</p>
<p>They are $, `, ", \, or newline. More infos are available in the <a
href="https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Double-Quotes.html">bash
manual</a>.</p>
<h3 id="retired">Retired:</h3>
<p>This warning is no longer emitted as of d8a32da07 (strictly after
v0.5).</p>
<p>The number of harmlessly affected <code>printf</code>,
<code>sed</code> and <code>grep</code> statements was significantly
higher than the number of actual unexpanded escape sequences. It may
return some day under a <code>-pedantic</code> type flag.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1118 – Delete whitespace after the here-doc end token.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1118 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1118">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="delete-whitespace-after-the-here-doc-end-token">Delete
whitespace after the here-doc end token.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<p>"▭" below indicates an otherwise invisible space:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">cat</span> <span class="op">&lt;&lt; &quot;eof&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">Hello</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">eof▭   </span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">cat</span> <span class="op">&lt;&lt; &quot;eof&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">Hello</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">eof</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>The end token of your here document has trailing whitespace. This is
invisible to the naked eye, but shells do not accept it.</p>
<p>Remove the trailing whitespace.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC1119 – Add a linefeed between end token and terminating `)`.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1119 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1119">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="add-a-linefeed-between-end-token-and-terminating-">Add a
linefeed between end token and terminating <code>)</code>.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">fmt</span> <span class="at">-s</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$COLUMNS</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="op">&lt;&lt; &quot;eof&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">This is a bunch of text</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">eof)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">fmt</span> <span class="at">-s</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$COLUMNS</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="op">&lt;&lt; &quot;eof&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">This is a bunch of text</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">eof</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>When embedding a here document in <code>$(..)</code> or
<code>(..)</code>, there needs to be a linefeed (newline) between the
here doc token and the closing <code>)</code>. Please insert one.</p>
<p>Failing to do so may cause warnings like this:</p>
<pre><code>bash: warning: here-document at line 15 delimited by end-of-file (wanted `eof&#39;)`
dash: 5: Syntax error: end of file unexpected (expecting &quot;)&quot;)</code></pre>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>This error may be incorrectly emitted for <code>ksh</code>, where
this is allowed. In this case, please either write it in a standard way
or ignore this warning.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1120 – No comments allowed after here-doc token. Comment the next line instead.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />

  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1120 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1120">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="no-comments-allowed-after-here-doc-token-comment-the-next-line-instead">No
comments allowed after here-doc token. Comment the next line
instead.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">cat</span> <span class="op">&lt;&lt; eof</span>  <span class="st"># --- Start greeting --</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">Hello</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">eof         # --- End greeting ---</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">cat</span> <span class="op">&lt;&lt; eof</span>  <span class="st"># --- Start greeting --</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">Hello</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">eof</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>            <span class="co"># --- End greeting ---</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>The terminator token for a here document must be on an entirely
separate line. No comments are allowed on this line.</p>
<p>Place the comment somewhere else, such as on the following line.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
    <hr />
