    <title>ShellCheck: SC1121 – Add `;`/`&` terminators (and other syntax) on the line with the `<<`, not here.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1121 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1121">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="add--terminators-and-other-syntax-on-the-line-with-the--not-here">Add
<code>;</code>/<code>&amp;</code> terminators (and other syntax) on the
line with the <code>&lt;&lt;</code>, not here.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">sudo</span> bash <span class="at">-s</span> <span class="op">&lt;&lt; &quot;END&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">  cmd1</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">  cmd2</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">END &amp;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">sudo</span> bash <span class="at">-s</span> <span class="op">&lt;&lt; &quot;END&quot;</span> <span class="kw">&amp;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">  cmd1</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">  cmd2</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">END</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You are using <code>&amp;</code>, <code>;</code>,
<code>&amp;&gt;</code> or similar after a here document. This is not
allowed.</p>
<p>This should instead be part of the line that initiated the here
document, i.e. the one with the <code>&lt;&lt;</code>.</p>
<p>If it helps, look at <code>&lt;&lt; "END"</code> as if it was
<code>&lt; file</code>, and make sure the resulting command is valid.
This is what the shell does. You can then append here document data
after the command.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1122 – Nothing allowed after end token. To continue a command, put it on the line with the `<<`.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1122 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1122">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="nothing-allowed-after-end-token-to-continue-a-command-put-it-on-the-line-with-the-">Nothing
allowed after end token. To continue a command, put it on the line with
the <code>&lt;&lt;</code>.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">cat</span> <span class="op">&lt;&lt; EOF</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">Hello</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">EOF | nl</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">cat</span> <span class="op">&lt;&lt; EOF</span> <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="fu">nl</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">Hello</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">EOF</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You have a here document, and appear to have added text after the
terminating token.</p>
<p>This is not allowed. If it was meant to continue the command, put it
on the line with the <code>&lt;&lt;</code>.</p>
<p>If it helps, look at &lt;&lt; "END" as if it was &lt; file, and make
sure the resulting command is valid. This is what the shell does. You
can then append here document data after the command.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1123 – ShellCheck directives are only valid in front of complete compound commands, like `if`, not e.g. individual `elif` branches.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1123 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1123">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="shellcheck-directives-are-only-valid-in-front-of-complete-compound-commands-like-if-not-eg-individual-elif-branches">ShellCheck
directives are only valid in front of complete compound commands, like
<code>if</code>, not e.g. individual <code>elif</code> branches.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$prod</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;true&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Prod mode&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># shellcheck disable=2154</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">elif</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$debug</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;true&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb1-6"><a href="#cb1-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-7"><a href="#cb1-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Debug mode&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-8"><a href="#cb1-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Applies to entire `if...fi` command</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># shellcheck disable=2154</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$prod</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;true&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Prod mode&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">elif</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$debug</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;true&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb2-7"><a href="#cb2-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-8"><a href="#cb2-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Debug mode&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-9"><a href="#cb2-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$prod</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;true&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Prod mode&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">elif</span>  <span class="co"># Applies only to this [ .. ] command</span></span>
<span id="cb3-5"><a href="#cb3-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      <span class="co"># shellcheck disable=2154</span></span>
<span id="cb3-6"><a href="#cb3-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$debug</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;true&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb3-7"><a href="#cb3-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb3-8"><a href="#cb3-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Debug mode&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-9"><a href="#cb3-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You appear to have put a directive before a non-command keyword, such
as <code>elif</code>, <code>else</code>, <code>do</code>,
<code>;;</code> or similar.</p>
<p>Unlike many other linters, ShellCheck comment directives apply to the
next shell command, rather than to the next line of text.</p>
<p>This means that you can put a directive in front of a
<code>while</code> loop, <code>if</code> statement or function
definition, and it will apply to that entire structure.</p>
<p>However, it also means that you can not apply the directive to
non-commands like an individual <code>elif</code> or <code>else</code>
block since these are not commands by themselves, and rather just parts
of an <code>if</code> compound command.</p>
<p>Please move the directive in front of the nearest applicable command
that contains the code you want to apply it to, such as before the
<code>if</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>
</html>

    <h1>SC1124 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1124">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="shellcheck-directives-are-only-valid-in-front-of-complete-commands-like-case-statements-not-individual-case-branches">ShellCheck
directives are only valid in front of complete commands like
<code>case</code> statements, not individual case branches.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">case</span> <span class="va">$?</span> <span class="kw">in</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="ss">0</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Success&quot;</span> <span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="co"># shellcheck disable=2154</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="pp">*</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$cmd</span><span class="st"> </span><span class="va">$flag</span><span class="st"> returned failure&quot;</span> <span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">esac</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Applies to everything in the `case` statement</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># shellcheck disable=2154</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">case</span> <span class="va">$?</span> <span class="kw">in</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="ss">0</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Success&quot;</span> <span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="pp">*</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$cmd</span><span class="st"> </span><span class="va">$flag</span><span class="st"> returned failure&quot;</span> <span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">esac</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">case</span> <span class="va">$?</span> <span class="kw">in</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="ss">0</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Success&quot;</span> <span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="pp">*</span><span class="kw">)</span></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>     <span class="co"># Applies to a single command within the `case`</span></span>
<span id="cb3-5"><a href="#cb3-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>     <span class="co"># shellcheck disable=2154</span></span>
<span id="cb3-6"><a href="#cb3-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>     <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$cmd</span><span class="st"> </span><span class="va">$flag</span><span class="st"> returned failure&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-7"><a href="#cb3-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>     <span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-8"><a href="#cb3-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">esac</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You appear to have put a directive before a branch in a case
statement.</p>
<p>ShellCheck directives can not be scoped to individual branches of
<code>case</code> statements, only to the entire <code>case</code>, or
to individual commands within it. Please move the directive as
appropriate.</p>
<p>(It is possible to apply directives to all commands within a
<code>{ ..: }</code> command group, if you truly wish to apply a
directive to multiple commands but not the full <code>case</code>
statement.)</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <h2 id="place-shellcheck-directives-before-commands-not-after">Place
shellcheck directives before commands, not after.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span>1 <span class="co"># shellcheck disable=SC2034</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># shellcheck disable=SC2034</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span>1 </span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck expects directives to come before the relevant command.
They are not allowed after.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If this is not a directive and just a comment mentioning ShellCheck,
please rewrite or capitalize:</p>
<pre><code>var=1 # ShellCheck encourages lowercase variable names</code></pre>

    <h2 id="was-this-intended-as-a-comment-use--in-sh">Was this intended as
a comment? Use <code>#</code> in sh.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode c"><code class="sourceCode c"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">// This is a comment.</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">/* This too. */</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># This is a comment.</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># This too.</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found what appears to be a C-style comment, a line
starting with <code>//</code> or <code>/*</code>.</p>
<p>In Bourne based shell scripts, the comment character is
<code>#</code></p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1128 – The shebang must be on the first line. Delete blanks and move comments.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1128 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1128">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="the-shebang-must-be-on-the-first-line-delete-blanks-and-move-comments">The
shebang must be on the first line. Delete blanks and move comments.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Copyright 2018 Foobar, All rights reserved</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/bash</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/bash</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Copyright 2018 Foobar, All rights reserved</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>A shebang only has an effect when it appears as the first line in a
script. Specifically, the first two bytes of the file must be
<code>#!</code>.</p>
<p>Adding comments, copyright notices or simply an accidental blank line
before it will turn a shebang into an ineffectual comment. This means
that the script is no longer in charge of its own interpreter, and may
fail to run or produce different results depending on the context it's
run (e.g. it may work from <code>bash</code> but not from
<code>zsh</code> or via <code>sudo</code>).</p>
<p>Delete any leading blank lines, and move all comments after the
shebang.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>

    <h2 id="you-need-a-space-before-the-">You need a space before the
<code>!</code>.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">while</span><span class="ot">! </span><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-f</span> file <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span> <span class="fu">sleep</span> 1<span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>

<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span> <span class="fu">sleep</span> 1<span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC1130 – You need a space before the :.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1130 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1130">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="you-need-a-space-before-the-">You need a space before the
:.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">until</span> <span class="fu">make</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">do:</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">until</span> <span class="fu">make</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span> <span class="bu">:</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a keyword immediately followed by a <code>:</code>.
<code>:</code> is a synonym for <code>true</code>, the command that
"does nothing, successfully", and as a command name it needs a
space.</p>
<p><code>do:</code> is as invalid as <code>dotrue</code>. Use
<code>do :</code>, or preferably, <code>do true</code> for
readability.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1131 – Use `elif` to start another branch.</title>

    <h1>SC1131 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>

    <hr />
    <h2 id="use-elif-to-start-another-branch">Use <code>elif</code> to start
another branch.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="fu">false</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;hi&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">elseif</span> true</span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-6"><a href="#cb1-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;ho&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-7"><a href="#cb1-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="fu">false</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;hi&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">elif</span> <span class="fu">true</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;ho&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-7"><a href="#cb2-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck noticed that you appear to be using <code>elseif</code> or
<code>elsif</code> as a keyword. This is not valid.</p>
<p><code>sh</code> instead uses <code>elif</code> as its alternative
branch keyword.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you have made your own function called <code>elseif</code> and
intend to call it, you can ignore this message.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1132 – This `&` terminates the command. Escape it or add space after `&` to silence.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1132 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1132">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="this--terminates-the-command-escape-it-or-add-space-after--to-silence">This
<code>&amp;</code> terminates the command. Escape it or add space after
<code>&amp;</code> to silence.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">curl</span> https://www.google.com/search<span class="pp">?</span>q=cats<span class="kw">&amp;</span><span class="va">tbm</span><span class="op">=</span>isch</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">curl</span> <span class="st">&quot;https://www.google.com/search?q=cats&amp;tbm=isch&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>An unescaped and unquoted <code>&amp;</code> terminates the command,
but here it's used in the middle of what would otherwise be a shell
word. This most commonly happens when copying a URL with query string
parameters without escaping the <code>&amp;</code>.</p>
<p>Either quote or escape the <code>&amp;</code> if you wanted it as a
literal ampersand, or add a space after it to make it easier to see
where the previous command stopped.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you do want to background one command and run another, e.g.
<code>sleep 10&amp;wait</code>, just add a space or linefeed after the
<code>&amp;</code> to make this more obvious:
<code>sleep 10&amp; wait</code></p>
<p>This does not change the meaning of the script, it just makes it
clear to ShellCheck (and other humans) that the <code>&amp;</code> isn't
supposed to be a part of the shell world.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1133 – Unexpected start of line. If breaking lines, `|`/`||`/`&&` should be at the end of the previous one.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1133 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1133">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="unexpected-start-of-line-if-breaking-lines--should-be-at-the-end-of-the-previous-one">Unexpected
start of line. If breaking lines,
<code>|</code>/<code>||</code>/<code>&amp;&amp;</code> should be at the
end of the previous one.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">dmesg</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="fu">grep</span> <span class="st">&quot;error&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">dmesg</span> <span class="kw">|</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">grep</span> <span class="st">&quot;error&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck has found a line that unexpectedly started with
<code>|</code>, <code>||</code> or <code>&amp;&amp;</code>. This usually
happens when a line is broken incorrectly.</p>
<p>When breaking around a <code>|</code>, <code>||</code> or
<code>&amp;&amp;</code>, there are two options:</p>
<ul>
<li>Break the line <em>after</em> this token. <code>dmesg</code> is a
complete command by itself, but <code>dmesg |</code> is not so the shell
knows to continue on the next line.</li>
<li>Use a <code>\</code> at the end of the previous line to explicitly
tell the shell to continue on the next.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>In v0.7.2 and below, this warning triggered incorrectly when starting
a line with <code>&amp;&gt;</code>. In these versions, you can either <a
href="ignore">ignore</a> the warning, or move the redirection after the
command name.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1135 – Prefer escape over ending quote to make `$` literal. Instead of `"It costs $"5`, use `"It costs \$5"`</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1135 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1135">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="prefer-escape-over-ending-quote-to-make--literal-instead-of-it-costs-5-use-it-costs-5">Prefer
escape over ending quote to make <code>$</code> literal. Instead of
<code>"It costs $"5</code>, use <code>"It costs \$5"</code></h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;The apples are $&quot;&quot;1 each&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">eval</span> <span class="st">&quot;var=$&quot;</span>name</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;The apples are </span><span class="dt">\$</span><span class="st">1 each&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">eval</span> <span class="st">&quot;var=</span><span class="dt">\$</span><span class="st">name&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># or better yet: var=&quot;${!name}&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>The script appears to be closing a double quoted string for the sole
purpose of making a dollar sign <code>$</code> literal.</p>
<p>While this happens to work, the better solution is instead to escape
it with a backslash. This allows the double quoted string to continue
uninterrupted, thereby reducing the visual noise of stopping and
starting quotes in the middle of a shell word.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1136 – Unexpected characters after terminating `]`. Missing semicolon/linefeed?</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1136 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1136">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="unexpected-characters-after-terminating--missing-semicolonlinefeed">Unexpected
characters after terminating <code>]</code>. Missing
semicolon/linefeed?</h2>
<p><em>Note: Removed in <a
href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/commit/8e332ce87978e6f6afdfabcc15b382983ea32550">V0.7.2
2021-04-20</a></em></p>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-e</span> <span class="st">&quot;foo.txt&quot;</span> <span class="er">]:</span> <span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Exists&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-e</span> <span class="st">&quot;foo.txt&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Exists&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found unexpected characters after the <code>]</code> or
<code>]]</code> in a <code>test</code> expression. In the example, a
colon was accidentally used instead of a semicolon.</p>
<p>Similarly, a missing space before a comment
(<code>[ -e foo ]#comment</code>), an additional square bracket
(<code>[[ -e foo ]]]</code>), or a missing semicolon before a
<code>then</code> on the same line (<code>if [ foo ]then</code>) can
cause this warning.</p>
<p>Make sure the <code>]</code> or <code>]]</code> is not immediately
followed by another shell word character.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1139 – Use `||` instead of `-o` between test commands.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1139 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1139">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="use--instead-of--o-between-test-commands">Use <code>||</code>
instead of <code>-o</code> between test commands.</h2>
<p>And variations, like "Use <code>&amp;&amp;</code> instead of
<code>and</code>".</p>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$1</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;-v&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="ex">-o</span> [ <span class="at">-n</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$VERBOSE</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> ]</span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Verbose log&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$1</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;-v&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="kw">||</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-n</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$VERBOSE</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Verbose log&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You have a <code>[ .. ]</code> or <code>[[ .. ]]</code> test
expression followed by <code>-o</code>/<code>-a</code> (or by
Python-style <code>or</code>/<code>and</code>).</p>
<p><code>-o</code> and <code>-a</code> work <em>inside</em>
<code>[ .. ]</code>, but they do not work <em>between</em> them. The
Python operators <code>or</code> and <code>and</code> are never
recognized in Bash.</p>
<p>To join two separate test expressions, instead use <code>||</code>
for "logical OR", or <code>&amp;&amp;</code> for "logical AND".</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1140 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1140">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="unexpected-parameters-after-condition-missing--or-bad-expression">Unexpected
parameters after condition. Missing
<code>&amp;&amp;</code>/<code>||</code>, or bad expression?</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$1</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="va">input</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$1</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$1</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="va">input</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$1</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found characters (other than redirections) after the
<code>]</code> or <code>]]</code> in a test expression. This is not
valid.</p>
<p>This sometimes happens when there was an additional expression or
command, but joining <code>||</code> or <code>&amp;&amp;</code> is
missing. Alternatively, it could happen due to typos (like
<code>[[ $1 ]]]</code> with an extra <code>]</code>), or generally from
malformed test expressions.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1141 – Unexpected tokens after compound command. Bad redirection or missing `;`/`&&`/`||`/`|`?</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1141 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1141">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="unexpected-tokens-after-compound-command-bad-redirection-or-missing-">Unexpected
tokens after compound command. Bad redirection or missing
<code>;</code>/<code>&amp;&amp;</code>/<code>||</code>/<code>|</code>?</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">while</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$2</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">do</span> <span class="fu">true</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">done</span> <span class="dt">\</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">head</span> <span class="at">-n</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$1</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">while</span> <span class="fu">sleep</span> 1<span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">do</span> <span class="fu">date</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">done</span> <span class="op">&gt;</span> my <span class="fu">file</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">while</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$2</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">do</span> <span class="fu">true</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">done</span> <span class="dt">\</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="fu">head</span> <span class="at">-n</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$1</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">while</span> <span class="fu">sleep</span> 1<span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">do</span> <span class="fu">date</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">done</span> <span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="st">&quot;my file&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found unexpected trailing characters after a compound
command.</p>
<p>The only things allowed after compound commands are redirections,
shell keywords, and the various command separators (<code>;</code>,
<code>&amp;</code>, <code>|</code>, <code>&amp;&amp;</code>,
<code>||</code>).</p>
<p>In the first example, a <code>|</code> was missing, causing
<code>head</code> to appear as an unexpected trailing word, instead of
being piped to. In the second example, a lack of quoting caused
<code>file</code> to appear as an unexpected trailing word, instead of
being part of the redirection.</p>
<p>Examine your statement and correct the problem.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1142 – Use `done < <(cmd)` to redirect from process substitution (currently missing one `<`).</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1142 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1142">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="use-done--cmd-to-redirect-from-process-substitution-currently-missing-one-">Use
<code>done &lt; &lt;(cmd)</code> to redirect from process substitution
(currently missing one <code>&lt;</code>).</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">sum</span><span class="op">=</span>0</span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">while</span> <span class="va">IFS</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;&quot;</span> <span class="bu">read</span> <span class="at">-r</span> <span class="va">n</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">((</span> <span class="va">sum</span> <span class="op">+=</span> <span class="va">n</span> <span class="kw">))</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span> <span class="op">&lt;(</span><span class="fu">file</span><span class="op">)</span> </span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">sum</span><span class="op">=</span>0</span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">while</span> <span class="va">IFS</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;&quot;</span> <span class="bu">read</span> <span class="at">-r</span> <span class="va">n</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">((</span> <span class="va">sum</span> <span class="op">+=</span> <span class="va">n</span> <span class="kw">))</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span> <span class="op">&lt;</span> <span class="op">&lt;(</span><span class="fu">file</span><span class="op">)</span> </span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a <code>done</code> keyword followed by a process
substitution, e.g. <code>done &lt;(cmd)</code>.</p>
<p>The intention was most likely to redirect from this process
substitution, in which case you will need one extra <code>&lt;</code>:
<code>done &lt; &lt;(cmd)</code>.</p>
<p>This is because <code>&lt;(cmd)</code> expands to a filename (e.g.
<code>/dev/fd/63</code>), and you need a <code>&lt;</code> to redirect
from filenames.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC1143 – This backslash is part of a comment and does not continue the line.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC1143 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1143">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="this-backslash-is-part-of-a-comment-and-does-not-continue-the-line">This
backslash is part of a comment and does not continue the line.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">sed</span> <span class="dt">\</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="at">-e</span> <span class="st">&quot;s/HOST/</span><span class="va">$HOSTNAME</span><span class="st">/g&quot;</span>   <span class="dt">\</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a># <span class="at">-e</span> <span class="st">&quot;s/USER/</span><span class="va">$USER</span><span class="st">/g&quot;</span>       <span class="dt">\</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="at">-e</span> <span class="st">&quot;s/ARCH/</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">uname</span> <span class="at">-m</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st">/g&quot;</span> <span class="dt">\</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$buildfile</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">sed</span> <span class="dt">\</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="at">-e</span> <span class="st">&quot;s/HOST/</span><span class="va">$HOSTNAME</span><span class="st">/g&quot;</span>   <span class="dt">\</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="at">-e</span> <span class="st">&quot;s/ARCH/</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">uname</span> <span class="at">-m</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st">/g&quot;</span> <span class="dt">\</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$buildfile</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># This comment is moved out:</span></span>
<span id="cb2-7"><a href="#cb2-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># -e &quot;s/USER/$USER/g&quot;       \</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or using backticked, inlined comments:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">sed</span> <span class="dt">\</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="at">-e</span> <span class="st">&quot;s/HOST/</span><span class="va">$HOSTNAME</span><span class="st">/g&quot;</span>   <span class="dt">\</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">`</span><span class="co"># -e &quot;s/USER/$USER/g&quot;</span><span class="kw">`</span>     <span class="dt">\</span></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="at">-e</span> <span class="st">&quot;s/ARCH/</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">uname</span> <span class="at">-m</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st">/g&quot;</span> <span class="dt">\</span></span>
<span id="cb3-5"><a href="#cb3-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$buildfile</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>(ShellCheck recognizes this idiom and does not suggest quotes or
<code>$()</code>, neither of which would have worked)</p>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a line continuation followed by a commented line
that appears to try to do the same.</p>
<p>Backslash line continuations are not respected in comments, and the
line instead simply terminates. This is a problem when commenting out
one line in a multi-line command like the example.</p>
<p>Instead, either move the line away from its statement, or use an
<code>`# inline comment`</code> in an unquoted backtick command
substitution.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>

<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>

    <h1>SC1144 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC1144">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="external-sources-can-only-be-enabled-in-shellcheckrc-not-in-individual-files"><code>external-sources</code>
can only be enabled in .shellcheckrc, not in individual files.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># shellcheck external-sources=true</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">source</span> /dev/zero</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<p>Add <code>external-sources=true</code> to
<code>.shellcheckrc</code></p>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Due to its origins as an online tool, ShellCheck will by default run
in a sandbox where it only reads the files explicitly named on the
command line.</p>
<p>The <code>external-sources</code> <a href="directive">directive</a>
allows disabling this, but must be specified in
<code>.shellcheckrc</code>. This is because the sandbox would be useless
if the sandboxed script can disable it for itself.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>

<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />

    <h2 id="unknown-external-sources-value-expected-truefalse">Unknown
<code>external-sources</code> value. Expected
<code>true</code>/<code>false</code>.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<p><code>.shellcheckrc</code>:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">external-sources=maybe</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">external-sources=true</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>The <code>external-sources</code> <a href="directive">directive</a>
expects a value of <code>true</code> or <code>false</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2000 – See if you can use `${#variable}` instead</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2000 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2000">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h1 id="see-if-you-can-use-variable-instead">See if you can use
<code>${#variable}</code> instead</h1>
<p><code>${#variable}</code> will be equal to the number of characters
in <code>"${variable}"</code></p>
<p>This is the same result as
<code>"$( echo "$variable" | wc -m )"</code> When "$variable" only
contains single-byte characters, it's also the same as
<code>"$( echo "$variable" | wc -c )"</code></p>
<h2 id="example-code">example code</h2>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre
class="sourceCode bash"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/usr/bin/env  bash</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>

<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;greater than 1&quot;</span></span>

<span id="cb1-6"><a href="#cb1-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb1-7"><a href="#cb1-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$(</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$1</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="fu">wc</span> <span class="at">-m</span> <span class="va">)</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">-gt</span> 1 <span class="bu">]</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-8"><a href="#cb1-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;greater than 1&quot;</span></span>

<span id="cb1-12"><a href="#cb1-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;greater than 1&quot;</span></span>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2001 – See if you can use `${variable//search/replace}` instead.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2001 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2001">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="see-if-you-can-use-variablesearchreplace-instead">See if you can
use <code>${variable//search/replace}</code> instead.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">string</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;bwol&quot;</span> <span class="kw">;</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$string</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="fu">sed</span> <span class="at">-e</span> <span class="st">&quot;s/wo/ow/&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">string</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;bwol&quot;</span> <span class="kw">;</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${string</span><span class="op">//</span><span class="ss">wo</span><span class="op">/</span>ow<span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<hr />
<p>Here is a demonstration of the different search/replace available in
Bash:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre
class="sourceCode bash"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;foo foo&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># the following two echo&#39;s should be equivalent:</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="fu">sed</span> <span class="st">&#39;s/^foo/bar/g&#39;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="va">${var</span><span class="op">/#</span><span class="ss">foo</span><span class="op">/</span>bar<span class="va">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
<table>
<thead>
<tr class="header">
<th>$var</th>
<th>sed expression</th>
<th>bash equivalent</th>
<th>result</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td>foo foo</td>
<td>s/foo/bar/</td>
<td>${var/foo/bar}</td>
<td>bar foo</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>foo foo</td>
<td>s/foo/bar/g</td>
<td>${var//foo/bar}</td>
<td>bar bar</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>foo foo</td>
<td>s/^foo/bar/</td>
<td>${var/#foo/bar}</td>
<td>bar foo</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>-foo foo</td>
<td>s/^foo/bar/</td>
<td>${var/#foo/bar}</td>
<td>-foo foo</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>-foo foo</td>
<td>s/foo$/bar/</td>
<td>${var/%foo/bar}</td>
<td>-foo bar</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>-foo foo-</td>
<td>s/foo$/bar/</td>
<td>${var/%foo/bar}</td>
<td>-foo foo-</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Let's assume somewhere earlier in your code, you have put data into a
variable (Ex: $string). Now you want to search and replace inside the
contents of $string and echo the contents out. You could pass this to
sed as done in the example above, but for simple substitutions, a
parameter expansion can do it with less overhead.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>Occasionally a more complex sed substitution is required. For
example, getting the last character of a string.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">string</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;bwol&quot;</span> <span class="kw">;</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$string</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="fu">sed</span> <span class="at">-e</span> <span class="st">&quot;s/^.*\(.\)$/\1/&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>This is a bit simple for the example, and there are alternative ways
of doing this in the shell, but this SC2001 flags on several of my crazy
complex sed commands beyond this example's scope. Utilizing some of the
more complex capabilities of sed is required occasionally, and it is
safe to ignore SC2001.</p>

<li>Wooledge BashGuide: <a

Expansion</a>.</li>

  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2002 – Useless cat. Consider `cmd < file | ..` or `cmd file | ..` instead.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2002 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2002">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h1 id="useless-cat-consider-cmd--file---or-cmd-file---instead">Useless
cat. Consider <code>cmd &lt; file | ..</code> or
<code>cmd file | ..</code> instead.</h1>
<h3 id="optional---useless-use-of-cat">Optional -
<code>useless-use-of-cat</code></h3>
<p>This is an <a href="optional">optional</a> rule, which means that it
has a special "long name" and is not enabled by default. See the <a
href="optional">optional</a> page for more details. In short, you have
to enable it with the long name instead of the "SC" code like you would
with a normal rule:</p>
<h4 id="shellcheckrc"><code>.shellcheckrc</code></h4>
<pre><code>enable=useless-use-of-cat # SC2002</code></pre>
<p>(Note that this check was not optional prior to version 0.11.0.)</p>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">cat</span> file <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="fu">tr</span> <span class="st">&#39; &#39;</span> _ <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="fu">nl</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">cat</span> file <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="cf">while</span> <span class="va">IFS</span><span class="op">=</span> <span class="bu">read</span> <span class="at">-r</span> <span class="va">i</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">do</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${i</span><span class="op">%</span><span class="pp">?</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">&lt;</span> file <span class="fu">tr</span> <span class="st">&#39; &#39;</span> _ <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="fu">nl</span>  </span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">while</span> <span class="va">IFS</span><span class="op">=</span> <span class="bu">read</span> <span class="at">-r</span> <span class="va">i</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">do</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${i</span><span class="op">%</span><span class="pp">?</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">done</span> <span class="op">&lt;</span> file</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p><code>cat</code> is a tool for con"cat"enating files. Reading a
single file as input to a program is considered a <a
href="http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cat_(Unix)#Useless_use_of_cat">Useless
Use Of Cat (UUOC)</a>.</p>
<p>It's more efficient and less roundabout to simply use redirection.
This is especially true for programs that can benefit from seekable
input, like <code>tail</code> or <code>tar</code>.</p>
<p>Many tools also accept optional filenames, e.g.
<code>grep -q foo file</code> instead of
<code>cat file | grep -q foo</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>Pointing out UUOC is a long standing shell programming tradition, and
removing them from a short-lived pipeline in a loop can speed it up by
2x. However, it's not necessarily a good use of time in practice, and
rarely affects correctness. <a href="Ignore">Ignore</a> as you see
fit.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2003 – expr is antiquated. Consider rewriting this using `$((..))`, `${}` or `[[  ]]`.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2003 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2003">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h1 id="expr-is-antiquated-consider-rewriting-this-using---or---">expr
is antiquated. Consider rewriting this using <code>$((..))</code>,
<code>${}</code> or <code>[[  ]]</code>.</h1>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">i</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">expr</span> 1 + 2<span class="va">)</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">l</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">expr</span> length <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">i</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$((</span><span class="dv">1</span><span class="op">+</span><span class="dv">2</span><span class="va">))</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">l</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">${</span><span class="op">#</span><span class="va">var}</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>WARNING:</strong> constants with a leading 0 are interpreted
as octal numbers by bash, but not by expr. Then you should specify the
base when a leading zero may occur:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> x=08</span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> echo <span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">expr</span> 1 + <span class="va">$x)</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">9</span></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> echo <span class="va">$((</span><span class="dv">1</span> <span class="op">+</span> <span class="va">$x))</span></span>
<span id="cb3-5"><a href="#cb3-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">-bash:</span> 1 + 08: value too great for base <span class="er">(</span><span class="ex">error</span> token is <span class="st">&quot;08&quot;</span><span class="kw">)</span></span>
<span id="cb3-6"><a href="#cb3-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> echo <span class="va">$((</span><span class="dv">1</span> <span class="op">+</span> <span class="dt">10#</span><span class="va">$x))</span></span>
<span id="cb3-7"><a href="#cb3-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">9</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>See <a
href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/issues/1910#issuecomment-610439789">issue
#1910</a></p>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p><a
href="https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/009695399/utilities/expr.html#tag_04_50_17">To
quote POSIX:</a></p>
<blockquote>
<p>The expr utility has a rather difficult syntax [...] In many cases,
the arithmetic and string features provided as part of the shell command
language are easier to use than their equivalents in expr. Newly written
scripts should avoid expr in favor of the new features within the
shell.</p>
</blockquote>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p><code>sh</code> doesn't have a great replacement for the
<code>:</code> operator (regex match). ShellCheck tries not to warn when
using <code>expr</code> with <code>:</code>, but e.g.
<code>op=:; expr string "$op" regex</code> will still trigger it.</p>
<p>Bash has <code>[[ string =~ regex ]]</code>, so not even
<code>expr .. : ..</code> is necessary.</p>
<p>Bash doesn't check for integer overflow. When dealing with extremely
large numbers, it may be necessary to use an external tool like
<code>expr</code>.</p>
<p>Other than that, all uses of <code>expr</code> can be rewritten to
use modern shell features instead.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
