    <title>ShellCheck: SC2066 – Since you double-quoted this, it will not word split, and the loop will only run once.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2066 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2066">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="since-you-double-quoted-this-it-will-not-word-split-and-the-loop-will-only-run-once">Since
you double-quoted this, it will not word split, and the loop will only
run once.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> s <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="ex">mycommand</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">do</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$s</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<p>The correct code depends on your intention. Let's say you're in a
directory with the files <code>file.png</code> and
<code>My cat.png</code>, and you want to loop over a command that
outputs (or variable that contains):</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">hello</span> world</span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">My</span> <span class="pp">*</span>.png</span></code></pre></div>
<h4 id="loop-over-each-line-without-globbing-hello-world-my-png">Loop
over each line without globbing (<code>hello world</code>,
<code>My *.png</code>)</h4>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">mycommand</span> <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="cf">while</span> <span class="va">IFS</span><span class="op">=</span> <span class="bu">read</span> <span class="at">-r</span> <span class="va">s</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">do</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$s</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h4
id="loop-over-each-word-with-globbing-hello-world-my-filepng-my-catpng">Loop
over each word with globbing (<code>hello</code>, <code>world</code>,
<code>My</code>, <code>file.png</code>, <code>My cat.png</code>):</h4>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># relies on the fact that IFS by default contains space-tab-linefeed</span></span>
<span id="cb4-2"><a href="#cb4-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> s <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="va">$(</span><span class="ex">mycommand</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">do</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$s</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h4 id="loop-over-each-line-with-globbing-hello-world-my-catpng">Loop
over each line with globbing (<code>hello world</code>,
<code>My cat.png</code>)</h4>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb5"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb5-1"><a href="#cb5-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># explicitly set IFS to contain only a line feed</span></span>
<span id="cb5-2"><a href="#cb5-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">IFS</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&#39;</span></span>
<span id="cb5-3"><a href="#cb5-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">&#39;</span></span>
<span id="cb5-4"><a href="#cb5-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> s <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="va">$(</span><span class="ex">mycommand</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">do</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$s</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You get this warning because you have a loop that will only ever run
exactly one iteration. Since you have a loop, you clearly expect it to
run more than once. You just have to decide how it should be split
up.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>None.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2067 – Missing `;` or `+` terminating `-exec`. You can't use `|`/`||`/`&&`, and `;` has to be a separate, quoted argument.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2067 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2067">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="missing--or--terminating--exec-you-cant-use--and--has-to-be-a-separate-quoted-argument">Missing
<code>;</code> or <code>+</code> terminating <code>-exec</code>. You
can't use <code>|</code>/<code>||</code>/<code>&amp;&amp;</code>, and
<code>;</code> has to be a separate, quoted argument.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">find</span> . <span class="at">-type</span> f <span class="at">-exec</span> shellcheck {} <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="fu">wc</span> <span class="at">-l</span> <span class="dt">\;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">find</span> . <span class="at">-exec</span> echo {} <span class="kw">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">find</span> . <span class="at">-type</span> f <span class="at">-exec</span> sh <span class="at">-c</span> <span class="st">&#39;shellcheck &quot;$1&quot; | wc -l&#39;</span> <span class="at">--</span> {} <span class="dt">\;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">find</span> . <span class="at">-exec</span> echo {} <span class="dt">\;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p><code>find -exec</code> is still subject to all normal shell rules,
so all shell features like <code>|</code>, <code>||</code>,
<code>&amp;</code> and <code>&amp;&amp;</code> will apply to the
<code>find</code> command itself, and not to the command you are trying
to construct with <code>-exec</code>.</p>
<p><code>find . -exec foo {} &amp;&amp; bar {} \;</code> means run the
command <code>find . -exec foo {}</code>, and if find is successful, run
the command <code>bar "{}" ";"</code>.</p>
<p>To instead go through each file and run
<code>foo file &amp;&amp; bar file</code> on it, invoke a shell that can
interpret <code>&amp;&amp;</code>:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">find</span> . <span class="at">-exec</span> sh <span class="st">&#39;foo &quot;$1&quot; &amp;&amp; bar &quot;$1&quot;&#39;</span> <span class="at">--</span> {} <span class="dt">\;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>You can also use find <code>-a</code> instead of shell
<code>&amp;&amp;</code>:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">find</span> . <span class="at">-exec</span> foo {} <span class="dt">\;</span> <span class="at">-a</span> <span class="at">-exec</span> bar {} <span class="dt">\;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>This will have the same effect (<code>-a</code> is also the default
when two commands are specified, and can therefore be omitted).</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>None</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2068 – Double quote array expansions to avoid re-splitting elements.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2068 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2068">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="double-quote-array-expansions-to-avoid-re-splitting-elements">Double
quote array expansions to avoid re-splitting elements.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">cp</span> <span class="va">$@</span> ~/dir</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">cp</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$@</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> ~/dir</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Double quotes around <code>$@</code> (and similarly,
<code>${array[@]}</code>) prevents globbing and word splitting of
individual elements, while still expanding to multiple separate
arguments.</p>
<p>Let's say you have four arguments: <code>baz</code>,
<code>foo bar</code>, <code>*</code> and <code>/*/*/*/*</code></p>
<p><code>"$@"</code> will expand into exactly that: <code>baz</code>,
<code>foo bar</code>, <code>*</code> and <code>/*/*/*/*</code></p>
<p><code>$@</code> will expand into multiple other arguments:
<code>baz</code>, <code>foo</code>, <code>bar</code>,
<code>file.txt</code>, <code>otherfile.jpg</code>, and (eventually) a
list of most files on the system</p>
<p>Since the latter is rarely expected or desired, ShellCheck warns
about it.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>When you want globbing of individual elements.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2069 – To redirect stdout+stderr, `2>&1` must be last (or use `{ cmd > file; } 2>&1` to clarify).</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2069 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2069">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="to-redirect-stdoutstderr-21-must-be-last-or-use--cmd--file--21-to-clarify">To
redirect stdout+stderr, <code>2&gt;&amp;1</code> must be last (or use
<code>{ cmd &gt; file; } 2&gt;&amp;1</code> to clarify).</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">firefox</span> <span class="dv">2</span><span class="op">&gt;&amp;</span><span class="dv">1</span> <span class="op">&gt;</span> /dev/null</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">firefox</span> <span class="op">&gt;</span> /dev/null <span class="dv">2</span><span class="op">&gt;&amp;</span><span class="dv">1</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>When it comes to redirection, order matters.</p>
<p>The problematic code means "Point stderr to where stdout is currently
pointing (the terminal). Then point stdout to /dev/null".</p>
<p>The correct code means "Point stdout to /dev/null. Then point stderr
to where stdout is currently pointing (/dev/null)".</p>
<p>In other words, the problematic code hides stdout and shows stderr.
The correct code hides both stderr and stdout, which is usually the
intention.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>If you actually do want to redirect stdout to a file, and then turn
stderr into the new stdout, you can make this more explicit with
braces:</p>
<pre><code>{ firefox &gt; /dev/null; } 2&gt;&amp;1</code></pre>
<p>Also note that this warning does not trigger when output is piped or
captured.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://mywiki.wooledge.org/BashPitfalls#pf43">Bash
Pitfalls: somecmd 2&gt;&amp;1 &gt;&gt;logfile</a></li>
<li><a href="https://mywiki.wooledge.org/BashFAQ/055">BashFaq: Tell me
all about 2&gt;&amp;1 -- what's the difference between 2&gt;&amp;1
&gt;foo and &gt;foo 2&gt;&amp;1, and when do I use which?</a></li>
</ul>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2070 – `-n` doesn't work with unquoted arguments. Quote or use `[[ ]]`.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2070 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2070">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="-n-doesnt-work-with-unquoted-arguments-quote-or-use--"><code>-n</code>
doesn't work with unquoted arguments. Quote or use
<code>[[ ]]</code>.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-n</span> <span class="va">$var</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;var has a value&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">else</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;var is empty&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-6"><a href="#cb1-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<p>In POSIX:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-n</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;var has a value&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">else</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;var is empty&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>In bash/ksh:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="ot">-n</span> <span class="va">$var</span> <span class="kw">]]</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;var has a value&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">else</span></span>
<span id="cb3-5"><a href="#cb3-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;var is empty&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-6"><a href="#cb3-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>When <code>$var</code> is unquoted, a blank value will cause it to
wordsplit and disappear. If <code>$var</code> is empty, these two
statements are identical:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-n</span> <span class="va">$var</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb4-2"><a href="#cb4-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-n</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p><code>[ string ]</code> is shorthand for testing if a string is
empty. This is still true if <code>string</code> happens to be
<code>-n</code>. <code>[ -n ]</code> is therefore true, and by extension
so is <code>[ -n $var ]</code>.</p>
<p>To fix this, either quote the variable, or (if your shell supports
it) use <code>[[ -n $var ]]</code> which generally has fewer caveats
than <code>[</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
    <hr />

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2071 – `>` is for string comparisons. Use `-gt` instead.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2071 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2071">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="-is-for-string-comparisons-use--gt-instead"><code>&gt;</code> is
for string comparisons. Use <code>-gt</code> instead.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="va">$var</span> <span class="ot">&gt;</span> 10 <span class="kw">]]</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Incorrectly triggers when var=5&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="va">$var</span> <span class="ot">-gt</span> 10 <span class="kw">]]</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Correct numerical comparison&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p><code>&lt;</code> and <code>&gt;</code>, in both <code>[[</code> and
<code>[</code> (when escaped) will do a lexicographical comparison, not
a numerical comparison.</p>
<p>This means that <code>[[ 5 &gt; 10 ]]</code> is true because 5 comes
after 10 alphabetically. Meanwhile <code>[[ 5 -gt 10 ]]</code> is false
because 5 does not come after 10 numerically.</p>
<p>If you want to compare numbers by value, use the numerical comparison
operators <code>-gt</code>, <code>-ge</code>, <code>-lt</code> and
<code>-le</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If the strings happen to be version numbers and you're using &lt;, or
&gt; to compare them as strings, and you consider this an acceptable
thing to do, then you can ignore this warning.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://mywiki.wooledge.org/BashPitfalls#pf7">Bash
Pitfalls: <code>[[ $foo &gt; 7 ]]</code></a></li>
<li><a
href="https://stackoverflow.com/questions/18668556/comparing-numbers-in-bash">StackOverflow:
Comparing numbers in Bash</a></li>
</ul>

    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2072 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2072">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="decimals-are-not-supported-either-use-integers-only-or-use-bc-or-awk-to-compare">Decimals
are not supported. Either use integers only, or use <code>bc</code> or
<code>awk</code> to compare.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> 2 <span class="ot">-lt</span> 3.14 <span class="kw">]]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> 200 <span class="ot">-lt</span> 314 <span class="kw">]]</span>                   <span class="co"># Use fixed point math</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="va">$(</span><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;2 &lt; 3.14&quot;</span> <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="fu">bc</span><span class="va">)</span> <span class="ot">==</span> 1 <span class="kw">]]</span>  <span class="co"># Use bc</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Bash and Posix sh does not support decimals in numbers. Decimals
should either be avoided, or compared using a tool that does support
them.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>If the strings happen to be version numbers and you're using
<code>&lt;</code>, or <code>&gt;</code> to compare them as strings, and
you consider this an acceptable thing to do, then you can ignore this
warning.</p>

    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2073 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2073">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="escape--to-prevent-it-redirecting-or-switch-to---">Escape
<code>\&lt;</code> to prevent it redirecting (or switch to
<code>[[ .. ]]</code>).</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;aardvark&quot;</span> <span class="er">&lt;</span> <span class="st">&quot;zebra&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Alphabetical!&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;aardvark&quot;</span> <span class="dt">\&lt;</span> <span class="st">&quot;zebra&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Alphabetical!&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or optionally in Bash/Ksh:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="st">&quot;aardvark&quot;</span> <span class="ot">&lt;</span> <span class="st">&quot;zebra&quot;</span> <span class="kw">]]</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Alphabetical!&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You are using the operator <code>&lt;</code> or <code>&gt;</code> in
a <code>[</code> test expression.</p>
<p>In this context, it will be considered a file redirection operator
instead, so <code>[ "aardvark" &lt; "zebra" ]</code> is equivalent to
<code>[ "aardvark" ] &lt; ./zebra</code>, which is true if there exists
a readable file <code>zebra</code> in the current directory.</p>
<p>If you wanted to compare two strings lexicographically
(alphabetically), escape the <code>&lt;</code> or <code>&gt;</code> with
a backslash as in the correct example.</p>
<p>If you want to compare two numbers numerically, use <code>-lt</code>
or <code>-ge</code> instead.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>

<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2074 – Can't use `=~` in `[ ]`. Use `[[..]]` instead.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2074 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2074">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="cant-use--in---use--instead">Can't use <code>=~</code> in
<code>[ ]</code>. Use <code>[..](..)</code> instead.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$input</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> =~ DOC<span class="pp">[</span><span class="ss">0</span><span class="pp">-</span><span class="ss">9</span><span class="pp">]*</span><span class="dt">\.</span>txt <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;match&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$input</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=~</span> <span class="ss">DOC</span><span class="op">[</span><span class="ss">0</span><span class="op">-</span><span class="ss">9</span><span class="op">]</span><span class="pp">*</span><span class="dt">\.</span><span class="ss">txt</span> <span class="kw">]]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;match&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p><code>=~</code> only works in <code>[[ .. ]]</code> tests. It does
not work with <code>test</code> or <code>[</code> in any shell.</p>
<p>If you're targeting POSIX <code>sh</code>, rewrite in terms of
<code>case</code> or <code>grep</code> instead.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2075 – Escaping `\<` is required in `[..]`, but invalid in `[[..]]`</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2075 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2075">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="escaping--is-required-in--but-invalid-in-">Escaping
<code>\&lt;</code> is required in <code>[..]</code>, but invalid in
<code>[..](..)</code></h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> aardvark <span class="dt">\&lt;</span> zebra <span class="kw">]]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> aardvark <span class="ot">&lt;</span> zebra <span class="kw">]]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Grammatically speaking, <code>[</code> is considered a normal command
name, so <code>&lt;</code> and <code>&gt;</code> are interpreted as
redirections. When using the lexicographical string operators
<code>&lt;</code> and <code>&gt;</code> in <code>[ .. ]</code>, they
must be escaped (e.g. <code>\&lt;</code> or <code>"&lt;"</code>).</p>
<p><code>[[</code> is considered its own grammatical construct, and
therefore it does not require (nor does it allow) escaping
<code>&lt;</code> or <code>&gt;</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2076 – Don't quote rhs of `=~`, it'll match literally rather than as a regex.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2076 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2076">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="dont-quote-rhs-of--itll-match-literally-rather-than-as-a-regex">Don't
quote rhs of <code>=~</code>, it'll match literally rather than as a
regex.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="va">$foo</span> <span class="ot">=~</span> <span class="st">&quot;^fo+ bar$&quot;</span> <span class="kw">]]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="va">$foo</span> <span class="ot">=~</span> <span class="pp">^</span><span class="ss">fo</span><span class="pp">+</span><span class="dt">\ </span><span class="ss">bar</span><span class="op">$</span> <span class="kw">]]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Quotes on the right hand side of <code>=~</code> can be used to match
literally, so that <code>[[ $1 =~ ^"$2".* ]]</code> works even if
<code>$2</code> contains regex metacharacters. This mirrors the behavior
of globs, <code>[[ $1 = "$2"* ]]</code>.</p>
<p>This also means that the problematic code tries to match literal
carets and plus signs instead of interpreting them as regular expression
matchers. To match as a regex, the regex metacharacters it must be
unquoted. Literal parts of the expression can be quoted with double or
single quotes, or escaped.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you do want to match literally just to do a plain substring
search, e.g. <code>[[ $foo =~ "bar" ]]</code>, you could ignore this
message, but consider using a more canonical glob match instead:
<code>[[ $foo == *"bar"* ]]</code>.</p>
<h3 id="compatibility">Compatibility:</h3>
<ul>
<li>In Bash 3.2 and newer with shopt <code>compat31</code> <em>disabled
(the default)</em>, quoted patterns are literal whereas unquoted
patterns are parsed for regex metacharacters.</li>
<li>In Bash 3.2 and newer with shopt <code>compat31</code>
<em>enabled</em>, quoted and unquoted patterns match identically.</li>
<li>In Bash 3.1 quoted and unquoted patterns match identically.</li>
</ul>
<p>See <a
href="http://stackoverflow.com/questions/218156/bash-regex-with-quotes"
class="uri">http://stackoverflow.com/questions/218156/bash-regex-with-quotes</a></p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2077 – You need spaces around the comparison operator.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2077 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2077">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="you-need-spaces-around-the-comparison-operator">You need spaces
around the comparison operator.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> 0=1 <span class="kw">]]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> 0 <span class="ot">=</span> 1 <span class="kw">]]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p><code>[[ 0 = 1 ]]</code> means "check if 0 and 1 are equal".</p>
<p><code>[[ str ]]</code> is short form for <code>[[ -n str ]]</code>,
and means "check if <code>str</code> is non-empty". It doesn't matter if
<code>str</code> happens to contain <code>0=1</code>.</p>
<p>Always use spaces around the comparison operator in <code>[..]</code>
and <code>[..](..)</code>, otherwise it won't be recognized as an
operator.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>None.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2078 – This expression is constant. Did you forget a `$` somewhere?</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2078 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2078">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="this-expression-is-constant-did-you-forget-a--somewhere">This
expression is constant. Did you forget a <code>$</code> somewhere?</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;myvar&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;myvar is set&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$myvar</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;myvar is set&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck has found a <code>[ .. ]</code> or <code>[[ .. ]]</code>
statement that just contains a literal string. Such a check does not do
anything useful, and will always be true (or always false, for empty
strings).</p>
<p>This is usually due to missing <code>$</code> or bad quoting:</p>
<pre><code>if [[ STY ]             # always true
if [[ $STY ]]           # checks variable $STY

if [[ &#39;grep foo bar&#39; ]] # always true
if [[ `grep foo bar` ]] # checks grep output (poorly)
if grep -q foo bar      # checks for grep match (preferred)</code></pre>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2079 – `(( ))` doesn't support decimals. Use `bc` or `awk`.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2079 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2079">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="--doesnt-support-decimals-use-bc-or-awk"><code>(( ))</code>
doesn't support decimals. Use <code>bc</code> or <code>awk</code>.</h2>
<p>Bash <a
href="https://www.tldp.org/LDP/abs/html/comparison-ops.html">arithmetic
conditional evaluation can only be performed on integers</a>. More
detail: Bash has limited data types which <a
href="http://www.tldp.org/LDP/abs/html/declareref.html">include
integer</a>, but everything is effectively <a
href="http://www.tldp.org/LDP/abs/html/untyped.html">untyped</a>.</p>
<p>Suggested workarounds to this constraint use bc or awk, here are <a
href="https://stackoverflow.com/questions/11237794/how-to-compare-two-decimal-numbers-in-bash-awk">some
examples</a>.</p>

    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2080 – Numbers with leading 0 are considered octal.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2080 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2080">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="numbers-with-leading-0-are-considered-octal">Numbers with
leading 0 are considered octal.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="va">$((</span> <span class="dv">16</span> <span class="op">-</span> <span class="dv">08 ))</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="va">$((</span> <span class="dv">16</span> <span class="op">-</span> <span class="dv">8</span> <span class="va">))</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found an integer literal with a leading zero, but
containing the digits 8 or 9.</p>
<p>This is invalid, as the integer will be interpreted as an octal value
(e.g. 0777 == 0x1FF == 511).</p>
<p>To have the value parsed in base 10, either remove the leading zeros
as in the example, or specify the radix explicitly:</p>
<pre><code>echo $((10#08)) </code></pre>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>

etc!</li>

href="https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Shell-Arithmetic.html">The
BASH manual "Shell Arithmetic" chapter</a></p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2081 – `[ .. ]` can't match globs. Use `[[ .. ]]` or grep.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2081 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2081">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="---cant-match-globs-use----or-grep"><code>[ .. ]</code> can't
match globs. Use <code>[[ .. ]]</code> or grep.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="va">$var</span> <span class="ot">==</span> <span class="pp">*[^</span><span class="ss">0</span><span class="pp">-</span><span class="ss">9</span><span class="pp">]*</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st"> is not numeric&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span> </span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="va">$var</span> <span class="ot">==</span> <span class="pp">*[^</span><span class="ss">0</span><span class="pp">-</span><span class="ss">9</span><span class="pp">]*</span> <span class="kw">]]</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st"> is not numeric&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span> </span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p><code>[ .. ]</code> aka <code>test</code> can not match against
globs.</p>
<p>In bash/ksh, you can instead use <code>[[ .. ]]</code> which supports
this behavior.</p>
<p>In sh, you can rewrite to use <code>grep</code>.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="va">$var</span> <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="fu">grep</span> <span class="at">-q</span> <span class="st">&#39;^[0-9]*$&#39;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st"> is numeric&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None. If you are not trying to match a glob, quote the argument (e.g.
<code>[ $var == '*' ]</code> to match literal asterisk.</p>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2082 – To expand via indirection, use `name="foo$n"; echo "${!name}"`.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2082 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2082">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="to-expand-via-indirection-use-namefoon-echo-name">To expand via
indirection, use <code>name="foo$n"; echo "${!name}"</code>.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var_1</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;hello world&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">n</span><span class="op">=</span>1</span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${var_</span><span class="er">$n</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<p>Bash/ksh:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Use arrays instead of dynamic names</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">declare</span> <span class="at">-a</span> <span class="va">var</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">[</span><span class="dv">1</span><span class="op">]=</span><span class="st">&quot;hello world&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">n</span><span class="op">=</span>1</span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${var</span><span class="op">[</span>n<span class="op">]</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Expand variable names dynamically</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var_1</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;hello world&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">n</span><span class="op">=</span>1</span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">name</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;var_</span><span class="va">$n</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-5"><a href="#cb3-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${</span><span class="op">!</span><span class="va">name}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>POSIX sh:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Expand dynamically with eval</span></span>
<span id="cb4-2"><a href="#cb4-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var_1</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;hello world&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-3"><a href="#cb4-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">n</span><span class="op">=</span>1</span>
<span id="cb4-4"><a href="#cb4-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">eval</span> <span class="st">&quot;tmp=</span><span class="dt">\$</span><span class="st">var_</span><span class="va">$n</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-5"><a href="#cb4-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${tmp}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You can expand a variable <code>var_1</code> with
<code>${var_1}</code>, but you can not generate the string
<code>var_1</code> with an embedded expansion, like
<code>${var_$n}</code>.</p>
<p>Instead, if at all possible, you should use an array. Bash and ksh
support both numerical and associative arrays, and an example is shown
above.</p>
<p>If you can't use arrays, you can indirectly reference variables by
creating a temporary variable with its name, e.g.
<code>myvar="var_$n"</code> and then expanding it indirectly with
<code>${!myvar}</code>. This will give the contents of the variable
<code>var_1</code>.</p>
<p>If using POSIX sh, where neither arrays nor <code>${!var}</code> is
available, <code>eval</code> can be used. You must be careful in
sanitizing the data used to construct the variable name to avoid
arbitrary code execution.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://mywiki.wooledge.org/BashFAQ/006">BashFaq: How can I
use variable variables (indirect variables, pointers, references) or
associative arrays?</a></li>
<li><a
href="https://stackoverflow.com/questions/16553089/dynamic-variable-names-in-bash">StackOverflow:
Dynamic variable names in Bash</a></li>
</ul>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2083 – Don't add spaces after the slash in `./file`.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2083 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2083">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="dont-add-spaces-after-the-slash-in-file">Don't add spaces after
the slash in <code>./file</code>.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">gcc</span> <span class="at">-o</span> myfile file.c</span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">./</span> myfile</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">gcc</span> <span class="at">-o</span> myfile file.c</span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">./myfile</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Contrary to popular belief, there is no command or syntax
<code>./</code> that runs a file.</p>
<p><code>./myfile</code> is simply the shortest path equivalent to
<code>myfile</code> that specifies a directory and therefore causes a
shell to run it as-is, instead of trying to find its directory using
$PATH.</p>
<p>Therefore, to run a file in the current directory, use
<code>./myfile</code> and not <code>./ myfile</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

<!DOCTYPE html>

  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2084 – Remove `$` or use `_=$((expr))` to avoid executing output.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2084 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2084">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="remove--or-use-_expr-to-avoid-executing-output">Remove
<code>$</code> or use <code>_=$((expr))</code> to avoid executing
output.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">i</span><span class="op">=</span>4</span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">$((</span> <span class="va">i</span><span class="op">++</span> <span class="va">))</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<p>Bash, Ksh:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">i</span><span class="op">=</span>4</span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">((</span> <span class="va">i</span><span class="op">++</span> <span class="kw">))</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>POSIX (assuming <code>++</code> is supported):</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">i</span><span class="op">=</span>4</span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">_</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$((</span> <span class="va">i</span><span class="op">++</span> <span class="va">))</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Alternative POSIX version that does not preserve the exit code:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">:</span> <span class="va">$((</span> <span class="va">i</span><span class="op">++</span> <span class="va">))</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p><code>$((..))</code> expands to a number. If it's the only word on
the line, the shell will try to execute this number as a command
name:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb5"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb5-1"><a href="#cb5-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> i=4</span>
<span id="cb5-2"><a href="#cb5-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> <span class="va">$((</span> <span class="va">i</span><span class="op">++</span> <span class="va">))</span></span>
<span id="cb5-3"><a href="#cb5-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">4:</span> command not found</span>
<span id="cb5-4"><a href="#cb5-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> echo <span class="va">$i</span></span>
<span id="cb5-5"><a href="#cb5-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">5</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>To avoid trying to execute the number as a command name, use one of
the methods mentioned:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb6"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb6-1"><a href="#cb6-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> i=4</span>
<span id="cb6-2"><a href="#cb6-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> _=<span class="va">$((</span> <span class="va">i</span><span class="op">++</span> <span class="va">))</span></span>
<span id="cb6-3"><a href="#cb6-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">$</span> echo <span class="va">$i</span></span>
<span id="cb6-4"><a href="#cb6-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">5</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2086 – Double quote to prevent globbing and word splitting.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2086 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2086">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="double-quote-to-prevent-globbing-and-word-splitting">Double
quote to prevent globbing and word splitting.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="va">$1</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> i <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="va">$*</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">do</span> <span class="bu">:</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">done</span> <span class="co"># this one and the next one also apply to expanding arrays.</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> i <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="va">$@</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">do</span> <span class="bu">:</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$1</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> i <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$@</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">do</span> <span class="bu">:</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">done</span> <span class="co"># or, &#39;for i; do&#39;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale</h3>
<p>The first code looks like "print the first argument". It's actually
"Split the first argument by IFS (spaces, tabs and line feeds). Expand
each of them as if it was a glob. Join all the resulting strings and
filenames with spaces. Print the result."</p>
<p>The second one looks like "iterate through all arguments". It's
actually "join all the arguments by the first character of IFS (space),
split them by IFS and expand each of them as globs, and iterate on the
resulting list". The third one skips the joining part.</p>
<p>Quoting variables prevents word splitting and glob expansion, and
prevents the script from breaking when input contains spaces, line
feeds, glob characters and such.</p>
<p>Strictly speaking, only expansions themselves need to be quoted, but
for stylistic reasons, entire arguments with multiple variable and
literal parts are often quoted as one:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">$HOME</span><span class="ex">/</span><span class="va">$dir</span><span class="ex">/dist/bin/</span><span class="va">$file</span>        <span class="co"># Unquoted (bad)</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$HOME</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="ex">/</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$dir</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="ex">/dist/bin/</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$file</span><span class="st">&quot;</span>  <span class="co"># Minimal quoting (good)</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$HOME</span><span class="st">/</span><span class="va">$dir</span><span class="st">/dist/bin/</span><span class="va">$file</span><span class="st">&quot;</span>      <span class="co"># Canonical quoting (good)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>When quoting composite arguments, make sure to exclude globs and
brace expansions, which lose their special meaning in double quotes:
<code>"$HOME/$dir/src/*.c"</code> will not expand, but
<code>"$HOME/$dir/src"/*.c</code> will.</p>
<p>Note that <code>$( )</code> starts a new context, and variables in it
have to be quoted independently:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;This </span><span class="va">$variable</span><span class="st"> is quoted </span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="ex">but</span> this <span class="va">$variable</span> is not<span class="va">)</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-2"><a href="#cb4-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;This </span><span class="va">$variable</span><span class="st"> is quoted </span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="ex">and</span> now this <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$variable</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> is too<span class="va">)</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h2 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h2>
<p>Sometimes you want to split on spaces, like when building a command
line:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb5"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb5-1"><a href="#cb5-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">options</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;-j 5 -B&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb5-2"><a href="#cb5-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="va">$debug</span> <span class="ot">==</span> <span class="st">&quot;yes&quot;</span> <span class="kw">]]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="va">options</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$options</span><span class="st"> -d&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb5-3"><a href="#cb5-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">make</span> <span class="va">$options</span> file</span></code></pre></div>
<p>Just quoting this doesn't work. Instead, you should have used an
array (bash, ksh, zsh):</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb6"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb6-1"><a href="#cb6-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">options</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span>-j 5 -B<span class="va">)</span> <span class="co"># ksh88: set -A options -- -j 5 -B</span></span>
<span id="cb6-2"><a href="#cb6-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="va">$debug</span> <span class="ot">==</span> <span class="st">&quot;yes&quot;</span> <span class="kw">]]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="va">options</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${options</span><span class="op">[@]</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> -d<span class="va">)</span></span>
<span id="cb6-3"><a href="#cb6-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">make</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${options</span><span class="op">[@]</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> file</span></code></pre></div>
<p>or a function (POSIX):</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb7"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb7-1"><a href="#cb7-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">make_with_flags()</span> <span class="kw">{</span></span>
<span id="cb7-2"><a href="#cb7-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$debug</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;yes&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="bu">set</span> <span class="at">--</span> <span class="at">-d</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$@</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb7-3"><a href="#cb7-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">make</span> <span class="at">-j</span> 5 <span class="at">-B</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$@</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb7-4"><a href="#cb7-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span></span>
<span id="cb7-5"><a href="#cb7-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">make_with_flags</span> file</span></code></pre></div>
<p>To split on spaces but not perform glob expansion, POSIX has a
<code>set -f</code> to disable globbing. You can disable word splitting
by setting <code>IFS=''</code>.</p>
<p>Similarly, you might want an optional argument:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb8"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb8-1"><a href="#cb8-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">debug</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb8-2"><a href="#cb8-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="va">$1</span> <span class="ot">==</span> <span class="st">&quot;--trace-commands&quot;</span> <span class="kw">]]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="va">debug</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;-x&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb8-3"><a href="#cb8-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">bash</span> <span class="va">$debug</span> script</span></code></pre></div>
<p>Quoting this doesn't work, since in the default case,
<code>"$debug"</code> would expand to one empty argument while
<code>$debug</code> would expand into zero arguments. In this case, you
can use an array with zero or one elements as outlined above, or you can
use an unquoted expansion with an alternate value:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb9"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb9-1"><a href="#cb9-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">debug</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb9-2"><a href="#cb9-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="va">$1</span> <span class="ot">==</span> <span class="st">&quot;--trace-commands&quot;</span> <span class="kw">]]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="va">debug</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;yes&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb9-3"><a href="#cb9-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">bash</span> <span class="va">${debug</span><span class="op">:+</span><span class="st">&quot;-x&quot;</span><span class="va">}</span> script</span></code></pre></div>
<p>This is better than an unquoted value because the alternative value
can be properly quoted, e.g.
<code>wget ${output:+ -o "$output"}</code>.</p>
<p>Here are two common cases where this warning seems unnecessary but
may still be beneficial:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb10"><pre
class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb10-1"><a href="#cb10-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">cmd</span> <span class="op">&lt;&lt;&lt;</span> <span class="va">$var</span>         <span class="co"># Requires quoting on Bash 3 (but not 4+)</span></span>
<span id="cb10-2"><a href="#cb10-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">:</span> <span class="va">${var</span><span class="op">=</span>default<span class="va">}</span>     <span class="co"># Should be quoted to avoid DoS when var=&#39;*/*/*/*/*/*&#39;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>As always, this warning can be <a
href="https://www.shellcheck.net/wiki/ignore">ignored</a> on a
case-by-case basis.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2087 – Quote `EOF` to make here document expansions happen on the server side rather than on the client.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2087 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2087">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="quote-eof-to-make-here-document-expansions-happen-on-the-server-side-rather-than-on-the-client">Quote
<code>EOF</code> to make here document expansions happen on the server
side rather than on the client.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">ssh</span> host.example.com <span class="op">&lt;&lt; EOF</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">  echo &quot;Logged in on </span><span class="va">$HOSTNAME</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">EOF</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">ssh</span> host.example.com <span class="op">&lt;&lt; &quot;EOF&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">  echo &quot;Logged in on $HOSTNAME&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">EOF</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>When the end token of a here document is unquoted, parameter
expansion and command substitution will happen on in contents of the
here doc.</p>
<p>This means that before sending the commands to the server, the client
replaces <code>$HOSTNAME</code> with localhost, thereby sending
<code>echo "Logged in on localhost"</code> to the server. This has the
effect of printing the client's hostname instead of the server's.</p>
<p>Scripts with any kind of variable use are especially problematic
because all references will be expanded before the script run. For
example,</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">ssh</span> host <span class="op">&lt;&lt; EOF</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">  x=&quot;</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">uname</span> <span class="at">-a</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">  echo &quot;</span><span class="va">$x</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">EOF</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>will never print anything, neither client nor server details, since
before evaluation, it will be expanded to:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="va">x</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;Linux localhost ... x86_64 GNU/Linux&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-2"><a href="#cb4-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>By quoting the here token, local expansion will not take place, so
the server sees <code>echo "Logged in on $HOSTNAME"</code> which is
expanded and printed with the server's hostname, which is usually the
intention.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If the client should expand some or all variables, this message can
and should be ignored.</p>
<p>To expand a mix of local and remote variables, the here doc end token
should be unquoted, and the remote variables should be escaped, e.g.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb5"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb5-1"><a href="#cb5-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">ssh</span> host.example.com <span class="op">&lt;&lt; EOF</span></span>
<span id="cb5-2"><a href="#cb5-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">  echo &quot;Logged in on </span><span class="dt">\$</span><span class="st">HOSTNAME from </span><span class="va">$HOSTNAME</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb5-3"><a href="#cb5-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">EOF</span></span></code></pre></div>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2088 – Tilde does not expand in quotes. Use `$HOME`.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2088 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2088">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="tilde-does-not-expand-in-quotes-use-home">Tilde does not expand
in quotes. Use <code>$HOME</code>.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">rm</span> <span class="st">&quot;~/Desktop/</span><span class="va">$filename</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">rm</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$HOME</span><span class="st">/Desktop/</span><span class="va">$filename</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Tilde does not expand to the user's home directory when it's single
or double quoted. Use double quotes and <code>$HOME</code> instead.</p>
<p>Alternatively, the <code>~/</code> can be left unquoted, as in
<code>rm ~/"Desktop/$filename"</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>If you don't want the tilde to be expanded, you can ignore this
message.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>StackOverflow: <a
href="https://stackoverflow.com/questions/41871596/why-isnt-tilde-expanding-inside-double-quotes">Why
isn't tilde (~) expanding inside double quotes?</a></li>
</ul>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
