    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2165 – This nested loop overrides the index variable of its parent.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2165 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2165">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="this-nested-loop-overrides-the-index-variable-of-its-parent">This
nested loop overrides the index variable of its parent.</h2>
<p>And companion warning "This parent loop has its index variable
overridden." in <a href="SC2167">SC2167</a>.</p>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span><span class="kw">((</span><span class="va">i</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="dv">0</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="va">i</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="dv">10</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="va">i</span><span class="op">++</span><span class="kw">))</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">for</span> i <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="pp">*</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$i</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-6"><a href="#cb1-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">done</span></span>
<span id="cb1-7"><a href="#cb1-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span><span class="kw">((</span><span class="va">i</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="dv">0</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="va">i</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="dv">10</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="va">i</span><span class="op">++</span><span class="kw">))</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">for</span> j <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="pp">*</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$j</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">done</span></span>
<span id="cb2-7"><a href="#cb2-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>When nesting loops, especially arithmetic for loops, using the same
loop variable can cause unexpected results.</p>
<p>In the problematic code, <code>i</code> will contain the last
filename from the inner loop, which will be interpreted as a value in
the next iteration out the outer loop. This results in either an
infinite loop or a syntax error, depending on whether the last filename
is a valid shell variable name.</p>
<p>In nested for-in loops, variable merely shadow each other and won't
cause infinite loops or syntax errors, but reusing the variable name is
rarely intentional.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2166 – Prefer `[ p ] && [ q ]` as `[ p -a q ]` is not well-defined.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2166 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2166">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="prefer--p----q--as--p--a-q--is-not-well-defined">Prefer
<code>[ p ] &amp;&amp; [ q ]</code> as <code>[ p -a q ]</code> is not
well-defined.</h2>
<p>And likewise, prefer <code>[ p ] || [ q ]</code> over
<code>[ p -o q ]</code>.</p>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$1</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;test&quot;</span> <span class="ot">-a</span> <span class="ot">-z</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$2</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$1</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;test&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-z</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$2</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p><code>-a</code> and <code>-o</code> to mean AND and OR in a
<code>[ .. ]</code> test expression is not well defined, and can cause
incorrect results when arguments start with dashes or contain
<code>!</code>. <a
href="https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/utilities/test.html">From
POSIX</a>:</p>
<blockquote>
<p>The -a and -o binary primaries and the '(' and ')' operators have
been removed. (Many expressions using them were ambiguously defined by
the grammar depending on the specific expressions being evaluated.)
Scripts using these expressions should be converted to the forms given
below. Even though many implementations will continue to support these
forms, scripts should be extremely careful when dealing with
user-supplied input that could be confused with these and other
primaries and operators. Unless the application developer knows all the
cases that produce input to the script, invocations like:</p>
<p><code>test "$1" -a "$2"</code></p>
<p>should be written as:</p>
<p><code>test "$1" &amp;&amp; test "$2"</code></p>
</blockquote>
<p>Using multiple <code>[ .. ]</code> expressions with shell AND/OR
operators <code>&amp;&amp;</code> and <code>||</code> is well defined
and therefore preferred (but note that they have equal precedence, while
<code>-a</code>/<code>-o</code> is unspecified but usually implemented
as <code>-a</code> having higher precedence).</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If the shell variant being used is ksh derived (such as the bash
shell) it will have the shell builtin command <code>[[ ... ]]</code>.
This has the operators <code>&amp;&amp;</code>, <code>||</code>,
<code>(</code>, <code>)</code>, <code>!</code> which safely avoid the
ambiguity by noting which arguments were quoted and requiring the
operators to be unquoted (except by the <code>[[ ... ]]</code> construct
itself).</p>
<h3 id="see-also">See also:</h3>
<ul>
<li><a href="http://www.oilshell.org/blog/2017/08/31.html">Problems With
the test Builtin: What Does -a Mean?</a></li>
</ul>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>
</html>

    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="local-is-only-valid-in-functions"><code>local</code> is only
valid in functions.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">local</span> <span class="va">foo</span><span class="op">=</span>bar</span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$foo</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">foo</span><span class="op">=</span>bar</span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$foo</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>In Bash, <code>local</code> can only be used in functions. In other
contexts, it's an error.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>It's possible to source files containing <code>local</code> from a
function context but not from any other context. This is not good
practice, but in these cases you can <a href="ignore">ignore</a> this
error.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2170 – Invalid number for `-eq`. Use `=` to compare as string (or use `$var` to expand as a variable).</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2170 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2170">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="invalid-number-for--eq-use--to-compare-as-string-or-use-var-to-expand-as-a-variable">Invalid
number for <code>-eq</code>. Use <code>=</code> to compare as string (or
use <code>$var</code> to expand as a variable).</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">read</span> <span class="at">-r</span> <span class="va">n</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> n <span class="ot">-lt</span> 0 <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>   <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;bad input&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span>
<span id="cb1-6"><a href="#cb1-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb1-7"><a href="#cb1-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$USER</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">-eq</span> root <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb1-8"><a href="#cb1-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-9"><a href="#cb1-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;You are root&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-10"><a href="#cb1-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">read</span> <span class="at">-r</span> <span class="va">n</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$n</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">-lt</span> 0 <span class="bu">]</span>        <span class="co"># Numerical comparison</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>   <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;bad input&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-7"><a href="#cb2-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$USER</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> root <span class="bu">]</span>    <span class="co"># String comparison</span></span>
<span id="cb2-8"><a href="#cb2-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-9"><a href="#cb2-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;You are root&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-10"><a href="#cb2-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You are comparing a string value with a numerical operator, such as
<code>-eq</code>, <code>-ne</code>, <code>-lt</code> or
<code>-gt</code>. These only work for numbers.</p>
<p>If you want to compare the value as a string, switch to the
equivalent string operator: <code>=</code>, <code>!=</code>
<code>\&lt;</code> or <code>\&gt;</code>.</p>
<p>If you want to compare it as a number, such as
<code>n=42; while [ n -gt 1024/8 ]; ..</code>, then keep the operator
and expand the operands yourself with <code>$var</code> or
<code>$((expr))</code>: <code>while [ "$n" -gt $((1024/8)) ]</code></p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>

    <h2
id="found-trailing--outside-test-add-missing--or-quote-if-intentional">Found
trailing <code>]</code> outside test. Add missing <code>[</code> or
quote if intentional.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="ex">foo</span> <span class="at">-eq</span> bar ]<span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">then</span> <span class="fu">true</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">tr</span> <span class="at">-d</span> ]</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> foo <span class="ot">-eq</span> bar <span class="bu">]</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">then</span> <span class="fu">true</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">tr</span> <span class="at">-d</span> <span class="st">&#39;]&#39;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a non-test command that ends with <code>]</code> or
<code>]]</code>.</p>
<p>If this was intended to be a test expression like in the first
example, add the missing <code>[</code> or <code>[[</code>.</p>
<p>If the <code>]</code> was intended to be literal, like in
<code>tr -d ]</code>, you can quote to make this obvious.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p><code>tr -d ]</code> is valid and not different from
<code>tr -d ']'</code>, so in these cases you can ignore the error
instead.</p>

<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>

    <h2
id="trapping-signals-by-number-is-not-well-defined-prefer-signal-names">Trapping
signals by number is not well-defined. Prefer signal names.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">trap</span> myfunc 28</span></code></pre></div>

<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">trap</span> myfunc WINCH</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Signal numbers can vary between platforms. Prefer signal names, which
are fixed.</p>
<p>Signal numbers 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 14 and 15 are specified as parts of the
optional POSIX XSI and ShellCheck will not warn about these.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>

<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">trap</span> <span class="st">&#39;echo &quot;unkillable&quot;&#39;</span> KILL</span></code></pre></div>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2174 – When used with `-p`, `-m` only applies to the deepest directory.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2174 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2174">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="when-used-with--p--m-only-applies-to-the-deepest-directory">When
used with <code>-p</code>, <code>-m</code> only applies to the deepest
directory.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">mkdir</span> <span class="at">-p</span> <span class="at">-m</span> 0755 foo/bar/baz</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">mkdir</span> <span class="at">-p</span> foo/bar/baz</span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">chmod</span> 0755 foo/bar/baz foo/bar foo</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>When using <code>-m 0755</code>, the mode of the directory created
will be set to 0755. When using <code>-p</code>, parent directories
which do not exist will be created, but the mode specified by
<code>-m</code> will only be used on the last directory. The parent
directories will get their access mode the default way, via <a
href="http://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/umask.2.html">umask(2)</a>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck does not warn if the path only has one component, as in
<code>mkdir -p -m 0755 mydir</code>, but will not attempt to determine
whether this applies for a variable as in
<code>mkdir -p -m 0755 "$mydir"</code>. You can mkdir/chmod separately
or <a href="ignore">ignore</a> this message.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>
</html>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2175 – Quote this invalid brace expansion since it should be passed literally to eval</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2175 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2175">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="quote-this-invalid-brace-expansion-since-it-should-be-passed-literally-to-eval">Quote
this invalid brace expansion since it should be passed literally to
eval</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">eval</span> echo {1..<span class="va">$n</span>}</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">eval</span> <span class="st">&quot;echo {1..</span><span class="va">$n</span><span class="st">}&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Using <code>eval somecommand {1..$n}</code> depends both on bash
silently failing to interpret the brace expansion, and on it passing
failing brace expansions literally.</p>
<p>Rather than depending on these questionable features (which already
behave differently in other shells), use the explicit, predictable way
of passing values literally: quoting.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2176 – `time` is undefined for pipelines. time single stage or `bash -c` instead.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2176 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2176">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="time-is-undefined-for-pipelines-time-single-stage-or-bash--c-instead"><code>time</code>
is undefined for pipelines. time single stage or <code>bash -c</code>
instead.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">time</span> foo <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="ex">bar</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<p>To time the most relevant stage:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">foo</span> <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="kw">{</span> <span class="bu">time</span> bar<span class="kw">;</span> <span class="kw">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>To time everything in a pipeline:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">time</span> bash <span class="at">-c</span> <span class="st">&#39;foo | bar&#39;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Note that you can not use <code>time sh -c</code> to time an entire
pipeline, because POSIX does not guarantee that anything other than the
last stage is waited upon by the shell.</p>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>This behavior is explicitly left undefined <a
href="http://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/utilities/time.html">in
POSIX</a>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None. This warning is not emitted in <code>ksh</code> or
<code>bash</code> where <code>time</code> is defined for pipelines.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2177 – `time` is undefined for compound commands, use `time sh -c` instead.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />

  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2177 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2177">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="time-is-undefined-for-compound-commands-use-time-sh--c-instead"><code>time</code>
is undefined for compound commands, use <code>time sh -c</code>
instead.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">time</span> for i in <span class="pp">*</span>.bmp<span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">do</span> <span class="ex">convert</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$i</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$i</span><span class="st">.png&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">time</span> sh <span class="at">-c</span> <span class="st">&#39;for i in *.bmp; do convert &quot;$i&quot; &quot;$i.png&quot;; done&#39;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p><code>time</code> is only defined for Simple Commands <a
href="http://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/utilities/time.html">by
POSIX</a>. Timing loops, command groups and similar is not.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None. If you use a shell that supports this (e.g. bash, ksh), specify
this shell in the shebang.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2178 – Variable was used as an array but is now assigned a string.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2178 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2178">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="variable-was-used-as-an-array-but-is-now-assigned-a-string">Variable
was used as an array but is now assigned a string.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">flags</span><span class="op">[</span><span class="dv">0</span><span class="op">]=</span><span class="st">&quot;-r&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">flags</span><span class="op">[</span><span class="dv">1</span><span class="op">]=</span><span class="st">&quot;--delete-after&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$dryrun</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-6"><a href="#cb1-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>   <span class="va">flags</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;--dry-run&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-7"><a href="#cb1-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">flags</span><span class="op">[</span><span class="dv">0</span><span class="op">]=</span><span class="st">&quot;-r&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">flags</span><span class="op">[</span><span class="dv">1</span><span class="op">]=</span><span class="st">&quot;--delete-after&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$dryrun</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>   <span class="va">flags</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span> <span class="st">&quot;--dry-run&quot;</span> <span class="va">)</span></span>
<span id="cb2-7"><a href="#cb2-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck noticed that you have used a variable as an array, but
then assign it a string. <code>array=foo</code> is equivalent to
<code>array[0]=foo</code>, and leaves the rest of the elements
unaffected.</p>
<p>In the incorrect code, <code>"${flags[@]}"</code> would contain
<code>--dry-run</code> <code>--delete-after</code>.</p>
<p>To set an array to only a single, given element, you should use
<code>array=( foo )</code>.</p>
<p>In the correct code, <code>"${flags[@]}"</code> will contain
<code>--dry-run</code> only.</p>
<p>Another possible cause is accidentally missing the <code>$</code> on
a previous assignment: <code>var=(my command); var=bar</code> instead of
<code>var=$(my command); var=bar</code>. If the variable is not intended
to be an array, ensure that it's never assigned as one.</p>
<h3 id="bugs">Bugs:</h3>
<p>There is a <a
href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/issues/1309">known
issue</a> with this check's handling of <code>local</code> variables,
causing ShellCheck to flag variables that were previously declared as
arrays, even if they are in different scopes.</p>
<p>The easiest workaround is to simply use different variable names.
Alternatively, you can <a href="ignore">ignore</a> the check.</p>
<p>It is also possible to satisfy ShellCheck by declaring the
<code>local</code> variable separately from assigning to it, e.g.:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">foo ()</span> <span class="kw">{</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>   <span class="bu">local</span> <span class="at">-a</span> <span class="va">baz</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>   <span class="va">baz</span><span class="op">+=</span><span class="va">(</span><span class="st">&quot;foo&quot;</span> <span class="st">&quot;bar&quot;</span><span class="va">)</span></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>   <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${baz</span><span class="op">[@]</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-5"><a href="#cb3-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span></span>
<span id="cb3-6"><a href="#cb3-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb3-7"><a href="#cb3-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">bar ()</span> <span class="kw">{</span></span>
<span id="cb3-8"><a href="#cb3-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>   <span class="bu">local</span> <span class="va">baz</span> <span class="co"># ShellCheck gets confused if these lines are merged as local baz=&quot;qux&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-9"><a href="#cb3-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>   <span class="va">baz</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;qux&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-10"><a href="#cb3-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>   <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$baz</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-11"><a href="#cb3-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2179 – Use `array+=("item")` to append items to an array.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2179 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2179">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="use-arrayitem-to-append-items-to-an-array">Use
<code>array+=("item")</code> to append items to an array.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span>one two<span class="va">)</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">+=</span>three</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span>one two<span class="va">)</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">+=</span><span class="va">(</span> three <span class="va">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>It looks like you are trying to append a string to an array with
<code>var+=string</code>. This instead appends to the first element of
the array (equivalent to <code>var[0]+=three</code>).</p>
<p>In the problematic code, the array will therefore contain
<code>onethree</code> <code>two</code>.</p>
<p>Instead, append an array to the array with
<code>var+=( elements )</code>. This will append the new items to the
array.</p>
<p>In the correct code, it will contain <code>one</code>
<code>two</code> <code>three</code> as expected.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If ShellCheck mistakenly thinks the variable is an array when it's
not (e.g. because the same name was used in a different context), you
can ignore this error.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2180 – Bash does not support multidimensional arrays. Use 1D or associative arrays.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2180 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2180">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="bash-does-not-support-multidimensional-arrays-use-1d-or-associative-arrays">Bash
does not support multidimensional arrays. Use 1D or associative
arrays.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">foo</span><span class="op">[</span><span class="dv">1</span><span class="op">][</span><span class="dv">2</span><span class="op">]=</span>bar</span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${foo</span><span class="op">[</span><span class="dv">1</span><span class="op">][</span><span class="dv">2</span><span class="op">]</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<p>In bash4, consider using associative arrays:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">declare</span> <span class="at">-A</span> <span class="va">foo</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">foo</span><span class="op">[</span><span class="dv">1</span>,2<span class="op">]=</span>bar</span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${foo</span><span class="op">[</span><span class="dv">1</span>,2<span class="op">]</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Otherwise, do your own index arithmetic:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">size</span><span class="op">=</span>10</span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">foo</span><span class="op">[</span><span class="dv">1</span><span class="pp">*</span>size+2<span class="op">]=</span>bar</span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${foo</span><span class="op">[</span><span class="dv">1</span><span class="pp">*</span>size+2<span class="op">]</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Bash does not support multidimensional arrays. Rewrite it to use 1D
arrays. Associative arrays map arbitrary strings to values, and are
therefore useful since you can construct keys like <code>"1,2,3"</code>
or <code>"val1;val2;val3"</code> to index them.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2181 – Check exit code directly with e.g. `if mycmd;`, not indirectly with `$?`.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2181 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2181">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="check-exit-code-directly-with-eg-if-mycmd-not-indirectly-with-">Check
exit code directly with e.g. <code>if mycmd;</code>, not indirectly with
<code>$?</code>.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">make</span> mytarget</span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="va">$?</span> <span class="ot">-ne</span> 0 <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Build failed&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-6"><a href="#cb1-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="ot">! </span><span class="fu">make</span> mytarget</span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Build failed&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>For the Solaris 10 Bourne shell:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="fu">make</span> mytarget</span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">:</span></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">else</span></span>
<span id="cb3-5"><a href="#cb3-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Build failed&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-6"><a href="#cb3-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Running a command and then checking its exit status <code>$?</code>
against 0 is redundant.</p>
<p>Instead of just checking the exit code of a command, it checks the
exit code of a command (e.g. <code>[</code>) that checks the exit code
of a command.</p>
<p>Apart from the redundancy, there are other reasons to avoid this
pattern:</p>
<ul>
<li>Since the command and its status test are decoupled, inserting an
innocent command like <code>echo "make finished"</code> after
<code>make</code> will cause the <code>if</code> statement to silently
start comparing <code>echo</code>'s status instead.</li>
<li>Scripts that run or are called with <code>set -e</code> aka
<code>errexit</code> will exit immediately if the command fails, even
though they're followed by a clause that handles failure.</li>
<li>The value of <code>$?</code> is overwritten by
<code>[</code>/<code>[[</code>, so you can't get the original value in
the relevant then/else block (e.g.
<code>if mycmd; then echo "Success"; else echo "Failed with $?"; fi</code>).</li>
</ul>
<p>To check that a command returns success, use
<code>if mycommand; then ...</code>.</p>
<p>To check that a command returns failure, use
<code>if ! mycommand; then ...</code>. Notice that <code>!</code> will
overwrite <code>$?</code> value.</p>
<p>To additionally capture output with command substitution:
<code>if ! output=$(mycommand); then ...</code></p>
<p>This also applies to <code>while</code>/<code>until</code> loops.</p>
<p>The default Solaris 10 Bourne shell does not support negating exit
statuses with <code>!</code>, so <code>! mycommand</code> tries to
invoke a utility named "!" instead. To test for failure, use
<code>if mycommand; then :; else ...; fi</code> and
<code>until mycommand; do ...; done</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>
</html>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2182 – This printf format string has no variables. Other arguments are ignored.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2182 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2182">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="this-printf-format-string-has-no-variables-other-arguments-are-ignored">This
printf format string has no variables. Other arguments are ignored.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">place</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;world&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">printf</span> hello <span class="va">$place</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">place</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;world&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">printf</span> <span class="st">&quot;hello %s\n&quot;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$place</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck has noticed that you're using a <code>printf</code> with
multiple arguments, but where the first argument has no <code>%s</code>
or equivalent variable placeholders.</p>
<p><code>echo</code> accepts zero or more strings to write, e.g.
<code>echo hello world</code>.</p>
<p><code>printf</code> instead accepts one pattern/template with zero or
more <code>%s</code>-style placeholders, and one argument for each
placeholder.</p>
<p>Rewrite your command using the right semantics, otherwise all
arguments after the first one will be ignored:</p>
<pre><code>$ printf hello world\\n
hello

$ printf &quot;hello world\n&quot;
hello world

$ printf &quot;hello %s\n&quot; &quot;world&quot;
hello world</code></pre>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you wanted a no-op, use <code>:</code> instead.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">:</span> <span class="va">${place</span><span class="op">=</span>world<span class="va">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2183 – This format string has 2 variables, but is passed 1 argument.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2183 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2183">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="this-format-string-has-2-variables-but-is-passed-1-argument">This
format string has 2 variables, but is passed 1 argument.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">printf</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello %s, welcome to %s.\n&quot;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$USER</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">printf</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello %s, welcome to %s.\n&quot;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$USER</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$HOSTNAME</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck has noticed that you're using a <code>printf</code> format
string with more <code>%s</code> variables than arguments to fill
them.</p>
<p>In the problematic example case, the last <code>%s</code> will just
become an empty string every time.</p>
<p>Either remove the unused variables from the format string, or add
enough arguments to fill them.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>When using the Ksh/Bash <code>%T</code> timestamp extension, such as
<code>printf 'The time is %(%H:%M)T\n'</code>, an argument of
<code>-1</code> and no argument are both taken to mean the current time.
In these cases, consider specifying <code>-1</code> explicitly.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2184 – Quote arguments to unset so they're not glob expanded.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2184 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2184">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="quote-arguments-to-unset-so-theyre-not-glob-expanded">Quote
arguments to unset so they're not glob expanded.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">unset</span> <span class="va">foo[</span>index<span class="op">]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">unset</span> <span class="st">&#39;foo[index]&#39;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Arguments to <code>unset</code> are subject to regular glob
expansion. This is especially relevant when unsetting indices in arrays,
where <code>[..]</code> is considered a glob character group.</p>
<p>In the problematic code, having a file called <code>food</code> in
the current directory will result in <code>unset foo[index]</code>
expanding to <code>unset food</code>, which will silently succeed
without unsetting the element.</p>
<p>Quoting so that the <code>[..]</code> is passed literally to
<code>unset</code> solves the issue.</p>
<p>Note that you can unset element using variable for index name like
this:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">unset</span> <span class="st">&#39;foo[$var]&#39;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you know that pathname expansion is disabled you can ignore this
message. <code>set -o noglob</code> (and variations like invoking the
script with <code>#!/bin/bash -f</code>) will prevent glob expansion of
arguments to <code>unset</code>.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2185 – Some finds don't have a default path. Specify `.` explicitly.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2185 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2185">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="some-finds-dont-have-a-default-path-specify--explicitly">Some
finds don't have a default path. Specify <code>.</code> explicitly.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">find</span> <span class="at">-type</span> f</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">find</span> . <span class="at">-type</span> f</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>When not provided a search path, GNU and Busybox <code>find</code>
will use a default path of <code>.</code>, the current directory.</p>
<p>On POSIX, macOS/OSX, FreeBSD, OpenBSD and NetBSD, it will instead
result in an error.</p>
<p>Explicitly specifying a path works across all implementations, and is
therefore preferred.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>You will get a false positive if you concatenate a series of pre-path
flags:</p>
<pre><code>find -XLE .</code></pre>
<p>In such cases, please either use <code>find -X -L -E .</code> or <a
href="ignore">ignore</a> the message.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2186 – tempfile is deprecated. Use mktemp instead.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2186 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2186">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="tempfile-is-deprecated-use-mktemp-instead">tempfile is
deprecated. Use mktemp instead.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">tmp</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">tempfile</span><span class="va">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">tmp</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">mktemp</span><span class="va">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p><code>tempfile</code> is a Debian specific utility for creating
temporary files. Its man page notes:</p>
<blockquote>
<p>tempfile is deprecated; you should use mktemp(1) instead.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>Neither <code>tempfile</code> nor <code>mktemp</code> are POSIX, but
<code>tempfile</code> is Debian specific while <code>mktemp</code> works
on GNU, OSX, BusyBox, *BSD and Solaris.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck will not recognize when a function overrides this
name.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2187 – Ash scripts will be checked as Dash. Add `# shellcheck shell=dash` to silence.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2187 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2187">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="ash-scripts-will-be-checked-as-dash-add--shellcheck-shelldash-to-silence">Ash
scripts will be checked as Dash. Add
<code># shellcheck shell=dash</code> to silence.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/ash</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/ash</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># shellcheck shell=dash</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck has no first class support for <code>ash</code>, but it
does support its Debian fork <code>dash</code> and defaults to this
whenever <code>ash</code> is specified.</p>
<p>Unfortunately, while the two are similar, they are not completely
compatible. For example, <code>ash</code> supports <code>echo -e</code>
but <code>dash</code> does not, so ShellCheck will incorrectly warn
about it.</p>
<p>You can use a <a href="directive">directive</a> to let ShellCheck
know you're aware of this problem.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2188 – This redirection doesn't have a command. Move to its command (or use `true` as no-op).</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2188 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2188">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="this-redirection-doesnt-have-a-command-move-to-its-command-or-use-true-as-no-op">This
redirection doesn't have a command. Move to its command (or use
<code>true</code> as no-op).</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">{</span> </span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Report for </span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">date</span> +%F<span class="va">)</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">uptime</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">df</span> <span class="at">-h</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span></span>
<span id="cb1-6"><a href="#cb1-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="op">&gt;</span> report.txt</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">{</span> </span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Report for </span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">date</span> +%F<span class="va">)</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">uptime</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">df</span> <span class="at">-h</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span> <span class="op">&gt;</span> report.txt</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a redirection that doesn't actually redirect from/to
anything.</p>
<p>This could indicate a bug, such as in the problematic code where an
additional linefeed causes <code>report.txt</code> to be truncated
instead of containing report output, or in
<code>foo &amp; &gt; bar</code>, where either
<code>foo &amp;&gt; bar</code> or <code>foo &gt; bar &amp;</code> was
intended.</p>
<p>However, it could also be intentionally used to truncate a file or
check that it's readable. You can make this more explicit for both
ShellCheck and human readers by using <code>true</code> or
<code>:</code> as a dummy command, e.g. <code>true &gt; file</code> or
<code>: &gt; file</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>There are no semantic problems with using <code>&gt; foo</code> over
<code>true &gt; foo</code>, so if you don't see this as a potential
source of bugs or confusion, you can <a href="ignore">ignore</a> it.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2189 – You can't have `|` between this redirection and the command it should apply to.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2189 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2189">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="you-cant-have--between-this-redirection-and-the-command-it-should-apply-to">You
can't have <code>|</code> between this redirection and the command it
should apply to.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">&lt;</span> file.txt <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="fu">grep</span> foo</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">&lt;</span> file.txt <span class="fu">grep</span> foo   <span class="co"># or more canonically: grep foo &lt; file.txt</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck has found a stage in a pipeline that consists of a
redirection but no command. This doesn't make sense because a
redirection without a command will not read or write any data.</p>
<p>This is most likely to occur when deleting a command that had a
redirection, but leaving a <code>|</code> behind instead of moving the
redirection to a different command:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Match lines with line numbers</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">nl</span> <span class="op">&lt;</span> foo.txt <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="fu">grep</span> bar</span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Incorrect attempt at removing line numbers. grep now has no input:</span></span>
<span id="cb3-5"><a href="#cb3-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">&lt;</span> foo.txt <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="fu">grep</span> bar</span>
<span id="cb3-6"><a href="#cb3-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb3-7"><a href="#cb3-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Line numbers correctly removed. grep now reads foo.txt as intended.</span></span>
<span id="cb3-8"><a href="#cb3-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">grep</span> bar <span class="op">&lt;</span> foo.txt</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>It's technically valid to do e.g.
<code>echo foo | &gt; "$(cat)"</code> to truncate a file called "foo",
but please consider rewriting such code.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2190 – Elements in associative arrays need index, e.g. `array=( [index]=value )` .</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2190 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2190">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="elements-in-associative-arrays-need-index-eg-array-indexvalue--">Elements
in associative arrays need index, e.g.
<code>array=( [index]=value )</code> .</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">declare</span> <span class="at">-A</span> <span class="va">foo</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">foo</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span> myvalue <span class="va">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">declare</span> <span class="at">-A</span> <span class="va">foo</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">foo</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span> <span class="op">[</span>key<span class="op">]</span><span class="va">=</span>myvalue <span class="va">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You appear to be initializing or appending an array element to an
associative array without giving it an index. In an indexed array,
elements will be auto-indexed by incremented characters. In associative
arrays, the index must be given explicitly.</p>
<p>This could happen because of invalid spaces or otherwise malformed
index assignment, such as <code>array=( [key] = value )</code>. This
should instead be <code>array=( [key]=value )</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck may be confused when a variable name is reused in
different contexts. If ShellCheck mistakenly believes the array is
associative, please <a href="ignore">ignore</a> this error.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2191 – The `=` here is literal. To assign by index, use `( [index]=value )` with no spaces. To keep as literal, quote it.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2191 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2191">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="the--here-is-literal-to-assign-by-index-use--indexvalue--with-no-spaces-to-keep-as-literal-quote-it">The
<code>=</code> here is literal. To assign by index, use
<code>( [index]=value )</code> with no spaces. To keep as literal, quote
it.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">array</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span> <span class="op">[</span>index<span class="op">]</span> = value <span class="va">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">array</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span> <span class="op">[</span>index<span class="op">]</span><span class="va">=</span>value <span class="va">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>The shell doesn't care about the <code>=</code> sign in your array
assignment because it's not part of a recognized index assignment.
Instead, it's considered a literal character and becomes part of an
array element's value.</p>
<p>In the example problematic code, this is because the <code>=</code>
was intended to set the index, but the shell will not recognize it when
it is surrounded by spaces.</p>
<p>Make sure to remove any spaces around the <code>=</code> when
assigning by index, such as in the correct code.</p>
<p>If you wanted the <code>=</code> to be a literal part of the array
element, add quotes around it, such as <code>env=( "LC_CTYPE=C" )</code>
or <code>specialChars=( "=" "%" ";" )</code> .</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2192 – This array element has no value. Remove spaces after `=` or use `""` for empty string.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2192 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2192">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="this-array-element-has-no-value-remove-spaces-after--or-use--for-empty-string">This
array element has no value. Remove spaces after <code>=</code> or use
<code>""</code> for empty string.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">array</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span><span class="op">[</span><span class="dv">1</span><span class="op">]</span><span class="va">=</span>one <span class="op">[</span><span class="dv">2</span><span class="op">]</span><span class="va">=</span> two<span class="va">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">array</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span><span class="op">[</span><span class="dv">1</span><span class="op">]</span><span class="va">=</span>one <span class="op">[</span><span class="dv">2</span><span class="op">]</span><span class="va">=</span>two<span class="va">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You have an array element on the form <code>[index]=</code>. The
shell will interpret this as an independent element with index
<code>index</code> and value <code>&lt;empty string&gt;</code>.</p>
<p>This may happen as part of the expression
<code>[index]= value</code>, where the space is not allowed and causes
the shell to interpret it as
<code>[index]="" [index+1]=value</code>.</p>
<p>If you wanted the element to have a value, remove the spaces after
<code>=</code>, e.g. <code>[index]=value</code>.</p>
<p>If you wanted to assign an empty string, explicitly use empty quotes:
<code>[index]=""</code>. This makes no difference to the shell, but will
make your intention clear to shellcheck and other humans.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>
