    <title>ShellCheck: SC2193 – The arguments to this comparison can never be equal. Make sure your syntax is correct.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2193 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2193">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="the-arguments-to-this-comparison-can-never-be-equal-make-sure-your-syntax-is-correct">The
arguments to this comparison can never be equal. Make sure your syntax
is correct.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="va">$var</span>+1 <span class="ot">==</span> 5 <span class="bu">]</span>              <span class="co"># Unevaluated math</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;{</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">}&quot;</span> <span class="ot">==</span> <span class="st">&quot;value&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span>      <span class="co"># Swapped around $ and {</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="ex">cmd1</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st"> | cmd2&quot;</span> <span class="ot">==</span> <span class="st">&quot;42&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="co"># Ended with ) too soon</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st"> &quot;</span> <span class="ot">==</span> <span class="pp">*</span>.png <span class="kw">]]</span>       <span class="co"># Trailing space</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="va">$((var</span><span class="op">+</span><span class="dv">1</span><span class="va">))</span> <span class="ot">==</span> 5 <span class="bu">]</span>          <span class="co"># Evaluated math</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${var}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">==</span> <span class="st">&quot;value&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span>      <span class="co"># Correct variable expansion</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="ex">cmd1</span> <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="ex">cmd2</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">==</span> <span class="st">&quot;42&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="co"># Correct command substitution</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">==</span> <span class="pp">*</span>.png <span class="kw">]]</span>        <span class="co"># No trailing space</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck has determined that the two values you're comparing can
never be equal.</p>
<p>Most of the time, this happens because of a syntax issue that
introduced unintended literal characters into one of the arguments.</p>
<p>The left-hand side in the problematic examples will always contain
(respectively) curly braces, pipe and trailing space. The right-hand
sides are literal values and a pattern without trailing spaces, so they
will never be equal. The statement is therefore useless, strongly
indicating a bug.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">case</span> foo <span class="kw">in</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="ss">bar</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Match&quot;</span></span>

    <h2
id="this-pattern-will-never-match-the-case-statements-word-double-check-them">This
pattern will never match the case statement's word. Double check
them.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">case</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st"> &quot;</span> <span class="kw">in</span>      <span class="co"># Trailing space</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="ss">value</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Match&quot;</span></span>

<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">case</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${var}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="kw">in</span>     <span class="co"># No trailing space</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="ss">value</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Match&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">esac</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck has detected that one of the patterns in a
<code>case</code> statement will never match.</p>
<p>Often, this is due to mistakes in the case statement word that
results in unintended literal characters. In the problematic code,
there's a trailing space that will prevent the match from ever
succeeding.</p>
<p>For more examples of when this could happen, see <a
href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2193">SC2193</a> for
the equivalent warning for <code>[[ .. ]]</code> statements.</p>
<p>Note that ShellCheck warns about individual patterns in a branch, and
will flag <code>*.png</code> in this example even though the branch is
not dead:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">case</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${img}</span><span class="st">.jpg&quot;</span> <span class="kw">in</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="pp">*</span><span class="ss">.png</span> <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="pp">*</span><span class="ss">.jpg</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;It&#39;s an image&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">esac</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None. If you encounter a bug and wish to <a href="ignore">ignore</a>
this warning, make sure the directive goes in front of the
<code>case</code> and not the individual branch.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2196 – `egrep` is non-standard and deprecated. Use `grep -E` instead.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2196 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2196">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="egrep-is-non-standard-and-deprecated-use-grep--e-instead"><code>egrep</code>
is non-standard and deprecated. Use <code>grep -E</code> instead.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">egrep</span> <span class="st">&#39;foo|bar&#39;</span> file</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">grep</span> <span class="at">-E</span> <span class="st">&#39;foo|bar&#39;</span> file</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p><code>egrep</code> is a non-standard command. Its functionality is
provided in POSIX by <code>grep -E</code>. <a
href="http://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/utilities/grep.html">POSIX
grep</a> says:</p>
<blockquote>
<p>This grep has been enhanced in an upwards-compatible way to provide
the exact functionality of the historical egrep and fgrep commands as
well. It was the clear intention of the standard developers to
consolidate the three greps into a single command.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>man grep for GNU says:</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Direct invocation as either egrep or fgrep is deprecated</p>
</blockquote>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck will fail to recognize when functions override
<code>egrep</code>. Consider giving it a different name or <a
href="ignore">ignore</a> this error.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <hr />
    <h2
id="fgrep-is-non-standard-and-deprecated-use-grep--f-instead"><code>fgrep</code>
is non-standard and deprecated. Use <code>grep -F</code> instead.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">fgrep</span> <span class="st">&#39;*.*&#39;</span> file</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">grep</span> <span class="at">-F</span> <span class="st">&#39;*.*&#39;</span> file</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p><code>fgrep</code> is a non-standard command. Its functionality is
provided in POSIX by <code>grep -F</code>. <a
href="http://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/utilities/grep.html">POSIX
grep</a> says:</p>
<blockquote>
<p>This grep has been enhanced in an upwards-compatible way to provide
the exact functionality of the historical egrep and fgrep commands as
well. It was the clear intention of the standard developers to
consolidate the three greps into a single command.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>man grep for GNU says:</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Direct invocation as either egrep or fgrep is deprecated</p>
</blockquote>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck will fail to recognize when functions override
<code>fgrep</code>. Consider giving it a different name or <a
href="ignore">ignore</a> this error.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2198 – Arrays don't work as operands in `[ ]`. Use a loop (or concatenate with `*` instead of `@`).</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2198 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2198">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="arrays-dont-work-as-operands-in---use-a-loop-or-concatenate-with--instead-of-">Arrays
don't work as operands in <code>[ ]</code>. Use a loop (or concatenate
with <code>*</code> instead of <code>@</code>).</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">ext</span><span class="op">=</span>png</span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">allowedExt</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span>jpg bmp png<span class="va">)</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$ext</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${allowedExt</span><span class="op">[@]</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Extension is valid&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">ext</span><span class="op">=</span>png</span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">allowedExt</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span>jpg bmp png<span class="va">)</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> value <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${allowedExt</span><span class="op">[@]</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$ext</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$value</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Extension is valid&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Array expansions become a series of words in <code>[ .. ]</code>.
Operators expect single words only.</p>
<p>The problematic code is equivalent to
<code>[ "$ext" = jpg bmp png ]</code>, which is invalid syntax. A
typical error message is <code>bash: [: too many arguments</code> or
<code>dash: somefile: unexpected operator</code>.</p>
<p>Instead, use a <code>for</code> loop to iterate over values, and
apply your condition to each.</p>
<p>Alternatively, if you want to concatenate all the values in the array
into a single string for your test, use <code>"$*"</code> or
<code>"${array[*]}"</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you are dynamically building an a test expression, make your array
the only thing in the test expression. ShellCheck will not emit a
warning for: <code>set -- 1 -lt 2; [ "$@" ]</code></p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <h1>SC2199 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2199">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="arrays-implicitly-concatenate-in---use-a-loop-or-explicit--instead-of-">Arrays
implicitly concatenate in <code>[[ ]]</code>. Use a loop (or explicit
<code>*</code> instead of <code>@</code>).</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">ext</span><span class="op">=</span>png</span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">allowedExt</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span>jpg bmp png<span class="va">)</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$ext</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${allowedExt</span><span class="op">[@]</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="kw">]]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Extension is valid&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">ext</span><span class="op">=</span>png</span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">allowedExt</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span>jpg bmp png<span class="va">)</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> value <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${allowedExt</span><span class="op">[@]</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$ext</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$value</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="kw">]]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Extension is valid&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Array expansions in <code>[[ .. ]]</code> will implicitly concatenate
into a single string, much like in assignments. The problematic code is
equivalent to <code>[ "$ext" = "jpg bmp png" ]</code>.</p>
<p>Instead, use a <code>for</code> loop to iterate over values, and
apply your condition to each.</p>
<p>Alternatively, if you do want to concatenate all the values in the
array into a single string for your test, use <code>"$*"</code> or
<code>"${array[*]}"</code> to make this explicit.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>

  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2201 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2201">See this page on GitHub</a>

    <h2 id="brace-expansion-doesnt-happen-in---use-a-loop">Brace expansion
doesn't happen in <code>[[ ]]</code>. Use a loop.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$file</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> index.{htm,html,php} <span class="kw">]]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;This is the main file&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> main <span class="kw">in</span> index.<span class="dt">{htm</span><span class="op">,</span><span class="dt">html</span><span class="op">,</span><span class="dt">php}</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$file</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$main</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="kw">]]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;This is the main file&quot;</span></span>

<p>Brace expansions doesn't happen in <code>[[ ]]</code>. They will just

<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>

    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2202 – Globs don't work as operands in `[ ]`. Use a loop.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2202 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2202">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="globs-dont-work-as-operands-in---use-a-loop">Globs don't work as
operands in <code>[ ]</code>. Use a loop.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> current.log <span class="ot">-nt</span> backup/<span class="pp">*</span>.log <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;This is the latest file&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">newerThanAll</span><span class="op">=</span>true</span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> log <span class="kw">in</span> backup/<span class="pp">*</span>.log</span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">[</span> current.log <span class="ot">-nt</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$log</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="kw">||</span> <span class="va">newerThanAll</span><span class="op">=</span>false</span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$newerThanAll</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;true&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;This is the latest file&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Globs in <code>[ ]</code> will expand to a sequence of words, one per
matching filename. Meanwhile, operators work on single words.</p>
<p>The problematic code is equivalent to
<code>[ current.log -nt backup/file1.log backup/file2.log backup/file3.log ]</code>,
which is invalid syntax. A typical error message is
<code>bash: [: too many arguments</code> or
<code>dash: somefile: unexpected operator</code>.</p>
<p>Instead, use a <code>for</code> loop to iterate over matching
filenames, and apply your condition to each.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you know your glob will only ever match one file, you can check
this explicitly and use the first file:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">set</span> <span class="at">--</span> backup/<span class="pp">*</span>.log</span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="va">$#</span> <span class="ot">-eq</span> 1 <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="kw">||</span> <span class="kw">{</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;There are too many matches.&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="bu">exit</span> 1<span class="kw">;</span> <span class="kw">}</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> file.log <span class="ot">-nt</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$1</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;This is the latest file&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Alternatively, <a href="ignore">ignore</a> this warning.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2203 – Globs are ignored in `[[ ]]` except right of `=`/`!=`. Use a loop.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2203 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2203">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="globs-are-ignored-in---except-right-of--use-a-loop">Globs are
ignored in <code>[[ ]]</code> except right of
<code>=</code>/<code>!=</code>. Use a loop.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> current.log <span class="ot">-nt</span> backup/<span class="pp">*</span>.log <span class="kw">]]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;This is the latest file&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">newerThanAll</span><span class="op">=</span>true</span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> log <span class="kw">in</span> backup/<span class="pp">*</span>.log</span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">[[</span> current.log <span class="ot">-nt</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$log</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="kw">]]</span> <span class="kw">||</span> <span class="va">newerThanAll</span><span class="op">=</span>false</span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$newerThanAll</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;true&quot;</span> <span class="kw">]]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;This is the latest file&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Globs in <code>[[ ]]</code> will not filename expand, and will be
treated literally (or as patterns on the right-hand side of
<code>=</code>, <code>==</code> and <code>!=</code>).</p>
<p>The problematic code is equivalent to
<code>[[ current.log -nt 'backup/*.png' ]</code>, and will look for a
file with a literal asterisk in the name.</p>
<p>Instead, you can iterate over the filenames you want with a loop, and
apply your condition to each filename.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2204 – `(..)` is a subshell. Did you mean `[ .. ]`, a test expression?</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2204 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2204">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="-is-a-subshell-did-you-mean----a-test-expression"><code>(..)</code>
is a subshell. Did you mean <code>[ .. ]</code>, a test expression?</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="kw">(</span> <span class="ex">-d</span> mydir <span class="kw">)</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;It&#39;s a directory&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-d</span> mydir <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;It&#39;s a directory&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Tests like <code>-d</code> to see if something is a directory or
<code>-z</code> to see if it's non-empty are actually flags to the
<code>test</code> command, and only work as tests in that context.
<code>[</code> is an alias for <code>test</code>, so you'll frequently
see them written as <code>[ -d mydir ]</code>.</p>
<p><code>( .. )</code> is completely unrelated, and is a subshell mostly
used to scope shell modifications. They should not be used in
<code>if</code> or <code>while</code> statements in shell scripts.</p>
<p>If you wanted to test a condition, rewrite the <code>( .. )</code> to
<code>[ .. ]</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
<p>This error is triggered by having a unary test operator as the first
command name in a subshell, which won't normally happen. Note that
there's a similar warning <a href="SC2205">SC2205</a> with a higher
false positive rate.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2205 – `(..)` is a subshell. Did you mean `[ .. ]`, a test expression?</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2205 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2205">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="-is-a-subshell-did-you-mean----a-test-expression"><code>(..)</code>
is a subshell. Did you mean <code>[ .. ]</code>, a test expression?</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="kw">(</span> <span class="ex">1</span> <span class="at">-lt</span> 2 <span class="kw">)</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;1 is less than 2&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> 1 <span class="ot">-lt</span> 2 <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;1 is less than 2&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Tests like <code>-eq</code> to check numeric equality or
<code>\&lt;</code> for string comparison only work are actually
parameters to the <code>test</code> command, and only work as tests in
that context. <code>[</code> is an alias for <code>test</code>, so
you'll frequently see them written as <code>[ 1 -eq 2 ]</code>.</p>
<p><code>( .. )</code> is completely unrelated, and is a subshell mostly
used to scope shell modifications. They should not be used in
<code>if</code> or <code>while</code> statements in shell scripts.</p>
<p>If you wanted to test a condition, rewrite the <code>( .. )</code> to
<code>[ .. ]</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>This error is triggered by having a binary operator as the first
parameter in a subshell, and could falsely trigger on e.g.
<code>if ( grep -eq "foo|bar" file )</code>. In these cases, check
whether the subshell is actually needed.</p>
<p>Note that there's a similar looking error <a href="SC2204">SC2204</a>
with a low false positive rate.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2206 – Quote to prevent word splitting/globbing, or split robustly with mapfile or `read -a`.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2206 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2206">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="quote-to-prevent-word-splittingglobbing-or-split-robustly-with-mapfile-or-read--a">Quote
to prevent word splitting/globbing, or split robustly with mapfile or
<code>read -a</code>.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">array</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span> <span class="va">$var</span> <span class="va">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<p>If the variable should be a single element:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">array</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="va">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>If it's multiple lines, each of which should be an element:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># For bash</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">mapfile</span> <span class="at">-t</span> array <span class="op">&lt;&lt;&lt;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># For ksh</span></span>
<span id="cb3-5"><a href="#cb3-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">printf</span> <span class="st">&#39;%s\n&#39;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="cf">while</span> <span class="va">IFS</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;&quot;</span> <span class="bu">read</span> <span class="at">-r</span> <span class="va">line</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">do</span> <span class="va">array</span><span class="op">+=</span><span class="va">(</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$line</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>If it's a line with multiple words (separated by spaces, other
delimiters can be chosen with IFS), <a
href="https://stackoverflow.com/a/30212526">each of which should be an
element</a>:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># For bash</span></span>
<span id="cb4-2"><a href="#cb4-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">IFS</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot; &quot;</span> <span class="bu">read</span> <span class="at">-r</span> <span class="at">-a</span> <span class="va">array</span> <span class="op">&lt;&lt;&lt;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-3"><a href="#cb4-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb4-4"><a href="#cb4-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># For ksh</span></span>
<span id="cb4-5"><a href="#cb4-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">IFS</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot; &quot;</span> <span class="bu">read</span> <span class="at">-r</span> <span class="at">-A</span> <span class="va">array</span> <span class="op">&lt;&lt;&lt;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You are expanding a variable unquoted in an array. This will invoke
the shell's sloppy word splitting and glob expansion.</p>
<p>Instead, prefer explicitly splitting (or not splitting):</p>
<ul>
<li>If the variable should become a single array element, quote it.</li>
<li>If you want to split into lines or words, use <code>mapfile</code>,
<code>read -ra</code> and/or <code>while</code> loops as
appropriate.</li>
</ul>
<p>This prevents the shell from doing unwanted splitting and glob
expansion, and therefore avoiding problems with data containing spaces
or special characters.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you have already taken care (through setting IFS and
<code>set -f</code>) to have word splitting work the way you intend, you
can <a href="ignore">ignore</a> this warning.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2207 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2207">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="prefer-mapfile-or-read--a-to-split-command-output-or-quote-to-avoid-splitting">Prefer
<code>mapfile</code> or <code>read -a</code> to split command output (or
quote to avoid splitting).</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">array</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span> <span class="va">$(</span><span class="ex">mycommand</span><span class="va">)</span> <span class="va">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<p>If it outputs multiple lines, each of which should be an element:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># For bash 4.4+, must not be in posix mode, may use temporary files</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">mapfile</span> <span class="at">-t</span> array <span class="op">&lt;</span> <span class="op">&lt;(</span><span class="ex">mycommand</span><span class="op">)</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># For bash 3.x+, must not be in posix mode, may use temporary files</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">array</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">()</span></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">while</span> <span class="va">IFS</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&#39;&#39;</span> <span class="bu">read</span> <span class="at">-r</span> <span class="va">line</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">do</span> <span class="va">array</span><span class="op">+=</span><span class="va">(</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$line</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">done</span> <span class="op">&lt;</span> <span class="op">&lt;(</span><span class="ex">mycommand</span><span class="op">)</span></span>
<span id="cb2-7"><a href="#cb2-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-8"><a href="#cb2-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># For ksh, and bash 4.2+ with the lastpipe option enabled (may require disabling monitor mode)</span></span>
<span id="cb2-9"><a href="#cb2-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">array</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">()</span></span>
<span id="cb2-10"><a href="#cb2-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">mycommand</span> <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="cf">while</span> <span class="va">IFS</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;&quot;</span> <span class="bu">read</span> <span class="at">-r</span> <span class="va">line</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">do</span> <span class="va">array</span><span class="op">+=</span><span class="va">(</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$line</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>If it outputs a line with multiple words (separated by spaces, other
delimiters can be chosen with IFS), each of which should be an
element:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># For bash, uses temporary files</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">IFS</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot; &quot;</span> <span class="bu">read</span> <span class="at">-r</span> <span class="at">-a</span> <span class="va">array</span> <span class="op">&lt;&lt;&lt;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="ex">mycommand</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># For bash 4.2+ with the lastpipe option enabled (may require disabling monitor mode)</span></span>
<span id="cb3-5"><a href="#cb3-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">array</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">()</span></span>
<span id="cb3-6"><a href="#cb3-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">mycommand</span> <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="va">IFS</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot; &quot;</span> <span class="bu">read</span> <span class="at">-r</span> <span class="at">-a</span> <span class="va">array</span></span>
<span id="cb3-7"><a href="#cb3-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb3-8"><a href="#cb3-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># For ksh</span></span>
<span id="cb3-9"><a href="#cb3-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">IFS</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot; &quot;</span> <span class="bu">read</span> <span class="at">-r</span> <span class="at">-A</span> <span class="va">array</span> <span class="op">&lt;&lt;&lt;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="ex">mycommand</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>If the output should be a single element:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">array</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="ex">mycommand</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="va">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You are doing unquoted command expansion in an array. This will
invoke the shell's sloppy word splitting and glob expansion.</p>
<p>Instead, prefer explicitly splitting (or not splitting):</p>
<ul>
<li>If you want to split the output into lines or words, use
<code>mapfile</code>, <code>read -ra</code> and/or <code>while</code>
loops as appropriate.</li>
<li>If the command output should become a single array element, quote
it.</li>
</ul>
<p>This prevents the shell from doing unwanted splitting and glob
expansion, and therefore avoiding problems with output containing spaces
or special characters.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you have already taken care (through setting IFS and
<code>set -f</code>) to have word splitting work the way you intend, you
can ignore this warning.</p>
<p>Another exception is the wish for error handling:
<code>array=( $(mycommand) ) || die-with-error</code> works the way it
looks while a similar <code>mapfile</code> construct like
<code>mapfile -t array &lt; &lt;(mycommand)</code> <strong>doesn't
fail</strong> and you will have to write more code for error
handling.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2208 – Use `[[ ]]` or quote arguments to `-v` to avoid glob expansion.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2208 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2208">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="use---or-quote-arguments-to--v-to-avoid-glob-expansion">Use
<code>[[ ]]</code> or quote arguments to <code>-v</code> to avoid glob
expansion.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-v</span> foo<span class="pp">[</span><span class="ss">0</span><span class="pp">]</span> <span class="bu">]</span> </span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-v</span> <span class="st">&#39;foo[0]&#39;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>With <code>[</code>, arguments will undergo glob expansion. If a file
<code>foo0</code> exists when the problematic code is run, it will check
for the variable <code>foo0</code> instead of the array entry
<code>foo[0]</code>. If there additionally exists a <code>foo1</code>,
it will simply fail with an error.</p>
<p>Use <code>[[ ]]</code> or quote the argument.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2209 – Use `var=$(command)` to assign output (or quote to assign string).</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2209 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2209">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="use-varcommand-to-assign-output-or-quote-to-assign-string">Use
<code>var=$(command)</code> to assign output (or quote to assign
string).</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">user</span><span class="op">=</span>whoami         <span class="co"># Want to run whoami and assign output</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">PAGER</span><span class="op">=</span>cat <span class="fu">git</span> log   <span class="co"># Want to assign the string &quot;cat&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">user</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">whoami</span><span class="va">)</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">PAGER</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;cat&quot;</span> <span class="fu">git</span> log</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Putting <code>var=</code> in front of a command will not assign its
output. Use <code>var=$(my command here)</code> to execute the command
and capture its output.</p>
<p>If you do want to assign a literal string, use quotes to make this
clear to shellcheck and humans alike.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
<p>Quoting a single command (as in <code>PAGER="cat"</code> above)
doesn't change how the script works. It's purely to show shellcheck (and
humans) that a literal assignment of a command name is intentional.</p>
<p>This warning triggers generally when a variable is assigned an
unquoted command name (from a list of hard coded names). See related
warning <a href="SC2037">SC2037</a> which detects the same kind of error
through the patterns <code>var=value -flag</code> and
<code>var=value *glob*</code>.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://mywiki.wooledge.org/BashFAQ/002">BashFaq: How can I
store the return value and/or output of a command in a
variable?</a></li>
<li><a
href="https://stackoverflow.com/questions/4651437/how-to-set-a-variable-to-the-output-from-a-command-in-bash">StackOverflow:
How to set a variable to the output from a command in Bash</a></li>
</ul>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2210 – This is a file redirection. Was it supposed to be a comparison or fd operation?</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2210 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2210">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="this-is-a-file-redirection-was-it-supposed-to-be-a-comparison-or-fd-operation">This
is a file redirection. Was it supposed to be a comparison or fd
operation?</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="ex">x</span> <span class="op">&gt;</span> 5<span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">then</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;true&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">foo</span> <span class="op">&gt;</span> /dev/null <span class="dv">2</span><span class="op">&gt;</span>1</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="kw">((</span> <span class="va">x</span> <span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="dv">5</span> <span class="kw">));</span> <span class="cf">then</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;true&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">foo</span> <span class="op">&gt;</span> /dev/null <span class="dv">2</span><span class="op">&gt;&amp;</span><span class="dv">1</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You are redirecting to or from a filename that is an integer. For
example, <code>ls &gt; file</code> where <code>file</code> happens to be
<code>3</code>.</p>
<p>This is not likely to be intentional. The most common causes are:</p>
<ol>
<li>Trying to compare two numbers, as in <code>x &gt; 5</code>. This
should instead be <code>[ "$x" -gt 5 ]</code> or
<code>(( x &gt; 5 ))</code>.</li>
<li>Trying similarly to compare command output, as in
<code>grep -c foo file &gt; 100</code> instead of
<code>[ "$(grep -c foo file)" -gt 100 ]</code></li>
<li>Malformed FD operations, such as writing <code>1&gt;2</code> instead
of <code>1&gt;&amp;2</code>.</li>
</ol>
<p>If you do want to create a file named <code>4</code>, you can quote
it to silence shellcheck and make it more clear to humans that it's not
supposed to be taken numerically.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you use the <code>&amp;&gt;</code> form of redirection, as in
<code>foo &gt; /dev/null 2&amp;&gt;1</code>, it will trigger this
warning. You can safely ignore this warning if that is what triggered
it, or change your redirection operator to the semantically preferable
<code>&gt;&amp;</code>.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2211 – This is a glob used as a command name. Was it supposed to be in `${..}`, array, or is it missing quoting?</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2211 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2211">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="this-is-a-glob-used-as-a-command-name-was-it-supposed-to-be-in--array-or-is-it-missing-quoting">This
is a glob used as a command name. Was it supposed to be in
<code>${..}</code>, array, or is it missing quoting?</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> f <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="va">$(</span><span class="ex">*.png</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">do</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$f</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">done</span>   <span class="co"># Trying to loop over a glob</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">array</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="ex">*.txt</span><span class="va">)</span>                          <span class="co"># Trying to assign an array</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$(array</span><span class="op">[</span><span class="dv">1</span><span class="op">]</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st">&quot;</span>                      <span class="co"># Trying to expand an array</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> f <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="pp">*</span>.png<span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">do</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$f</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">done</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">array</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span><span class="pp">*</span>.txt<span class="va">)</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${array</span><span class="op">[</span><span class="dv">1</span><span class="op">]</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You are using a glob as a command name. This is usually a mistake
caused by one of the following:</p>
<ul>
<li>Trying to use <code>`*foo*`</code> or <code>$(*foo*)</code> to
expand a glob.</li>
<li>Using <code>var=$(*.txt)</code> instead of <code>var=(*.txt)</code>
to assign an array.</li>
<li>Using <code>$(..)</code> instead of <code>${..}</code> when
expanding an array element.</li>
<li>Running a program with a name or directory that contains glob
characters without escaping them.</li>
</ul>
<p>Look up and double check the syntax of what you're trying to do.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None. If you want to specify a command name via glob, e.g. to not
hard code version in <code>./myprogram-*/foo</code>, expand to array or
parameters first to allow handling the cases of 0 or 2+ matches.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2212 – Use `false` instead of empty `[`/`[[` conditionals.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2212 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2212">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="use-false-instead-of-empty--conditionals">Use <code>false</code>
instead of empty <code>[</code>/<code>[[</code> conditionals.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Temporarily disabled&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="fu">false</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Temporarily disabled&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p><code>[ ]</code> is a somewhat obscure way of expressing falsehood,
and the behavior is likely intended to allow the incorrectly quoted
command <code>[ $var ]</code> to still work when the variable is
unset.</p>
<p>POSIX has a more descriptive command <code>false</code> for this.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None. This is a stylistic suggestion, and has no effect on how the
script works.</p>
    <hr />

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2213 – getopts specified `-n`, but it's not handled by this `case`.</title>

    <h2 id="getopts-specified--n-but-its-not-handled-by-this-case">getopts
specified <code>-n</code>, but it's not handled by this

<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>

<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">while</span> <span class="bu">getopts</span> <span class="st">&quot;vrn&quot;</span> <span class="va">n</span></span>

<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="ss">v</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Verbose&quot;</span> <span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="ss">r</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Recursive&quot;</span> <span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="ss">n</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Dry-run&quot;</span> <span class="cf">;;</span>    <span class="co"># -n handled here</span></span>
<span id="cb2-7"><a href="#cb2-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="dt">\?</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="ex">usage</span><span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-8"><a href="#cb2-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">esac</span></span>
<span id="cb2-9"><a href="#cb2-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You have a <code>while getopts</code> loop where the corresponding
<code>case</code> statement fails to handle one of the flags.</p>
<p>Either add a case to handle the flag, or remove it from the
<code>getopts</code> option string.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck may not correctly recognize less canonical uses of
<code>while getopts ..; do case ..;</code>, such as when modifying the
variable before using it:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">while</span> <span class="bu">getopts</span> <span class="st">&quot;rf-:&quot;</span> <span class="va">OPT</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$OPT</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;-&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">then</span>   <span class="co"># long option: reformulate OPT and OPTARG</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="va">OPT</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${OPTARG</span><span class="op">%%</span>=<span class="pp">*</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span>       <span class="co"># extract long option name</span></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="va">OPTARG</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${OPTARG</span><span class="op">#</span><span class="va">$OPT}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span>   <span class="co"># extract long option argument (may be empty)</span></span>
<span id="cb3-5"><a href="#cb3-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="va">OPTARG</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${OPTARG</span><span class="op">#</span>=<span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span>      <span class="co"># if long option argument, remove assigning `=`</span></span>
<span id="cb3-6"><a href="#cb3-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">fi</span></span>
<span id="cb3-7"><a href="#cb3-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb3-8"><a href="#cb3-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">case</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$OPT</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="kw">in</span></span>
<span id="cb3-9"><a href="#cb3-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="ss">r</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="ex">...</span> <span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-10"><a href="#cb3-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="ss">f</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="ex">...</span> <span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-11"><a href="#cb3-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="ss">my-long-option</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="ex">...</span> <span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-12"><a href="#cb3-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">esac</span></span>
<span id="cb3-13"><a href="#cb3-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>In such cases you can do one of:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="Ignore">Ignore</a> the warning.</li>
<li>Use the external tool <code>getopt</code> (no "s") which supports
long options natively.</li>
<li>Rewrite to not modify the variable first, in this case by instead
doing it in a <code>-)</code> branch.</li>
</ul>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span></span>

<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">while</span> <span class="bu">getopts</span> <span class="st">&quot;vrn&quot;</span> <span class="va">n</span>    <span class="co"># &#39;n&#39; added here</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">case</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$n</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="kw">in</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="ss">v</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Verbose&quot;</span> <span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="ss">r</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Recursive&quot;</span> <span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="ss">n</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Dry-run&quot;</span> <span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-7"><a href="#cb2-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="pp">*</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="ex">usage</span><span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-8"><a href="#cb2-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">esac</span></span>
<span id="cb2-9"><a href="#cb2-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You have a <code>case</code> statement in a
<code>while getopts</code> loop that matches a flag that hasn't been
provided in the <code>getopts</code> option string.</p>
<p>Either add the flag to the options list, or delete the case
statement.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2215 – This flag is used as a command name. Bad line break or missing `[ .. ]`?</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2215 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2215">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="this-flag-is-used-as-a-command-name-bad-line-break-or-missing---">This
flag is used as a command name. Bad line break or missing
<code>[ .. ]</code>?</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="ex">-e</span> .bashrc</span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;.bashrc already exists&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">find</span> . <span class="at">-name</span> <span class="st">&#39;*.mkv&#39;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>       <span class="ex">-exec</span> mplayer {} <span class="dt">\;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-e</span> .bashrc <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;.bashrc already exists&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">find</span> . <span class="at">-name</span> <span class="st">&#39;*.mkv&#39;</span> <span class="dt">\</span></span>
<span id="cb4-2"><a href="#cb4-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>       <span class="at">-exec</span> mplayer {} <span class="dt">\;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You are using a name that starts with a dash as a command name. This
is almost always a bug.</p>
<p>There are two typical ways in which this happens:</p>
<ul>
<li>Missing <code>[ .. ]</code> or <code>[[ .. ]]</code> around a test
expression, like in the first example example.</li>
<li>An invalid line break that splits a command in two, like in the
second example.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you actually have a command that starts with a dash—which you
should really reconsider—you can quote the name (or at least the leading
dash). This makes no difference to the shell, but makes it clear to
ShellCheck and humans that this is not intended as a flag.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
