    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2216 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2216">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="piping-to-rm-a-command-that-doesnt-read-stdin-wrong-command-or-missing-xargs">Piping
to <code>rm</code>, a command that doesn't read stdin. Wrong command or
missing <code>xargs</code>?</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">ls</span> <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="bu">echo</span>                      <span class="co"># Want to print result</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">cat</span> files <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="fu">rm</span>                 <span class="co"># Want to delete items from a file</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">find</span> . <span class="at">-type</span> f <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="fu">cp</span> dir        <span class="co"># Want to process &#39;find&#39; output</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">rm</span> file <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="fu">true</span>                 <span class="co"># Want to ignore errors</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">ls</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">cat</span> files <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="cf">while</span> <span class="va">IFS</span><span class="op">=</span> <span class="bu">read</span> <span class="at">-r</span> <span class="va">file</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">do</span> <span class="fu">rm</span> <span class="at">--</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$file</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">done</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">find</span> . <span class="at">-type</span> f <span class="at">-exec</span> cp {} dir <span class="dt">\;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">rm</span> file <span class="kw">||</span> <span class="fu">true</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You are piping to one of several commands that don't read from
stdin.</p>
<p>This may happen when:</p>
<ul>
<li>Confusing one command for another, e.g. using <code>echo</code>
where <code>cat</code> was intended.</li>
<li>Incorrectly refactoring, leaving a <code>|</code> on the previous
line.</li>
<li>Missing <code>xargs</code>, because stdin should be passed as
positional parameters instead (use <code>xargs -0</code> if at all
possible).</li>
<li>Intending to use <code>||</code> instead of <code>|</code></li>
</ul>
<p>Check your logic, and rewrite the command so data is passed
correctly.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you've overridden a command to return output, you can either
rename it to make this obvious, or <a href="ignore">ignore</a> this
message.</p>
    <hr />

  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2217 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2217">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="redirecting-to-echo-a-command-that-doesnt-read-stdin-bad-quoting-or-missing-xargs">Redirecting
to <code>echo</code>, a command that doesn't read stdin. Bad quoting or
missing <code>xargs</code>?</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="op">&lt;&lt; eof</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">  Hello World</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">eof</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">cat</span> <span class="op">&lt;&lt; eof</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">  Hello World</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">eof</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You are redirecting to one of several commands that don't read from
stdin.</p>
<p>This may happen when:</p>
<ul>
<li>Confusing one command for another, e.g. using <code>echo</code>
where <code>cat</code> was intended.</li>
<li>Incorrectly quoting angle brackets, e.g. using
<code>echo &lt;p&gt;Hello</code> which tries to read from a file
<code>p</code>.</li>
<li>Missing <code>xargs</code>, e.g. <code>mv -t dir &lt; files</code>
instead of <code>xargs mv -t dir &lt; files</code> (or more safely,
<code>tr '\n' '\0' &lt; files | xargs -0 mv -t dir</code>), because
stdin should be passed as parameters.</li>
</ul>
<p>Check your logic, and rewrite the command so data is passed
correctly.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you've overridden a command to return output, you can either
rename it to make this obvious, or <a href="ignore">ignore</a> this
message.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2218 – This function is only defined later. Move the definition up.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2218 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2218">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="this-function-is-only-defined-later-move-the-definition-up">This
function is only defined later. Move the definition up.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/sh</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">myfunction</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">myfunction()</span> <span class="kw">{</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-6"><a href="#cb1-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/sh</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">myfunction()</span> <span class="kw">{</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">myfunction</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You are calling a function that you are defining later in the file.
The function definition must come first.</p>
<p>Function definitions are much like variable assignments, and define a
name at the point the definition is "executed". This is why they must
happen before their first use.</p>
<p>This is especially apparent when defining functions
conditionally:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">case</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">uname</span> <span class="at">-s</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="kw">in</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="ss">Linux</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="fu">hi()</span> <span class="kw">{</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello from Linux&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="kw">}</span> <span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="ss">Darwin</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="fu">hi()</span> <span class="kw">{</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello from macOS&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="kw">}</span> <span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="pp">*</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="fu">hi()</span> <span class="kw">{</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello from something else&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="kw">}</span> <span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-5"><a href="#cb3-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">esac</span></span>
<span id="cb3-6"><a href="#cb3-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb3-7"><a href="#cb3-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">hi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2219 – Instead of `let expr`, prefer `(( expr ))` .</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2219 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2219">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="instead-of-let-expr-prefer--expr--">Instead of
<code>let expr</code>, prefer <code>(( expr ))</code> .</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">let</span> <span class="va">a</span><span class="op">++</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">((</span> <span class="va">a</span><span class="op">++</span> <span class="kw">))</span> <span class="kw">||</span> <span class="fu">true</span></span></code></pre></div>
<blockquote>
<p>Note, <code>|| true</code> bits ignore error status code when
incrementing from <code>0</code> to <code>1</code></p>
</blockquote>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>The <code>(( .. ))</code> arithmetic compound command evaluates
expressions in the same way as <code>let</code>, except it's not subject
to glob expansion and therefore requires no additional quoting or
escaping.</p>
<p>This warning only triggers in Bash/Ksh scripts. In Sh/Dash, neither
<code>let</code> nor <code>(( .. ))</code> are defined, but can be
simulated with <code>[ $(( expr )) -ne 0 ]</code> to retain exit code,
or <code>: $(( expr ))</code> to ignore it. For portability, the
<code>$(( expr ))</code> syntax is defined in POSIX standard.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
<h3 id="more-information">More information</h3>
<ul>
<li>Bash Hacker's Wiki: <a
href="https://web.archive.org/web/20230224010517/http://wiki.bash-hackers.org/commands/builtin/let">The
let builtin command</a></li>
</ul>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2220 – Invalid flags are not handled. Add a `*)` case.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2220 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2220">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="invalid-flags-are-not-handled-add-a--case">Invalid flags are not
handled. Add a <code>*)</code> case.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/sh</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">while</span> <span class="bu">getopts</span> <span class="st">&quot;vr&quot;</span> <span class="va">f</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">case</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$f</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="kw">in</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="ss">v</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;verbose&quot;</span> <span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-6"><a href="#cb1-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="ss">r</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;recursive&quot;</span> <span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-7"><a href="#cb1-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">esac</span></span>
<span id="cb1-8"><a href="#cb1-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/sh</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">while</span> <span class="bu">getopts</span> <span class="st">&quot;vr&quot;</span> <span class="va">f</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">case</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$f</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="kw">in</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="ss">v</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;verbose&quot;</span> <span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="ss">r</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;recursive&quot;</span> <span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-7"><a href="#cb2-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="pp">*</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;usage: </span><span class="va">$0</span><span class="st"> [-v] [-r]&quot;</span> <span class="op">&gt;&amp;</span><span class="dv">2</span></span>
<span id="cb2-8"><a href="#cb2-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>       <span class="bu">exit</span> 1 <span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-9"><a href="#cb2-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">esac</span></span>
<span id="cb2-10"><a href="#cb2-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>The <code>case</code> statement handling <code>getopts</code>
arguments does not have a default branch to handle unknown flags.</p>
<p>When a flag is not recognized, such as if passing <code>-Z</code> to
the example code, <code>getopts</code> will set the variable to a
literal question mark <code>?</code>. This should be handled along with
all the valid flags, usually by printing a usage message and exiting
with failure.</p>
<p>Using a <code>\?)</code> or <code>?)</code> case will also match
invalid flags, but<code>*)</code> would additionally match things like
the empty string if the variable name was misspelled.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If your script's logic handles unrecognized flags in another way,
e.g. after the <code>case</code> statement, you can ignore this
warning.</p>
    <hr />

  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2221 – This pattern always overrides a later one.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2221 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2221">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="this-pattern-always-overrides-a-later-one">This pattern always
overrides a later one.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">case</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$1</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="kw">in</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="ss">-</span><span class="pp">?</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Usage: </span><span class="va">$0</span><span class="st"> [-n]&quot;</span><span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="ss">-n</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span><span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>   <span class="pp">*</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">exit</span> 1<span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">esac</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">case</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$1</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="kw">in</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="ss">-</span><span class="dt">\?</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Usage: </span><span class="va">$0</span><span class="st"> [-n]&quot;</span><span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># &#39;-?&#39;) echo &quot;Usage: $0 [-n]&quot;;;  # Also valid</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="ss">-n</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span><span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>   <span class="pp">*</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="bu">exit</span> 1<span class="cf">;;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">esac</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You have specified multiple patterns in a <code>case</code>
statement, where one will always override the other. The pattern being
overridden is indicated with a <a href="SC2222">SC2222</a> warning.</p>
<p>In the example, <code>-?</code> actually matches a dash followed by
any character, such as <code>-n</code>. This means that the later
<code>-n</code> branch will never trigger. In this case, the correct
solution is to escape the <code>-\?</code> so that it doesn't match
<code>-n</code>.</p>
<p>Another common reason for this is accidentally duplicating a branch.
In this case, fix or delete the duplicate branch.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None. One could argue that having
<code>-*|--*) echo "Invalid flag";</code> is a readability issue, even
though the second pattern follows from the first. In this case, you can
either rearrange the pattern from most to least specific, i.e.
<code>--*|-*)</code> or ignore the error.</p>
<p>When ignoring this error, remember that ShellCheck directives have to
go in front of the <code>case</code> statement, and not in front of the
branch:</p>
<pre><code># shellcheck disable=SC2221,SC2222
case &quot;$1&quot; in
  -n) ...;;
  # no directive here
  -*|--*) echo &quot;Unknown flag&quot; ;;
esac</code></pre>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2223 – This default assignment may cause DoS due to globbing. Quote it.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2223 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2223">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="this-default-assignment-may-cause-dos-due-to-globbing-quote-it">This
default assignment may cause DoS due to globbing. Quote it.</h2>
<h3 id="optional---quote-safe-variables">Optional -
<code>quote-safe-variables</code></h3>
<p>This is an <a href="optional">optional</a> rule, which means that it
has a special "long name" and is not enabled by default. See the <a
href="optional">optional</a> page for more details. In short, you have
to enable it with the long name instead of the "SC" code like you would
with a normal rule:</p>
<h4 id="shellcheckrc"><code>.shellcheckrc</code></h4>
<pre><code>enable=quote-safe-variables # SC2223</code></pre>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">:</span> <span class="va">${COLUMNS</span><span class="op">:=</span>80<span class="va">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">:</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${COLUMNS</span><span class="op">:=</span>80<span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>This statement is an idiomatic way of assigning a default value to an
environment variable. However, even though it's passed to <code>:</code>
which ignores arguments, it's better to quote it.</p>
<p>If <code>COLUMNS='/*/*/*/*/*/*'</code>, the unquoted, problematic
code may spend 30+ minutes trashing the disk as it unnecessarily tries
to glob expand the value.</p>
<p>The correct code uses double quotes to avoid glob expansion, and
therefore does not have this problem.</p>
<p>When quoting, make sure to update any inner quotes:</p>
<pre><code>: ${var:=&#39;foo&#39;}    # Assigns foo without quotes
: &quot;${var:=&#39;foo&#39;}&quot;  # Assigns &#39;foo&#39; with quotes</code></pre>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None, though this issue is largely theoretical.</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2224 – This `mv` has no destination. Check the arguments.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2224 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2224">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="this-mv-has-no-destination-check-the-arguments">This
<code>mv</code> has no destination. Check the arguments.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">mv</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$file</span><span class="st"> </span><span class="va">$dir</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">mv</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$file</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$dir</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found an <code>mv</code> command with a single parameter.
This may be because the source and destination was accidentally merged
into a single argument, or because the line was broken in an invalid
way.</p>
<p>Fix the <code>mv</code> statement by correctly specifying both source
and destination.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>

    <h2 id="this-cp-has-no-destination-check-the-arguments">This
<code>cp</code> has no destination. Check the arguments.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">cp</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$file</span><span class="st"> </span><span class="va">$dir</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">cp</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$file</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$dir</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>

<p>ShellCheck found a <code>cp</code> command with a single parameter.
This may be because the source and destination was accidentally merged
into a single argument, or because the line was broken in an invalid
way.</p>
<p>Fix the <code>cp</code> statement by correctly specifying both source
and destination.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2226 – This `ln` has no destination. Check the arguments, or specify `.` explicitly.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2226 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2226">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="this-ln-has-no-destination-check-the-arguments-or-specify--explicitly">This
<code>ln</code> has no destination. Check the arguments, or specify
<code>.</code> explicitly.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">ln</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$file</span><span class="st"> </span><span class="va">$dir</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">ln</span> /foo/bar/baz</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">ln</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$file</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$dir</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">ln</span> /foo/bar/baz .</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a <code>ln</code> command with a single parameter.
This may be because the source and destination was accidentally merged
into a single argument, because the line was broken in an invalid way,
or because you're using a non-standard invocation of <code>ln</code>
that defaults to linking the argument into the current directory.</p>
<p>If you wanted to specify both source and destination, fix the
<code>ln</code> statement.</p>
<p>If you wanted to link a file into the current directory, prefer using
the more explicit and POSIX standard invocation
<code>ln /your/file .</code></p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2227 – Redirection applies to the find command itself. Rewrite to work per action (or move to end).</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2227 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2227">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="redirection-applies-to-the-find-command-itself-rewrite-to-work-per-action-or-move-to-end">Redirection
applies to the find command itself. Rewrite to work per action (or move
to end).</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">find</span> . <span class="at">-name</span> <span class="st">&#39;*.ppm&#39;</span> <span class="at">-exec</span> pnmtopng {} <span class="op">&gt;</span> {}.png <span class="dt">\;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">find</span> . <span class="at">-name</span> <span class="st">&#39;*.ppm&#39;</span> <span class="at">-exec</span> sh <span class="at">-c</span> <span class="st">&#39;pnmtopng &quot;$1&quot; &gt; &quot;$1.png&quot;&#39;</span> _ {} <span class="dt">\;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck detected a <code>find</code> command with a redirection in
the middle.</p>
<p>This redirection may have been intended to apply only to a specific
action like <code>-exec</code> or <code>-print</code>, but it does in
fact apply to the entire <code>find</code> command:</p>
<pre><code># This command
find . -name &#39;*.ppm&#39; -exec pnmtopng {} &gt; {}.png \;

# Is the same as this
{
   find . -name &#39;*.ppm&#39; -exec pnmtopng {} \;
} &gt; {}.png </code></pre>
<p>To perform a redirection per action, rewrite it with e.g.
<code>-exec sh -c '...' _ {} \;</code></p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If the redirection is something like <code>&gt; /dev/null</code>
where you don't mind it applying to the whole <code>find</code> and not
individual results, you can move the redirection to the end of command
to make it clear to ShellCheck (and humans) that it's not meant per
command:</p>
<pre><code>find . -exec foo {} &gt; /dev/null \;     # Ambiguous syntax. Is it per -exec or not?
find . -exec foo {} \;  &gt; /dev/null    # Identical command with clear intent.</code></pre>
<p>There is no difference in behavior between the two.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2229 – This does not read `foo`. Remove `$`/`${}` for that, or use `${var?}` to quiet.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2229 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2229">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="this-does-not-read-foo-remove--for-that-or-use-var-to-quiet">This
does not read <code>foo</code>. Remove <code>$</code>/<code>${}</code>
for that, or use <code>${var?}</code> to quiet.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">read</span> <span class="va">$foo</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">read</span> <span class="va">foo</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p><code>read</code> takes a variable name, but ShellCheck has noticed
that you give it an expanded variable instead. This will populate
whatever the variable expands to instead of the variable itself. For
example:</p>
<pre><code>foo=bar
read $foo   # Reads data into &#39;bar&#39;, not into &#39;foo&#39;
read foo    # Reads data into &#39;foo&#39;</code></pre>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If this is intentional and you do want to read a variable through an
indirect reference, you can silence this warning with a directive:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># shellcheck disable=SC2229</span></span>
<span id="cb4-2"><a href="#cb4-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">read</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$foo</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Or take advantage of the fact that ShellCheck only warns when no
parameter expansion modifiers are applied:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb5"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb5-1"><a href="#cb5-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">read</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${foo}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span>    <span class="co"># ShellCheck warns</span></span>
<span id="cb5-2"><a href="#cb5-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">read</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${foo</span><span class="op">?</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span>   <span class="co"># No warning</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p><code>${foo?}</code> fails when <code>foo</code> is unset, which is
fine since <code>read</code> would have failed too. The main side effect
is an improved runtime error message in that case.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://mywiki.wooledge.org/BashPitfalls#pf12">Bash
Pitfalls #12</a>: <code>read $foo</code></li>
</ul>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2230 – `which` is non-standard. Use builtin `command -v` instead.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2230 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2230">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="which-is-non-standard-use-builtin-command--v-instead"><code>which</code>
is non-standard. Use builtin <code>command -v</code> instead.</h2>
<h3 id="optional---deprecate-which">Optional -
<code>deprecate-which</code></h3>
<p>This is an <a href="optional">optional</a> rule, which means that it
has a special "long name" and is not enabled by default. See the <a
href="optional">optional</a> page for more details. In short, you have
to enable it with the long name instead of the "SC" code like you would
with a normal rule:</p>
<h4 id="shellcheckrc"><code>.shellcheckrc</code></h4>
<pre><code>enable=deprecate-which # SC2230</code></pre>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">which</span> grep</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># For the path of a single, unaliased, external command,</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># or to check whether this will just &quot;run&quot; in this shell:</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">command</span> <span class="at">-v</span> grep</span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># To check whether commands exist, without obtaining a reusable path:</span></span>
<span id="cb3-5"><a href="#cb3-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">hash</span> grep</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p><code>which</code> is a non-standard, external tool that locates an
executable in PATH. <code>command -v</code> is a POSIX standard builtin,
which uses the same lookup mechanism that the shell itself would.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>This check is opt-in only in 0.7.1+, and you may choose to <a
href="ignore">ignore</a> it in earlier versions. <code>which</code> is
very common, and some prefer its executable-or-nothing behavior over
<code>command -v</code>'s handling of builtins, functions and
aliases.</p>
<h3 id="caveats">Caveats:</h3>
<h4
id="command--v-does-not-check-all-parameters"><code>command -v</code>
does not check ALL parameters</h4>
<p><code>command -v</code> succeeds (with exit code 0) if <em>any</em>
command exists:</p>
<pre><code># grep is in /usr/bin/grep
# foobar is not in path
#
$ command -v -- grep foobar; echo $?
0</code></pre>
<p>In the above example, it should have failed and exited with 1 unless
<em>all</em> commands exist, if it were to be a replacement for
<code>which</code>. Other problems associated with <code>command</code>
include its inclusion of builtins, aliases, and functions.</p>
<p>An alternative is:</p>
<pre><code>$ hash &lt;file1&gt; &lt;file2&gt;</code></pre>
<p>Which observes the standard behaviour of failures.</p>
<p>To obtain a path, <code>type -p</code> can be used instead. Like
<code>command -v</code>, it has a similarly quirky behavior with
builtins, aliases, and functions, although this is arguably milder since
it would print nothing for these cases. The failure condition is similar
to <code>hash</code>.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li><code>shellcheck</code> issue: <a
href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/issues/1162">#1162 command
-v is not a direct replacement for which</a> (Discussion)</li>
<li><a href="https://stackoverflow.com/a/677212/1899640">Check if a
program exists from a Bash script</a> on StackOverflow.</li>
</ul>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2231 – Quote expansions in this `for` loop glob to prevent word splitting, e.g. `"${dir}"/*.txt`.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2231 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2231">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="quote-expansions-in-this-for-loop-glob-to-prevent-word-splitting-eg-dirtxt">Quote
expansions in this <code>for</code> loop glob to prevent word splitting,
e.g. <code>"${dir}"/*.txt</code>.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> file <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="va">${dir}</span>/<span class="pp">*</span>.txt</span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Found </span><span class="va">${file}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> file <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${dir}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span>/<span class="pp">*</span>.txt</span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Found </span><span class="va">${file}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>When iterating over globs containing expansions, you can still quote
all expansions in the path to better handle whitespace and special
characters.</p>
<p>Just make sure glob characters are outside quotes.
<code>"${dir}/*.txt"</code> will not glob expand, but
<code>"${dir}"/*.txt</code> or <code>"${dir}"/*."${ext}"</code>
will.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>Exceptions similar to <a href="SC2086">SC2086</a> apply. If the
variable is expected to contain globs, such as if
<code>dir="tmp/**"</code> in the example, you can ignore this
message.</p>

<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2232 – Can't use `sudo` with builtins like `cd`. Did you want `sudo sh -c ..` instead?</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2232 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2232">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="cant-use-sudo-with-builtins-like-cd-did-you-want-sudo-sh--c--instead">Can't
use <code>sudo</code> with builtins like <code>cd</code>. Did you want
<code>sudo sh -c ..</code> instead?</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">sudo</span> cd /root</span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">pwd</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">sudo</span> sh <span class="at">-c</span> <span class="st">&#39;cd /root &amp;&amp; pwd&#39;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Due to the Unix process model, <code>sudo</code> can only change the
privileges of a new, external process. It can not grant privileges to a
currently running process.</p>
<p>This means that shell builtins -- commands that are interpreted by
the current shell rather than through program invocation -- cannot be
run with <code>sudo</code>. This includes <code>cd</code>,
<code>source</code>, <code>read</code>, and others.</p>
<p>Instead you can run a shell with <code>sudo</code>, and have that
shell run the builtins you want. Just be aware that what happens in that
shell stays in that shell:</p>
<pre><code>sudo sh -c &#39;cd /root &amp;&amp; pwd&#39;  # This shows /root
pwd                           # This shows the original directory</code></pre>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2233 – Remove superfluous `(..)` around condition to avoid subshell overhead.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2233 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2233">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="remove-superfluous--around-condition-to-avoid-subshell-overhead">Remove
superfluous <code>(..)</code> around condition to avoid subshell
overhead.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="kw">(</span><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$x</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">-gt</span> 0 <span class="bu">]</span><span class="kw">)</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span> <span class="fu">true</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$x</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">-gt</span> 0 <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span> <span class="fu">true</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>The shell syntax is <code>if cmd</code>, <code>elif cmd</code>,
<code>while cmd</code> and <code>until cmd</code> without any
parentheses. Instead, parentheses are an independent construct used to
create subshells.</p>
<p>ShellCheck has noticed that you're wrapping <code>(..)</code> around
one or more test commands. This is unnecessary, and the resulting fork
adds quite a lot of overhead:</p>
<pre class="console"><code>$ i=0; time while ( [ &quot;$i&quot; -lt 10000 ] ); do i=$((i+1)); done
real    0m6.998s
user    0m3.453s
sys     0m3.464s

$ i=0; time while [ &quot;$i&quot; -lt 10000 ]; do i=$((i+1)); done
real    0m0.055s
user    0m0.054s
sys     0m0.001s</code></pre>
<p>Just delete the surrounding <code>(..)</code> since they serve no
purpose and only slows the script down.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>This issue only affects performance, not correctness, so it can be
safely <a href="ignore">ignore</a>d.</p>
<p>If you are considering doing it to stylistically match C-like
languages, please note that this is not conventional and that you'd
probably recommend someone use <code>if (1 == 2)</code> over
<code>if (system("[ 1 = 2 ]"))</code> in C no matter which language
they're used to.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <hr />
    <h2
id="remove-superfluous--around-test-command-to-avoid-subshell-overhead">Remove
superfluous <code>(..)</code> around test command to avoid subshell
overhead.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">(</span><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$x</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">-gt</span> 0 <span class="bu">]</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="ex">foo</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$x</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">-gt</span> 0 <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="ex">foo</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You are wrapping a single test command in <code>(..)</code>, creating
an unnecessary subshell. This serves no purpose, but is significantly
slower:</p>
<pre class="console"><code>$ i=0; time while ( [ &quot;$i&quot; -lt 10000 ] ); do i=$((i+1)); done
real    0m6.998s
user    0m3.453s
sys     0m3.464s

$ i=0; time while [ &quot;$i&quot; -lt 10000 ]; do i=$((i+1)); done
real    0m0.055s
user    0m0.054s
sys     0m0.001s</code></pre>
<p>Just delete the surrounding <code>(..)</code> since they serve no
purpose and only slows the script down.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>This issue only affects performance, not correctness, and can be <a
href="ignore">ignore</a>d for stylistic reasons.</p>

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2235 – Use `{ ..; }` instead of `(..)` to avoid subshell overhead.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2235 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2235">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="use----instead-of--to-avoid-subshell-overhead">Use
<code>{ ..; }</code> instead of <code>(..)</code> to avoid subshell
overhead.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">(</span><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$x</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="kw">||</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$y</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span><span class="kw">)</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$z</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">{</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$x</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="kw">||</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$y</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="kw">}</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$z</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You appear to be using <code>(..)</code> to group test commands. This
creates a subshell, making it unnecessarily slow. Avoid this by using
<code>{ ..; }</code> to group.</p>
<p>Be careful to note that unlike <code>(..)</code>, this requires both
a space after the <code>{</code> and a semicolon before the
<code>}</code>.</p>
<p>For example, <code>(cmd)</code>, <code>(cmd;)</code> and
<code>( cmd )</code> are all valid, but <code>{cmd}</code>,
<code>{cmd;}</code> and <code>{ cmd }</code> are all syntax errors
because they lack either or both of the spaces and semicolon. The
correct form is <code>{ cmd; }</code></p>
<p>Here's a small benchmark showing that the subshell version is more
than 100x slower:</p>
<pre class="console"><code>$ i=0; time for i in {1..10000}; do ([ &quot;$x&quot; ] || [ &quot;$y&quot; ]) &amp;&amp; [ &quot;$z&quot; ]; done
real    0m7.122s
user    0m4.204s
sys     0m2.825s

$ i=0; time for i in {1..10000}; do { [ &quot;$x&quot; ] || [ &quot;$y&quot; ]; } &amp;&amp; [ &quot;$z&quot; ]; done
real    0m0.055s
user    0m0.055s
sys     0m0.000s</code></pre>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>

<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2236 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2236">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="use--n-instead-of---z">Use <code>-n</code> instead of
<code>! -z</code>.</h2>
<p>(or "Use <code>-z</code> instead of <code>! -n</code>")</p>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">!</span> <span class="ot">-n</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$JAVA_HOME</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">then</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;JAVA_HOME not specified&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">fi</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">!</span> <span class="ot">-z</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$STY</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span><span class="kw">;</span>       <span class="cf">then</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;You are already running screen&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-z</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$JAVA_HOME</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">then</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;JAVA_HOME not specified&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">fi</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-n</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$STY</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span><span class="kw">;</span>       <span class="cf">then</span> <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;You are already running screen&quot;</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You have negated <code>test -z</code> or <code>test -n</code>,
resulting in a needless double-negative. You can just use the other
operator instead:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Identical tests to verify that a value is assigned</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">!</span> <span class="ot">-z</span> foo <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="co"># Not has no value</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-n</span> foo <span class="bu">]</span>   <span class="co"># Has value</span></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb3-5"><a href="#cb3-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Identical tests to verify that a value is empty</span></span>
<span id="cb3-6"><a href="#cb3-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">!</span> <span class="ot">-n</span> foo <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="co"># Not is non-empty</span></span>
<span id="cb3-7"><a href="#cb3-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-z</span> foo <span class="bu">]</span>   <span class="co"># Is empty</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>This is a stylistic issue that does not affect correctness. If you
prefer the original expression, you can <a href="Ignore">Ignore</a> it
with a directive or flag.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
<li><a
href="https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Bash-Conditional-Expressions.html#Bash-Conditional-Expressions">Bash
reference manual for -z and -n</a>.</li>
<li>Note: Be careful with quoting variables (which you should always do
anyway): <code>[ ! -z $var ]</code> might work, but
<code>[ -n $var]</code> will not. <code>[ -n "$var" ]</code> will do
what you expect.</li>
</ul>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2238 – Redirecting to/from command name instead of file. Did you want pipes/xargs (or quote to ignore)?</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2238 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2238">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="redirecting-tofrom-command-name-instead-of-file-did-you-want-pipesxargs-or-quote-to-ignore">Redirecting
to/from command name instead of file. Did you want pipes/xargs (or quote
to ignore)?</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">cat</span> file <span class="op">&gt;</span> tr <span class="at">-d</span> <span class="st">&#39;\r&#39;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">cat</span> file <span class="op">&gt;</span> rm</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">cat</span> file <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="fu">tr</span> <span class="at">-d</span> <span class="st">&#39;\r&#39;</span>         <span class="co"># tr reads stdin</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">cat</span> file <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="fu">xargs</span> <span class="at">-d</span> <span class="st">&#39;\n&#39;</span> rm   <span class="co"># rm reads arguments</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You are using file redirection, but the filename is an unquoted
command name. Instead of running the command and feeding data to it,
this just writes to a file with the same name.</p>
<p>To run the command and feed data to it, determine how it gets its
data:</p>
<ul>
<li>If the command reads from STDIN, simply use a pipe as in the first
example.</li>
<li>If the command reads multiple arguments, use a pipe to
<code>xargs</code> as in the second example</li>
</ul>
<p>Note that <code>xargs</code> has many pitfalls when it comes to
spaces and quotes. <code>cat file | xargs rm</code> will appear to work
during testing, but fails for filenames like <code>My File.txt</code> or
<code>Can't_Fight_This_Feeling.mp3</code>. The example uses the GNU
extension <code>-d '\n'</code> to more safely handle these names.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you actually did want to write a file named after a command,
simply quote the filename to let ShellCheck know you meant it literally
and not as a command name. This does not change anything about how the
script works:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Write to a file literally named &#39;rm&#39;, does not try to delete anything</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;A potentially dangerous command&quot;</span> <span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="st">&quot;rm&quot;</span> </span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />

  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2239 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2239">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="ensure-the-shebang-uses-the-absolute-path-to-the-interpreter">Ensure
the shebang uses the absolute path to the interpreter.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!bin/sh</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/sh</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>The script's interpreter, as specified in the shebang, does not start
with a <code>/</code>.</p>
<p>The interpreter should always be specified by absolute path to ensure
that the script can be executed from any directory. When it's not, it's
generally a typo like in the problematic example.</p>
<p>If you don't know where the interpreter is and you hoped to use
<code>#! bash</code>, this is not an option. Use
<code>/usr/bin/env</code> instead:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/usr/bin/env bash</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>While not required by POSIX, <code>env</code> can essentially always
be found in <code>/usr/bin</code> and will search the PATH for the
specified executable.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2240 – The dot command does not support arguments in sh/dash. Set them as variables.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2240 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2240">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="the-dot-command-does-not-support-arguments-in-shdash-set-them-as-variables">The
dot command does not support arguments in sh/dash. Set them as
variables.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/sh</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">.</span> include/myscript example.com 80</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/sh</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">host</span><span class="op">=</span>example.com <span class="va">port</span><span class="op">=</span>80 <span class="bu">.</span> include/myscript </span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>In Bash and Ksh, you can use <code>. myscript arg1 arg2..</code> to
set <code>$1</code> and <code>$2</code> in the sourced script.</p>
<p>This is not the case in Dash, where any additional arguments are
ignored, or in POSIX sh where the behavior is unspecified.</p>
<p>Instead, assign arguments to variables and rewrite the sourced script
to read from them.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2241 – The exit status can only be one integer 0-255. Use stdout for other data.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2241 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2241">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="the-exit-status-can-only-be-one-integer-0-255-use-stdout-for-other-data">The
exit status can only be one integer 0-255. Use stdout for other
data.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">exit</span> foo bar</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> foo</span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> bar</span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">exit</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>In bash, <code>exit</code> can only be used to signal success or
failure (0 = success, 1-255 = failure).</p>
<p>To exit with textual or multiple values from a function, write them
to stdout and capture them with command substitution instead.</p>
<p>See <a href="SC2242">SC2242</a> for more information.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2242 – Can only exit with status 0-255. Other data should be written to stdout/stderr.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2242 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2242">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="can-only-exit-with-status-0-255-other-data-should-be-written-to-stdoutstderr">Can
only exit with status 0-255. Other data should be written to
stdout/stderr.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">exit</span> <span class="st">&quot;Bad filename&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Bad filename&quot;</span> <span class="op">&gt;&amp;</span><span class="dv">2</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">exit</span> 1</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p><code>exit</code> can only be used to signal success or failure (0 =
success, 1-255 = failure). It can not be used to return string data, and
it can not be used to print error messages.</p>
<p>String data should be written stdout, before an <code>exit 0</code>
to exit with success.</p>
<p>Errors should instead be written to stderr, with an
<code>exit 1</code> (or higher) to exit with failure:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">!</span> <span class="ot">-f</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$1</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>   <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$1</span><span class="st"> is not a regular file&quot;</span> <span class="op">&gt;&amp;</span><span class="dv">2</span></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>   <span class="bu">exit</span> 1</span>
<span id="cb3-5"><a href="#cb3-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Note in particular that <code>exit -1</code> is equivalent to
<code>exit 255</code>, but that <code>exit 1</code> is the more
canonical way of expressing the first possible error code.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
