<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$1</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;install&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$USER</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">!=</span> <span class="st">&quot;root&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Must be root to install&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a <code>test</code> command followed by a

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2267 – GNU `xargs -i` is deprecated in favor of `-I{}`</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2267 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2267">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="gnu-xargs--i-is-deprecated-in-favor-of--i">GNU
<code>xargs -i</code> is deprecated in favor of <code>-I{}</code></h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Implicit replacement string</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">xargs</span> <span class="at">-i</span> ls {}</span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Explicit replacement string</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">xargs</span> <span class="at">-imyfilename</span> ls myfilename</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">xargs</span> <span class="at">-I</span> {} ls {}</span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">xargs</span> <span class="at">-I</span> filename ls filename</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p><code>xargs -i</code> is a GNU specific option. It has been
deprecated in favor of the POSIX standard option <code>-I</code>.</p>
<p>Note that <code>-i</code> will implicitly use <code>{}</code> as a
token if nothing is specified, while <code>-I</code> requires it to be
explicit.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2268 – Avoid x-prefix in comparisons as it no longer serves a purpose.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2268 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2268">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="avoid-x-prefix-in-comparisons-as-it-no-longer-serves-a-purpose">Avoid
x-prefix in comparisons as it no longer serves a purpose.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;x</span><span class="va">$pass</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;xswordfish&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">test</span> x<span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> = x </span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$pass</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;swordfish&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span> </span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">test</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> = <span class="st">&quot;&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Some older shells would get confused if the first argument started
with a dash, or consisted of <code>!</code> or <code>(</code>. As a
workaround, people would prefix variables and values to be compared with
<code>x</code> to ensure the left-hand side always started with an
alphanumeric character.</p>
<p>POSIX ensures <a
href="https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/utilities/test.html">this
is not necessary</a>, and all modern shells now follow suit.</p>
<h3 id="examples">Examples:</h3>
<p>Bash 1.14 from 1992 incorrectly fails this test. This was fixed for
Bash 2.0 in 1996:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&#39;!&#39;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;!&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Dash 0.5.4 from 2007 incorrectly passes this test. This was fixed for
Dash 0.5.5 in 2008:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">x</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&#39;(&#39;</span> <span class="va">y</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&#39;)&#39;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-2"><a href="#cb4-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$x</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$y</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Zsh (while not supported by ShellCheck) fixed the same problem in
2015.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you are targeting especially old shells, you can ignore this
warning (or use a different letter).</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>

Bash Pitfall #4</a></li>

</ul>

    <h2
id="this-variable-is-assigned-to-itself-so-the-assignment-does-nothing">This
variable is assigned to itself, so the assignment does nothing.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># If the goal is to do nothing</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">true</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a variable that is assigned to itself, e.g.
<code>x=$x</code>. This obviously has no effect.</p>
<p>Double check what the assignment was supposed to do.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2270 – To assign positional parameters, use `set -- first second ..` (or use `[ ]` to compare).</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2270 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2270">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="to-assign-positional-parameters-use-set----first-second--or-use---to-compare">To
assign positional parameters, use <code>set -- first second ..</code>
(or use <code>[ ]</code> to compare).</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-z</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$1</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="va">$1</span><span class="ex">=</span><span class="st">&quot;help&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="va">$1</span><span class="ex">=</span><span class="st">&quot;help&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Usage: </span><span class="va">$0</span><span class="st"> filename&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-z</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$1</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">set</span> <span class="at">--</span> <span class="st">&quot;help&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="va">$1</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;help&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb4-2"><a href="#cb4-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb4-3"><a href="#cb4-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Usage: </span><span class="va">$0</span><span class="st"> filename&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-4"><a href="#cb4-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You have a command on the form <code>$2=value</code>.</p>
<p>If the goal is to assign a new value to the positional parameters,
use the <code>set</code> builtin: <code>set -- one two ..</code> will
cause <code>$1</code> to be "one" and <code>$2</code> to be "two".</p>
<p>If you instead want to compare the value, use <code>[ ]</code> and
add spaces: <code>[ "$1" = "foo" ]</code></p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2271 – For indirection, use arrays, `declare "var$n=value"`, or (for sh) read/eval</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2271 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2271">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="for-indirection-use-arrays-declare-varnvalue-or-for-sh-readeval">For
indirection, use arrays, <code>declare "var$n=value"</code>, or (for sh)
read/eval</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">n</span><span class="op">=</span>1</span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">var</span><span class="va">$n</span><span class="ex">=</span><span class="st">&quot;hello&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<p>For integer indexing in ksh/bash, consider using an indexed
array:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">n</span><span class="op">=</span>1</span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">[</span>n<span class="op">]=</span><span class="st">&quot;hello&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${var</span><span class="op">[</span>n<span class="op">]</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>For string indexing in ksh/bash, use an associative array:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">typeset</span> <span class="at">-A</span> <span class="va">var</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">n</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;greeting&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">[</span><span class="va">$n</span><span class="op">]=</span><span class="st">&quot;hello&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${var</span><span class="op">[</span><span class="va">$n</span><span class="op">]</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>If you actually need a variable with the constructed name in bash,
use <code>declare</code>:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">n</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;Foo&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-2"><a href="#cb4-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">declare</span> <span class="st">&quot;var</span><span class="va">$n</span><span class="st">=42&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-3"><a href="#cb4-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$varFoo</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>For <code>sh</code>, with single line contents, consider
<code>read</code>:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb5"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb5-1"><a href="#cb5-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">n</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;Foo&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb5-2"><a href="#cb5-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">read</span> <span class="at">-r</span> <span class="st">&quot;var</span><span class="va">$n</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="op">&lt;&lt; EOF</span></span>
<span id="cb5-3"><a href="#cb5-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">hello</span></span>
<span id="cb5-4"><a href="#cb5-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">EOF</span></span>
<span id="cb5-5"><a href="#cb5-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$varFoo</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or with careful escaping, <code>eval</code>:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb6"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb6-1"><a href="#cb6-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">n</span><span class="op">=</span>Foo</span>
<span id="cb6-2"><a href="#cb6-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">eval</span> <span class="st">&quot;var</span><span class="va">$n</span><span class="st">=&#39;hello&#39;&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb6-3"><a href="#cb6-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$varFoo</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p><code>var$n=value</code> is not a valid way of assigning to a
dynamically created variable name in any shell. Please use one of the
other methods to assign to names via expanded strings. <a
href="https://mywiki.wooledge.org/BashFAQ/006">Wooledge BashFaq #6</a>
has significantly more information on the subject.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://mywiki.wooledge.org/BashFAQ/006">Wooledge BashFaq
#6</a>: How can I use variable variables (indirect variables, pointers,
references) or associative arrays?</li>
</ul>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2272 – Command name contains `==`. For comparison, use `[ "$var" = value ]`.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2272 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2272">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="command-name-contains--for-comparison-use--var--value-">Command
name contains <code>==</code>. For comparison, use
<code>[ "$var" = value ]</code>.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">$a</span><span class="ex">/</span><span class="va">$b</span><span class="ex">==foo/bar</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$a</span><span class="st">/</span><span class="va">$b</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;foo/bar&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span> </span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a command name that contains a <code>==</code>. Most
likely, this was intended as a kind of comparison.</p>
<p>To compare two values, use <code>[ value1 = value2 ]</code>. Both the
brackets and the spaces around the <code>=</code> are relevant.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None, though you can quote the <code>==</code> to suppress the
warning.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2273 – Sequence of `===`s found. Merge conflict or intended as a commented border?</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2273 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2273">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="sequence-of-s-found-merge-conflict-or-intended-as-a-commented-border">Sequence
of <code>===</code>s found. Merge conflict or intended as a commented
border?</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">=======</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<p>Either resolve the merge conflict, or use <code># =======</code> for
a border</p>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a series of <code>=======</code>s. If this was
supposed to be a border or separator, use a comment.</p>
<p>However, it could also be left behind from a source control merge
conflict:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">&lt;&lt;&lt;&lt;&lt;&lt;&lt;</span> HEAD</span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Goodbye World&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">=======</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello World!&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;</span> mybranch</span></code></pre></div>
<p>In this case, make sure the merge conflict is correctly resolved, and
all the markers removed.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

<!DOCTYPE html>

  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2274 – Command name starts with `===`. Intended as a commented border?</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2274 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2274">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="command-name-starts-with--intended-as-a-commented-border">Command
name starts with <code>===</code>. Intended as a commented border?</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">=====================</span> MAIN SECTION =======================</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># ===================== MAIN SECTION =======================</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a command that starts with a series of
<code>===</code>s. This may have been intended as a border, but is
missing the <code>#</code> to turn it into a harmless comment.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>

    <h2 id="command-name-starts-with--bad-line-break">Command name starts
with <code>=</code>. Bad line break?</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">my_variable</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="ex">=value</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">myvariable</span><span class="op">=</span>value</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a command name starting with a <code>=</code>. This
was likely not meant as a new command, but instead a continuation from a
previous line.</p>
<p>Make sure the <code>=</code> is used correctly.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None, though you can quote the value to make ShellCheck ignore it,
e.g. <code>"=foo"</code>.</p>

    <h1>SC2276 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2276">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="this-is-interpreted-as-a-command-name-containing--bad-assignment-or-comparison">This
is interpreted as a command name containing <code>=</code>. Bad
assignment or comparison?</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="ex">=42</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="ex">=42</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">true</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span>42</span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> 42 <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">true</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a command name containing an unquoted equals sign
<code>=</code>. This was likely intended as either a comparison or an
assignment.</p>
<p>To compare two values, use e.g. <code>[ "$var" = "42" ]</code></p>
<p>To assign a value, use e.g. <code>var="42"</code></p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None, though you can quote the <code>=</code> to make ShellCheck
ignore it: <code>"$var=42"</code>.</p>

    <hr />
    <h2 id="use-bash_argv0-to-assign-to-0-in-bash-or-use---to-compare">Use
<code>BASH_ARGV0</code> to assign to <code>$0</code> in bash (or use
<code>[ ]</code> to compare).</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/bash</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">$0</span><span class="ex">=myscriptname</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/bash</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">BASH_ARGV0</span><span class="op">=</span>myscriptname</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You appear to be trying to assign a new value to <code>$0</code> in a
Bash script. To do this, instead assign to the special variable
<code>BASH_ARGV0</code>.</p>
<p>If you instead wanted to compare the value of <code>$0</code>, use a
comparison like <code>[ "$0" = "myname" ]</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>

  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2278 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2278">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="0-cant-be-assigned-in-ksh-but-it-does-reflect-the-current-function"><code>$0</code>
can't be assigned in Ksh (but it does reflect the current
function).</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/ksh</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">$0</span><span class="ex">=myname</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Usage: </span><span class="va">$0</span><span class="st"> --help&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/ksh</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">myname()</span> <span class="kw">{</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Usage: </span><span class="va">$0</span><span class="st"> --help&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">myname</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You appear to be trying to assign a new value to <code>$0</code> in
Ksh.</p>
<p>This is not possible. However, <code>$0</code> will reflect the
current function name, so if you wrap your code in a function with your
chosen name, you can have <code>$0</code> expand to it.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you instead wanted to compare the value of <code>$0</code>, use a
comparison like <code>[ "$0" = "myname" ]</code>.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <h2
id="0-cant-be-assigned-in-dash-this-becomes-a-command-name"><code>$0</code>
can't be assigned in Dash. This becomes a command name.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/dash</span></span>

can't be assigned this way, and there is no portable alternative.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/sh</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">$0</span><span class="ex">=myname</span></span></code></pre></div>

<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2281 – Don't use `$`/`${}` on the left side of assignments.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2281 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2281">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="dont-use--on-the-left-side-of-assignments">Don't use
<code>$</code>/<code>${}</code> on the left side of assignments.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">$greeting</span><span class="ex">=</span><span class="st">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">${greeting}</span><span class="ex">=</span><span class="st">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">greeting</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Alternatively, if the goal was to assign to a variable whose name is
in another variable (indirection), use <code>declare</code>:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">name</span><span class="op">=</span>foo</span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">declare</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$name</span><span class="st">=hello world&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$foo</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Or if you actually wanted to compare the value, use a test
expression:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$greeting</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;hello world&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb4-2"><a href="#cb4-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb4-3"><a href="#cb4-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Programmer, I presume?&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-4"><a href="#cb4-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Unlike Perl or PHP, <code>$</code> is not used on the left-hand side
of <code>=</code> when assigning to a variable.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions</h3>
<p>None</p>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <h2
id="variable-names-cant-start-with-numbers-so-this-is-interpreted-as-a-command">Variable
names can't start with numbers, so this is interpreted as a
command.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">411toppm=true</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">_411toppm</span><span class="op">=</span>true</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You appear to be assigning to a variable name that starts with a
digit. This is not allowed: variables must start with A-Z, a-z or _.</p>
<p>Switch to a variable name that does not start with a digit.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>

<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,

    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2283 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2283">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="use---to-compare-values-or-remove-spaces-around--to-assign-or-quote--if-literal">Use
<code>[ ]</code> to compare values, or remove spaces around
<code>=</code> to assign (or quote <code>'='</code> if literal).</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Assignment</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">var</span> = value</span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Comparison</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="va">$var</span> = value</span>
<span id="cb1-6"><a href="#cb1-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-7"><a href="#cb1-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Match&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-8"><a href="#cb1-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Assignment</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span>value</span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Comparison</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> value <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-7"><a href="#cb2-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Match&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-8"><a href="#cb2-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found an unquoted <code>=</code> after a word.</p>
<p>If this was supposed to be a comparison, use square brackets:
<code>[ "$var" = value ]</code></p>
<p>If this was supposed to be an assignment, remove spaces around
<code>=</code>: <code>var=value</code></p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If the <code>=</code> was meant literally, quote it:</p>
<pre><code>grep &#39;=true&#39; file.cfg</code></pre>

<ul>

etc!</li>
</ul>

    <h2
id="this-empty-string-is-interpreted-as-a-command-name-double-check-syntax-or-use-true-as-a-no-op">This
empty string is interpreted as a command name. Double check syntax (or
use 'true' as a no-op).</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">jq</span> </span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>   <span class="st">&#39;&#39;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>   <span class="ex">file.json</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">jq</span> <span class="dt">\</span></span>

<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  file.json</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found an empty string used as a command name. This is
never valid.</p>
<p>If the command is intended to do nothing, use <code>true</code> aka
<code>:</code> instead. Otherwise, determine why an empty string ended
up as a command name and fix it accordingly. In the example, each line
was interpreted as a separate command due to missing line
continuations.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>

    <h2
id="this-is-interpreted-as-a-command-name-ending-with--double-check-syntax">This
is interpreted as a command name ending with '/'. Double check
syntax.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">df/</span></span></code></pre></div>

<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">df</span> /</span></code></pre></div>

    <h1>SC2288 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>

    <h2
id="this-is-interpreted-as-a-command-name-ending-with-apostrophe-double-check-syntax">This
is interpreted as a command name ending with apostrophe. Double check
syntax.</h2>
<p>(also applies to multiple other characters like
<code>.,([{&lt;&gt;}])#"'</code>)</p>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="st">&quot;wget &#39;http://www.shellcheck.net/&#39;&quot;</span><span class="va">)</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> Usage: <span class="va">$0</span> {start<span class="kw">|</span><span class="ex">stop</span><span class="kw">|</span><span class="ex">restart}</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">array</span><span class="op">=</span>val1, <span class="ex">val2,</span> val3</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">wget</span> <span class="st">&#39;http://www.shellcheck.net/&#39;</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Usage: </span><span class="va">$0</span><span class="st"> {start|stop|restart}&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">array</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span>val1 val2 val3<span class="va">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a command name ending with a symbol, such as a
comma, parenthesis, quote, or similar. This is almost always due to a
syntax issue in the script.</p>
<p>In the examples, bad quoting and invalid array syntax caused the
shell to try to run commands ending in apostrophe, curly brace, and
comma, respectively.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you have a command that <em>does</em> end in a symbol, you can
ignore this message.</p>

    <h2
id="this-is-interpreted-as-a-command-name-containing-a-linefeed-double-check-syntax">This
is interpreted as a command name containing a linefeed. Double check
syntax.</h2>
<p>(or tab)</p>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">&#39;&#39;&#39;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">This script greets the planet</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">&#39;&#39;&#39;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># This script greets the planet</span></span>

which a shell will merely interpreted as a multi-line command name
sandwiched between two empty strings.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you have a command name that <em>does</em> contain a tab or
linefeed you can ignore this message, but... wow.</p>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2290 – Remove spaces around = to assign.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2290 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2290">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="remove-spaces-around--to-assign">Remove spaces around = to
assign.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">export</span> <span class="va">LC_ALL</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;POSIX&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">export</span> <span class="va">LC_ALL</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;POSIX&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Parameters to <code>export</code>, <code>declare</code>,
<code>local</code>, <code>typeset</code> and <code>readonly</code> may
not have spaces around the <code>=</code> or <code>+=</code> operator.
This is the same as for regular variable assignments:</p>
<pre><code>export var = value   # Invalid: spaces around =
export var =value    # Invalid: space before =
export var= value    # Invalid: space after =
export var=value     # Valid</code></pre>
<p>This is because each individual argument to these commands is
interpreted as a string in the format <code>name=value</code>. By adding
spaces, you are instead passing the three strings <code>var</code>,
<code>=</code>, <code>value</code>, none of which follow this
format.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2291 – Quote repeated spaces to avoid them collapsing into one.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2291 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2291">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="quote-repeated-spaces-to-avoid-them-collapsing-into-one">Quote
repeated spaces to avoid them collapsing into one.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> Hello        World</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello        World&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found multiple unquoted spaces between words passed to
<code>echo</code>. Due to the way arguments are interpreted and passed
in the shell, these will collapse into a single space:</p>
<pre class="console"><code>$ echo Hello        World
Hello World</code></pre>
<p>If you want to output multiple spaces, such as when creating a notice
or banner, make sure the spaces are quoted, e.g. by adding (or
extending) double quotes to include them:</p>
<pre class="console"><code>$ echo &quot;Hello        World&quot;
Hello        World</code></pre>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you're aware of this behavior and didn't want multiple spaces to
show up in the output, you can either remove the unnecessary spaces or
<a href="ignore">ignore</a> this issue.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2292 – Prefer `[[ ]]` over `[ ]` for tests in Bash/Ksh.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2292 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2292">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="prefer---over---for-tests-in-bashksh">Prefer <code>[[ ]]</code>
over <code>[ ]</code> for tests in Bash/Ksh.</h2>
<h3 id="optional---require-double-brackets">Optional -
<code>require-double-brackets</code></h3>
<p>This is an <a href="optional">optional</a> rule, which means that it
has a special "long name" and is not enabled by default. See the <a
href="optional">optional</a> page for more details. In short, you have
to enable it with the long name instead of the "SC" code like you would
with a normal rule:</p>
<h4 id="shellcheckrc"><code>.shellcheckrc</code></h4>
<pre><code>enable=require-double-brackets # SC2292</code></pre>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="ot">-e</span> /etc/issue <span class="bu">]</span> </span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="ot">-e</span> /etc/issue <span class="kw">]]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck has been explicitly asked to warn about uses of
<code>[ .. ]</code> in favor of the extended Bash/Ksh test
<code>[[ .. ]]</code>.</p>
<p><code>[[ .. ]]</code> suppresses word splitting and globbing,
supports a wider variety of tests, and is generally safer and better
defined than <code>[ .. ]</code>. For an in-depth list of differences,
see the Related Resources.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>This check is not enabled by default, and may have been turned on for
your current project by someone who wants it enforced. You can still <a
href="ignore">ignore</a> it with a directive.</p>
<p>This suggestion does not trigger for Sh or Dash scripts, even when
explicitly enabled, as these shells don't support
<code>[[ .. ]]</code>.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>BashFAQ 031: <a href="https://mywiki.wooledge.org/BashFAQ/031">What
is the difference between test, [ and [[ ?</a></li>
</ul>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2293 – When eval'ing @Q-quoted words, use * rather than @ as the index.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2293 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2293">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="when-evaling-q-quoted-words-use--rather-than--as-the-index">When
eval'ing @Q-quoted words, use * rather than @ as the index.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">eval</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$MYCOMMAND</span><span class="st"> </span><span class="va">${@</span><span class="op">@</span><span class="va">Q}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">eval</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$MYCOMMAND</span><span class="st"> </span><span class="va">${*</span><span class="op">@</span><span class="va">Q}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck noticed that you are calling <code>eval</code> and
including an escaped array. However, the array is passed as multiple
arguments and relies on being implicitly joined together to form a
single shell string, which <code>eval</code> can then evaluate.</p>
<p>Instead, prefer building your shell string with explicit string
concatenation by using <code>*</code> instead of <code>@</code> for the
index, such as <code>${*@Q}</code> or <code>${array[*]@Q}</code>.</p>
<p>This suggestion is equivalent to <a href="SC2124">SC2124</a>, but for
<code>eval</code> arguments rather than string variables.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>
  </body>

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2294 – eval negates the benefit of arrays. Drop eval to preserve whitespace/symbols (or eval as string).</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2294 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2294">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="eval-negates-the-benefit-of-arrays-drop-eval-to-preserve-whitespacesymbols-or-eval-as-string">eval
negates the benefit of arrays. Drop eval to preserve whitespace/symbols
(or eval as string).</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">check()</span> <span class="kw">{</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">eval</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$@</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="kw">||</span> <span class="bu">exit</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">check()</span> <span class="kw">{</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$@</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="kw">||</span> <span class="bu">exit</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found <code>eval</code> used on an array (or equivalently,
<code>"$@"</code>). This is problematic because it effectively throws
away all boundary information and rebuilds it from shell words.</p>
<p>Let's say you invoke
<code>check sed -i '$d' "my file.txt"</code>:</p>
<p><code>eval "$@"</code> will:</p>
<ol>
<li>Join the elements on spaces: <code>sed -i $d my file.txt</code></li>
<li>Split the string on shell word boundaries: <code>sed</code>,
<code>-i</code>, <code>$d</code>, <code>my</code>
<code>file.txt</code></li>
<li>Perform shell expansions (assuming <code>$d</code> is unset):
<code>sed</code>, <code>-i</code>, <code>my</code>,
<code>file.txt</code></li>
<li>Execute the first element as the command and the rest as its
arguments, as if running <code>sed -i 'my' 'file.txt'</code></li>
</ol>
<p><code>"$@"</code> will</p>
<ol>
<li>Execute the first element as the command and the rest as its
arguments, as if running <code>sed -i '$d' 'my file.txt'</code></li>
</ol>
<p>Note that while <code>"$@"</code> is essentially always better than
<code>eval "$@"</code>, it's easy to unintentionally introduce a
dependency on bad behavior through the shell debugging anti-strategy of
"adding quotes until it works":</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Works with problematic example because of double-escaping, fails with correct example</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">check</span> ls <span class="at">-l</span> <span class="st">&quot;&#39;My File.txt&#39;&quot;</span> </span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Works with correct example the way it was always intended:</span></span>
<span id="cb3-5"><a href="#cb3-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">check</span> ls <span class="at">-l</span> <span class="st">&quot;My File.txt&quot;</span> </span></code></pre></div>
<p>The correct example is still better, but the function invocation has
to be tweaked as well.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If each of the array elements is a carefully escaped shell command or
word, use <code>*</code> instead of <code>@</code> to explicitly join
the elements on spaces which is what would happen anyways:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre
class="sourceCode bash"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">on_exit</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span></span>
<span id="cb4-2"><a href="#cb4-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="st">&#39;rm /tmp/myfile; &#39;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-3"><a href="#cb4-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="st">&#39;echo &quot;Finished on $(date)&quot; &gt; log.txt; &#39;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-4"><a href="#cb4-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">)</span></span>
<span id="cb4-5"><a href="#cb4-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb4-6"><a href="#cb4-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Equivalent to `eval &quot;${on_exit[@]}&quot;`, but more explicit</span></span>
<span id="cb4-7"><a href="#cb4-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">eval</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${on_exit</span><span class="op">[*]</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-8"><a href="#cb4-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb4-9"><a href="#cb4-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Even better in this case, as it does not require</span></span>
<span id="cb4-10"><a href="#cb4-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># semicolons and commands don&#39;t interfere:</span></span>
<span id="cb4-11"><a href="#cb4-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> cmd <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${on_exit</span><span class="op">[@]</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-12"><a href="#cb4-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb4-13"><a href="#cb4-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">eval</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$cmd</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-14"><a href="#cb4-14" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>If you require <code>eval</code> for another part of the command,
explicitly transform the array into a series of escaped shell words.
This ensures that the array elements will <code>eval</code> back to
themselves:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb5"><pre
class="sourceCode bash"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb5-1"><a href="#cb5-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Assumed to be outside of our control, </span></span>
<span id="cb5-2"><a href="#cb5-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># otherwise we would output this in an array as well:</span></span>
<span id="cb5-3"><a href="#cb5-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">COMMAND</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&#39;dialog --menu &quot;Choose file:&quot; 15 40 4&#39;</span></span>
<span id="cb5-4"><a href="#cb5-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb5-5"><a href="#cb5-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Our array:</span></span>
<span id="cb5-6"><a href="#cb5-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">array</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span></span>
<span id="cb5-7"><a href="#cb5-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  1 <span class="st">&quot;My File.txt&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb5-8"><a href="#cb5-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  2 <span class="st">&quot;My Other File.txt&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb5-9"><a href="#cb5-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">)</span></span>
<span id="cb5-10"><a href="#cb5-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">eval</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$COMMAND</span><span class="st"> </span><span class="va">${array</span><span class="op">[*]@</span><span class="va">Q}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span>                     <span class="co"># Bash 4+</span></span>
<span id="cb5-11"><a href="#cb5-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">eval</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$COMMAND</span><span class="st"> </span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="bu">printf</span> <span class="st">&quot;%q &quot;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${array</span><span class="op">[@]</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st">&quot;</span>     <span class="co"># Bash 1+</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2295 – Expansions inside `${..}` need to be quoted separately, otherwise they will match as a pattern.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2295 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2295">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="expansions-inside--need-to-be-quoted-separately-otherwise-they-will-match-as-a-pattern">Expansions
inside <code>${..}</code> need to be quoted separately, otherwise they
will match as a pattern.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">relative_path()</span> <span class="kw">{</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">printf</span> <span class="st">&#39;%s\n&#39;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${2</span><span class="op">#</span><span class="va">$1}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Results in &quot;/tmp/King_Kong_[1933]/extras/trailer.mkv&quot; because the prefix fails to match</span></span>
<span id="cb1-6"><a href="#cb1-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">relative_path</span> <span class="st">&quot;/tmp/King_Kong_[1933]/&quot;</span> <span class="st">&quot;/tmp/King_Kong_[1933]/extras/trailer.mkv&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-7"><a href="#cb1-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb1-8"><a href="#cb1-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Results in &quot;cover.jpg&quot; even though the prefix is different</span></span>
<span id="cb1-9"><a href="#cb1-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">relative_path</span> <span class="st">&quot;/tmp/King_Kong_[1933]/&quot;</span> <span class="st">&quot;/tmp/King_Kong_3/cover.jpg&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">relative_path()</span> <span class="kw">{</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">printf</span> <span class="st">&#39;%s\n&#39;</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${2</span><span class="op">#</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$1</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Results in &quot;extras/trailer.mkv&quot; as expected</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">relative_path</span> <span class="st">&quot;/tmp/King_Kong_[1933]/&quot;</span> <span class="st">&quot;/tmp/King_Kong_[1933]/extras/trailer.mkv&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-7"><a href="#cb2-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Results in &quot;/tmp/King_Kong_3/cover.jpg&quot; as expected</span></span>
<span id="cb2-8"><a href="#cb2-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">relative_path</span> <span class="st">&quot;/tmp/King_Kong_[1933]/&quot;</span> <span class="st">&quot;/tmp/King_Kong_3/cover.jpg&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>When using expansions in a parameter expansion prefix/suffix
expression, the expansion needs to be quoted separately or it will match
as a pattern. The quotes around the outer parameter expansion do not
protect against this.</p>
<p>This means that any variable that contains e.g. brackets, asterisks
or question marks may not match as expected. In the example,
<code>[1933]</code> was interpreted as a pattern character range and
would therefore match <code>/tmp/King_Kong_3/</code> but not
<code>/tmp/King_Kong_[1933]/</code> as was the intention.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you wanted to treat the string as a pattern, such as
<code>suffix=".*"; file="${var%$suffix}";</code> then you can <a
href="ignore">ignore</a> this suggestion.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2296 – Parameter expansions can't start with `{`. Double check syntax.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2296 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2296">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="parameter-expansions-cant-start-with--double-check-syntax">Parameter
expansions can't start with <code>{</code>. Double check syntax.</h2>
<p>(or any other character)</p>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello </span><span class="va">${</span><span class="er">{name</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello </span><span class="va">${name}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a parameter expansion <code>${something}</code> that
starts with an invalid character. In the example, this was caused by
accidentally duplicating the <code>{</code> in
<code>${{name}</code>.</p>
<p>Double check the syntax of what you're trying to do.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>Some Zsh specific parameter expansions like <code>${(q)value}</code>
trigger this warning, but ShellCheck does not support Zsh.</p>
<p>If this warning triggers in code that works on Bash, Ksh, Dash or Sh,
please <a
href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/issues/new">submit a
bug</a>.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2297 – Double quotes must be outside `${}`: `${"invalid"}` vs `"${valid}"`.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2297 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2297">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="double-quotes-must-be-outside--invalid-vs-valid">Double quotes
must be outside <code>${}</code>: <code>${"invalid"}</code> vs
<code>"${valid}"</code>.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="va">${</span><span class="er">&quot;USER&quot;</span><span class="va">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${USER}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a parameter expansion containing what appears to be
a quoted variable name.</p>
<p>While the parameter expansion itself must be quoted, as in
<code>"${valid}"</code>, the quotes may not appear inside the
<code>{}</code> as in <code>${"invalid"}</code>.</p>
<p>Also note that translated strings like <code>$"Hello"</code> may not
use curly braces.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>

<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>
