<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2298 – `${$x}` is invalid. For expansion, use ${x}. For indirection, use arrays, ${!x} or (for sh) eval.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2298 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2298">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="x-is-invalid-for-expansion-use-x-for-indirection-use-arrays-x-or-for-sh-eval"><code>${$x}</code>
is invalid. For expansion, use ${x}. For indirection, use arrays, ${!x}
or (for sh) eval.</h2>
<p>(or <code>${${x}}</code> is invalid)</p>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Expecting $RETRIES or 3 if unset</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">retries</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">${$</span><span class="er">RETRIES:-3</span><span class="va">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">mypath</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;/tmp/foo.txt&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span>mypath</span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">result</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">${$</span><span class="er">var##*/</span><span class="va">}</span>  <span class="co"># Expecting ${mypath##*/}, i.e. &#39;foo.txt&#39;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">retries</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">${RETRIES</span><span class="op">:-</span>3<span class="va">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">mypath</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;/tmp/foo.txt&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-2"><a href="#cb4-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span>mypath</span>
<span id="cb4-3"><a href="#cb4-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">result</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">${</span><span class="op">!</span><span class="va">var}</span></span>
<span id="cb4-4"><a href="#cb4-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">result</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">${result</span><span class="op">##</span><span class="pp">*</span>/<span class="va">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a parameter expansion <code>${..}</code> where the
first element was a second parameter expansion, either
<code>${$x..}</code> or <code>${${x}..}</code>. This is not valid.</p>
<p>In the first example, the extra <code>$</code> was unintentional and
should simply be deleted.</p>
<p>In the second example, <code>${$var##*/}</code> was used in the hopes
that it would expand to <code>${myvar##*/}</code> and subsequently strip
the path. This is not possible, and <code>var</code> must instead be
expanded indirectly in a separate step, before the path can be stripped
as usual. More information and other approaches can be found in the
description of <a href="SC2082">SC2082</a>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2299 – Parameter expansions can't be nested. Use temporary variables.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2299 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2299">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="parameter-expansions-cant-be-nested-use-temporary-variables">Parameter
expansions can't be nested. Use temporary variables.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">path</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;/path/to/MyFile.mp3&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Playing </span><span class="va">${$</span><span class="er">{path##*/</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">%.*}&quot;</span>    <span class="co"># Expect: Playing MyFile</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">path</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;/path/to/MyFile.mp3&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">tmp</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">${path</span><span class="op">##</span><span class="pp">*</span>/<span class="va">}</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Playing </span><span class="va">${tmp</span><span class="op">%</span>.<span class="pp">*</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found what appears to be a nested parameter expansion. In
the example, it was hoping to combine <code>${var##*/}</code> to strip
the directory and <code>${var%.*}</code> to strip the extension.</p>
<p>Parameter expansions can't be nested. Use temporary variables
instead, so that each parameter expansion only does a single
operation.</p>
<p>Alternatively, if the goal is to dynamically generate and expand a
variable name, see <a href="SC2082">SC2082</a>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>

<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2300 – Parameter expansion can't be applied to command substitutions. Use temporary variables.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2300 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2300">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="parameter-expansion-cant-be-applied-to-command-substitutions-use-temporary-variables">Parameter
expansion can't be applied to command substitutions. Use temporary
variables.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Building </span><span class="va">${$</span><span class="er">(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)##*/</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">tmp</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">git</span> rev-parse <span class="at">--show-toplevel</span><span class="va">)</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Building </span><span class="va">${tmp</span><span class="op">##</span><span class="pp">*</span>/<span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a parameter expansion that begins with a command
substitution, such as <code>$(..)</code> or <code>`..`</code>. This is
not valid. Parameter expansion only works on variables (normal or
special).</p>
<p>In the example, the user hoped to apply the construct
<code>${var##*/}</code>, stripping the path, to the current git root
directory as output by <code>git rev-parse --show-toplevel</code>. Since
parameter expansion only works on variable, the command substitution
must be assigned to a variable first like in the correct example.</p>
<p>If the goal was instead to dynamically generate a variable name to
expand, see <a href="SC2082">SC2082</a>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>

<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>

    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2301 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2301">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="parameter-expansion-starts-with-unexpected-quotes-double-check-syntax">Parameter
expansion starts with unexpected quotes. Double check syntax.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="va">${</span><span class="er">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span><span class="va">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">$&quot;Hello World&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a parameter expansion <code>${...}</code> that
contains an unexpected syntax element, such as single or double
quotes.</p>
<p>In the example, this was due to wrapping a translated string
<code>$".."</code> with curly braces, which is not valid.</p>
<p>It is unclear what the intention is with invalid expansions like
<code>${'foo'}</code>, <code>${$"foo"}</code>, so please look up how to
do what you were trying to do.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If this warning triggers for working code, please <a
href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/issues/new">submit a
bug</a>.</p>

  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2302 – This loops over values. To loop over keys, use `"${!array[@]}"`.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2302 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2302">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="this-loops-over-values-to-loop-over-keys-use-array">This loops
over values. To loop over keys, use <code>"${!array[@]}"</code>.</h2>
<p>Plus companion warning <a href="SC2303">SC2303</a>:
<code>i is an array value, not a key. Use directly or loop over keys instead.</code></p>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">array</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span>foo bar<span class="va">)</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> v <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${array</span><span class="op">[@]</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Value is </span><span class="va">${array</span><span class="op">[</span><span class="va">$v</span><span class="op">]</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<p>Either loop over values</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> v <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${array</span><span class="op">[@]</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Value is </span><span class="va">$v</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or loop over keys:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> k <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${</span><span class="op">!</span><span class="va">array</span><span class="op">[@]</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span>  <span class="co"># Note `!`</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Key is </span><span class="va">$k</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Value is </span><span class="va">${array</span><span class="op">[</span><span class="va">$k</span><span class="op">]</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-5"><a href="#cb3-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a <code>for</code> loop over array <em>values</em>,
where the variable is used as an array <em>key</em>.</p>
<p>In the problematic example, the loop will print
<code>Value is foo</code> twice. On the second iteration,
<code>v=bar</code>, and <code>bar</code> is unset and considered zero,
so <code>${array[$v]}</code> becomes <code>${array[bar]}</code> becomes
<code>${array[0]}</code> becomes <code>foo</code>.</p>
<p>If you don't care about the key, simply loop over array values and
use <code>$v</code> to refer to the array value, like in the first
correct example.</p>
<p>If you do want the key, loop over array keys with
<code>"${!array[@]}"</code>, use <code>$k</code> to refer to the array
key, and <code>${array[$k]}</code> to refer to the array value.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you do want to use values from the arrays as keys in the same
array, you can <a href="ignore">ignore</a> these messages with a
directive:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">declare</span> <span class="at">-A</span> <span class="va">fatherOf</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">(</span></span>
<span id="cb4-2"><a href="#cb4-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="op">[</span><span class="st">&quot;Eric Bloodaxe&quot;</span><span class="op">]</span><span class="va">=</span><span class="st">&quot;Harald Fairhair&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-3"><a href="#cb4-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="op">[</span><span class="st">&quot;Harald Fairhair&quot;</span><span class="op">]</span><span class="va">=</span><span class="st">&quot;Halfdan the Black&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-4"><a href="#cb4-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="op">[</span><span class="st">&quot;Halfdan the Black&quot;</span><span class="op">]</span><span class="va">=</span><span class="st">&quot;Gudrød the Hunter&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-5"><a href="#cb4-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="op">[</span><span class="st">&quot;Gudrød the Hunter&quot;</span><span class="op">]</span><span class="va">=</span><span class="st">&quot;Halfdan the Mild&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-6"><a href="#cb4-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">)</span></span>
<span id="cb4-7"><a href="#cb4-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb4-8"><a href="#cb4-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># shellcheck disable=SC2302,SC2303</span></span>
<span id="cb4-9"><a href="#cb4-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> i <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${fatherOf</span><span class="op">[@]</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> </span>
<span id="cb4-10"><a href="#cb4-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb4-11"><a href="#cb4-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${fatherOf</span><span class="op">[</span><span class="va">$i</span><span class="op">]:-</span>(missing)<span class="va">}</span><span class="st"> begat </span><span class="va">$i</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-12"><a href="#cb4-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">done</span></span></code></pre></div>

  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2304 – `*` must be escaped to multiply: `\*`. Modern `$((x * y))` avoids this issue.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2304 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2304">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="-must-be-escaped-to-multiply--modern-x--y-avoids-this-issue"><code>*</code>
must be escaped to multiply: <code>\*</code>. Modern
<code>$((x * y))</code> avoids this issue.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">result</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">expr</span> 2 <span class="pp">*</span> 3<span class="va">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Modern, efficient, POSIX standard approach</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">result</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$((</span> <span class="dv">2</span> <span class="op">*</span> <span class="dv">3</span> <span class="va">))</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Older, slower approach</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">result</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">expr</span> 2 <span class="dt">\*</span> 3<span class="va">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found an <code>expr</code> command whose operator is an
unescaped asterisk <code>*</code>.</p>
<p>When using <code>expr</code>, each argument is expanded the same way
as for any other command. This means that <code>expr 2 * 3</code> will
turn into
<code>expr 2 Desktop Documents Downloads Music Pictures 3</code>
depending on the files in the current directory, causing an error like
<code>expr: syntax error: unexpected argument ‘Desktop’</code></p>
<p>The best way to avoid this is to avoid <code>expr</code> and instead
use <code>$((..))</code> instead. If you for any reason prefer the 200x
slower, heavyweight process of forking a new process, you can escape the
<code>*</code>. Both ways are demonstrated in the correct example.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2305 – Quote regex argument to expr to avoid it expanding as a glob.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2305 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2305">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="quote-regex-argument-to-expr-to-avoid-it-expanding-as-a-glob">Quote
regex argument to expr to avoid it expanding as a glob.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">expr</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$input</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> : <span class="pp">[</span><span class="ss">0</span><span class="pp">-</span><span class="ss">9</span><span class="pp">]*</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">expr</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$input</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> : <span class="st">&quot;[0-9]*&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found an <code>expr</code> command using <code>:</code> to
match a regex, but the regex is not quoted and therefore being treated
as a glob.</p>
<p>This means that if the problematic code is ever executed in a
directory containing a file matching <code>[0-9]*</code>, such as
<code>2021-reports</code> or <code>12 Angry Men [1957].mkv</code>, it
will be replaced be replaced and cause the command to error or
incorrectly match.</p>
<p>The regex should be quoted to avoid this, like in the correct
example.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>

    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2306 – Escape glob characters in arguments to expr to avoid pathname expansion.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2306 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2306">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="escape-glob-characters-in-arguments-to-expr-to-avoid-pathname-expansion">Escape
glob characters in arguments to expr to avoid pathname expansion.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">f</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">expr</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$c</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="pp">*</span> 9 / 5 + 32<span class="va">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<p>Prefer rewriting to a modern style (see <a
href="SC2003">SC2003</a>):</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">f</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$((c</span> <span class="op">*</span> <span class="dv">9</span> <span class="op">/</span> <span class="dv">5</span> <span class="op">+</span> <span class="dv">32</span><span class="va">))</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>If you do not wish to do so, at least escape the glob characters when
passing them to <code>expr</code>:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">f</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">expr</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$c</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="dt">\*</span> 9 / 5 + 32<span class="va">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p><code>expr</code> is a command so <code>expr 2 * 2</code> will
consider <code>*</code> to mean "all files in the current directory".
This causes the expression to fail to evaluate unless you are in an
empty directory with the <code>failglob</code> and <code>nullglob</code>
options turned off.</p>
<p>Prefer rewriting it using the modern, POSIX standard arithmetic
expansion <code>$((..))</code>. If you do not wish to do so, you can
escape any characters like <code>*</code> to avoid the shell performing
pathname expansion on them.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2307 – 'expr' expects 3+ arguments but sees 1. Make sure each operator/operand is a separate argument, and escape <>&|.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2307 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2307">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="expr-expects-3-arguments-but-sees-1-make-sure-each-operatoroperand-is-a-separate-argument-and-escape-">'expr'
expects 3+ arguments but sees 1. Make sure each operator/operand is a
separate argument, and escape &lt;&gt;&amp;|.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># | not escaped</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">expr</span> 1 <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="ex">2</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># &gt; not escaped</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">expr</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$foo</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="op">&gt;</span>= <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$bar</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb1-6"><a href="#cb1-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Missing spaces around +</span></span>
<span id="cb1-7"><a href="#cb1-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">expr</span> 1+2</span>
<span id="cb1-8"><a href="#cb1-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Unexpected quoting around an expression</span></span>
<span id="cb1-9"><a href="#cb1-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">expr</span> <span class="st">&quot;1 + 2&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">expr</span> 16 <span class="dt">\|</span> 7</span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">expr</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$foo</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="dt">\&gt;</span>= <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$bar</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">expr</span> 1 + 2</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found an <code>expr</code> command with 1 or 2 arguments.
<code>expr</code> normally expects 3 or more.</p>
<p>Generally, this happens for one of two reasons:</p>
<ul>
<li>You are using an operator like <code>|</code>, <code>&amp;</code>,
<code>&gt;</code>, <code>&gt;=</code>, <code>&lt;</code>,
<code>&lt;=</code>, which needs to be escaped to avoid the shell
interpreting it as a pipe, backgrounded command, or redirection.</li>
<li>You don't have spaces around operators and operands (or have bad
quotes) which causes them not to be separate arguments.</li>
</ul>
<p>Make sure each operator or operand to <code>expr</code> is a separate
argument, and that anything containing shell metacharacters is escaped.
The correct code shows examples of each.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>

<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>

  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2308 – `expr length` has unspecified results. Prefer `${#var}`.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2308 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2308">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="expr-length-has-unspecified-results-prefer-var"><code>expr length</code>
has unspecified results. Prefer <code>${#var}</code>.</h2>
<p>or
<code>'expr match' has unspecified results. Prefer 'expr str : regex'.</code><br />
or
<code>'expr substr' has unspecified results. Prefer 'cut' or ${var#???}.</code><br />
or
<code>'expr index' has unspecified results. Prefer x=${var%%[chars]*}; $((${#x}+1)).</code></p>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Find length of string</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">length</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">expr</span> length <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">)</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Match string against regex</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">expr</span> match <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$input</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="st">&quot;[0-9]*&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-6"><a href="#cb1-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb1-7"><a href="#cb1-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Find character index in string</span></span>
<span id="cb1-8"><a href="#cb1-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">pos</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">expr</span> index <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$input</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="st">&quot;:&quot;</span><span class="va">)</span></span>
<span id="cb1-9"><a href="#cb1-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb1-10"><a href="#cb1-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Get substring by index</span></span>
<span id="cb1-11"><a href="#cb1-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">col2</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">expr</span> substr <span class="st">&quot;foo    bar  baz&quot;</span> 8 5<span class="va">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Find length of string</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">length</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">${</span><span class="op">#</span><span class="va">var}</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Match string against regex</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">expr</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$input</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> : <span class="st">&quot;[0-9]*&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-7"><a href="#cb2-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Find character index in string</span></span>
<span id="cb2-8"><a href="#cb2-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">pos</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">${input</span><span class="op">%%</span>:<span class="pp">*</span><span class="va">}</span> <span class="va">pos</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$((${</span><span class="op">#</span><span class="va">pos}</span><span class="op">+</span><span class="dv">1</span><span class="va">))</span></span>
<span id="cb2-9"><a href="#cb2-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-10"><a href="#cb2-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Get substring by index (bash)</span></span>
<span id="cb2-11"><a href="#cb2-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">str</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;foo    bar  baz&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-12"><a href="#cb2-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">col2</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${str</span><span class="op">:</span><span class="dv">7</span><span class="op">:</span><span class="dv">5</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-13"><a href="#cb2-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-14"><a href="#cb2-14" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Get substring by index (POSIX)</span></span>
<span id="cb2-15"><a href="#cb2-15" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">col2</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="bu">printf</span> <span class="st">&#39;foo    bar  baz\n&#39;</span> <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="fu">cut</span> <span class="at">-c</span> 8-12<span class="va">)</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>You are using a <code>expr</code> with <code>length</code>,
<code>match</code>, <code>index</code>, or <code>substr</code>. These
forms did not make it into POSIX, and fail on platforms like MacOS and
FreeBSD. Consider replacing them with portable equivalents:</p>
<h4 id="length"><code>length</code></h4>
<p>can be trivially replaced with <code>${#var}</code></p>
<h4 id="match"><code>match</code></h4>
<p>can be trivially replaced with the POSIX form
<code>expr str : regex</code></p>
<h4 id="index"><code>index</code></h4>
<p>if you only need a numerical index as part of trying to extract a
piece of the string, consider replacing it with parameter expansion:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">str</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;mykey=myvalue&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">key</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${str</span><span class="op">%%</span>=<span class="pp">*</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span>    <span class="co"># Remove everything after first =, no index required</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">value</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${str</span><span class="op">#</span><span class="pp">*</span>=<span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span>   <span class="co"># Remove everything before first =, no index required</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>otherwise, you can find the index of the first <code>=</code> using
parameter expansion and string length:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">str</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;mykey=myvalue&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-2"><a href="#cb4-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">x</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">${str</span><span class="op">%%</span>=<span class="pp">*</span><span class="va">}</span>     <span class="co"># Assign x=&quot;mystr&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-3"><a href="#cb4-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">index</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$((${</span><span class="op">#</span><span class="va">x}</span><span class="op">+</span><span class="dv">1</span><span class="va">))</span>   <span class="co"># Add 1 to length of x</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h4 id="substr"><code>substr</code></h4>
<p>Extract a substring via character index is generally fragile. For
example, in this example, any minor changes to the format, including
just the version increasing from 8.9 to 8.10, will cause the following
snippet to fail:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb5"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb5-1"><a href="#cb5-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">str</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;VIM - Vi IMproved 8.2 (2019 Dec 12, compiled Feb 15 2021 12:29:39)&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb5-2"><a href="#cb5-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">version</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">expr</span> substr <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$str</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> 19 3<span class="va">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Instead, consider a different approach:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb6"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb6-1"><a href="#cb6-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">x</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${str</span><span class="op">%%</span> (<span class="pp">*</span><span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span>     <span class="co"># Delete ` (` and everything after, giving &quot;VIM - Vi IMproved 8.2&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb6-2"><a href="#cb6-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">version</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${x</span><span class="op">##</span><span class="pp">*</span> <span class="va">}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span>  <span class="co"># Delete everything before last space, giving &quot;8.2&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb6-3"><a href="#cb6-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb6-4"><a href="#cb6-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Get the fifth word separated by spaces</span></span>
<span id="cb6-5"><a href="#cb6-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">IFS</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot; &quot;</span> <span class="bu">read</span> <span class="at">-r</span> <span class="va">_</span> <span class="va">_</span> <span class="va">_</span> <span class="va">_</span> <span class="va">version</span> <span class="va">_</span> <span class="op">&lt;&lt; EOF</span></span>
<span id="cb6-6"><a href="#cb6-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">$str</span></span>
<span id="cb6-7"><a href="#cb6-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">EOF</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>If you still want to use character index, this is trivially done in
Bash/Ksh with <code>${var:offset:length}</code> (0-based).</p>
<p>In POSIX, you can generally use <code>cut</code>, though be careful
if the value can contain multiple lines.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you know your script will only run on platforms where these forms
are supported, like GNU or BusyBox, you can <a href="ignore">ignore</a>
this warning.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2309 – -eq treats this as a variable. Use = to compare as string (or expand explicitly with $var)</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2309 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2309">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="-eq-treats-this-as-a-variable-use--to-compare-as-string-or-expand-explicitly-with-var">-eq
treats this as a variable. Use = to compare as string (or expand
explicitly with $var)</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">read</span> <span class="at">-p</span> <span class="st">&quot;Continue? [y/n] &quot;</span> <span class="va">var</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">-eq</span> <span class="st">&quot;n&quot;</span> <span class="er">​</span><span class="ex">]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="bu">exit</span> 1</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#read -p &quot;Continue? [y/n] &quot; var</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$var</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;n&quot;</span> <span class="er">​</span><span class="ex">]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="bu">exit</span> 1</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a string used as an argument to a numerical operator
like <code>-eq</code>, <code>-ne</code>, <code>-lt</code>,
<code>-ge</code>. Such strings will be treated as arithmetic
expressions, meaning <code>n</code> will refer to a variable
<code>$n</code>, and <code>24/12</code> will be evaluated into
<code>2</code>.</p>
<p>In the problematic example, the intention was instead to compare
<code>"n"</code> as a string, so it should use the equivalent string
operator instead, in this case <code>=</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>It is perfectly valid to use variables as operands. ShellCheck will
not flag any value that is an unquoted variable name assigned in the
script:</p>
<pre><code>a=42; [[ &quot;a&quot; -eq 0 ]]  # Flagged due to quotes
      [[ b -eq 0 ]]    # Flagged due to not being assigned
c=42; [[ c -eq 0 ]]    # Not flagged</code></pre>
<p>However, ShellCheck does not know whether you intended
<code>foo/bar</code> to be division or a file path.</p>
<p>If you intended to divide <code>$foo</code> and <code>$bar</code>,
you can either make it explicit with
<code>[[ $((foo/bar)) -ge 0 ]]</code>, or simply <a
href="ignore">ignore</a> the warning.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc</li>
</ul>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2310 – This function is invoked in an 'if' condition so set -e will be disabled. Invoke separately if failures should cause the script to exit.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2310 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2310">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="this-function-is-invoked-in-an-if-condition-so-set--e-will-be-disabled-invoke-separately-if-failures-should-cause-the-script-to-exit">This
function is invoked in an 'if' condition so set -e will be disabled.
Invoke separately if failures should cause the script to exit.</h2>
<h3 id="optional---check-set-e-suppressed">Optional -
<code>check-set-e-suppressed</code></h3>
<p>This is an <a href="optional">optional</a> rule, which means that it
has a special "long name" and is not enabled by default. See the <a
href="optional">optional</a> page for more details. In short, you have
to enable it with the long name instead of the "SC" code like you would
with a normal rule:</p>
<h4 id="shellcheckrc"><code>.shellcheckrc</code></h4>
<pre><code>enable=check-set-e-suppressed # SC2310</code></pre>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/sh</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#shellcheck enable=check-set-e-suppressed</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">set</span> <span class="at">-e</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">backup()</span> <span class="kw">{</span></span>
<span id="cb2-7"><a href="#cb2-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">cp</span> <span class="pp">*</span>.txt /backup</span>
<span id="cb2-8"><a href="#cb2-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">rm</span> <span class="pp">*</span>.txt            <span class="co"># Runs even if copy fails!</span></span>
<span id="cb2-9"><a href="#cb2-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span></span>
<span id="cb2-10"><a href="#cb2-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-11"><a href="#cb2-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="ex">backup</span></span>
<span id="cb2-12"><a href="#cb2-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-13"><a href="#cb2-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Backup successful&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-14"><a href="#cb2-14" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/sh</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#shellcheck enable=check-set-e-suppressed</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">set</span> <span class="at">-e</span></span>
<span id="cb3-5"><a href="#cb3-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb3-6"><a href="#cb3-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">backup()</span> <span class="kw">{</span></span>
<span id="cb3-7"><a href="#cb3-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">cp</span> <span class="pp">*</span>.txt /backup</span>
<span id="cb3-8"><a href="#cb3-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">rm</span> <span class="pp">*</span>.txt</span>
<span id="cb3-9"><a href="#cb3-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span></span>
<span id="cb3-10"><a href="#cb3-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb3-11"><a href="#cb3-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">backup</span></span>
<span id="cb3-12"><a href="#cb3-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Backup successful&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a function used as a condition in a script where
<code>set -e</code> is enabled. This means that the function will run
without <code>set -e</code>, and will power through any errors.</p>
<p>This applies to <code>if</code>, <code>while</code>, and
<code>until</code> statements, commands negated with <code>!</code>, as
well as the left-hand side of <code>||</code> and
<code>&amp;&amp;</code>. It does not matter how deeply the command is
nested in such a structure.</p>
<p>In the problematic example, the intent was that an error like
<code>cp: error writing '/backup/important.txt': No space left on device</code>
would cause the script to abort. Instead, since the function is invoked
in an <code>if</code> statement, the script will proceed to delete all
the files even though it failed to back them up.</p>
<p>The fix is to call it outside of an <code>if</code> statement. There
is no point in checking whether the command succeeded, since the script
would abort if it didn't. You may also want to consider replacing
<code>set -e</code> with explicit <code>|| exit</code> after every
relevant command to avoid such surprises.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you don't care that the function runs without <code>set -e</code>,
you can disable this warning.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>BashFaq #105: <a href="https://mywiki.wooledge.org/BashFAQ/105">Why
doesn't set -e (or set -o errexit, or trap ERR) do what I
expected?</a></li>
</ul>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2311 – Bash implicitly disabled set -e for this function invocation because it's inside a command substitution. Add set -e; before it or enable inherit_errexit.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2311 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2311">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="bash-implicitly-disabled-set--e-for-this-function-invocation-because-its-inside-a-command-substitution-add-set--e-before-it-or-enable-inherit_errexit">Bash
implicitly disabled set -e for this function invocation because it's
inside a command substitution. Add set -e; before it or enable
inherit_errexit.</h2>
<p>(This warning is optional and must be explicitly enabled)</p>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/bash</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#shellcheck enable=check-set-e-suppressed</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">set</span> <span class="at">-e</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb1-6"><a href="#cb1-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">deploy()</span> <span class="kw">{</span></span>
<span id="cb1-7"><a href="#cb1-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="fu">make</span> <span class="at">-j</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">nproc</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> foo test</span>
<span id="cb1-8"><a href="#cb1-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="fu">cp</span> ./foo /var/www/example.com/cgi-bin</span>
<span id="cb1-9"><a href="#cb1-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="ex">./foo</span> <span class="at">--version</span> <span class="dv">2</span><span class="op">&gt;&amp;</span><span class="dv">1</span></span>
<span id="cb1-10"><a href="#cb1-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span></span>
<span id="cb1-11"><a href="#cb1-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb1-12"><a href="#cb1-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">version</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="ex">deploy</span><span class="va">)</span></span>
<span id="cb1-13"><a href="#cb1-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Successfully deployed </span><span class="va">$version</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/bash</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#shellcheck enable=check-set-e-suppressed</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">set</span> <span class="at">-e</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">shopt</span> <span class="at">-s</span> inherit_errexit</span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-7"><a href="#cb2-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">deploy()</span> <span class="kw">{</span></span>
<span id="cb2-8"><a href="#cb2-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="fu">make</span> <span class="at">-j</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">nproc</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> foo test</span>
<span id="cb2-9"><a href="#cb2-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="fu">cp</span> ./foo /var/www/example.com/cgi-bin</span>
<span id="cb2-10"><a href="#cb2-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="ex">./foo</span> <span class="at">--version</span> <span class="dv">2</span><span class="op">&gt;&amp;</span><span class="dv">1</span></span>
<span id="cb2-11"><a href="#cb2-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span></span>
<span id="cb2-12"><a href="#cb2-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-13"><a href="#cb2-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">version</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="ex">deploy</span><span class="va">)</span></span>
<span id="cb2-14"><a href="#cb2-14" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Successfully deployed </span><span class="va">$version</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a Bash function invoked in a command substitution
with <code>set -e</code> enabled.</p>
<p>Unlike other shells, Bash disables <code>set -e</code> in command
substitution by default. This means that the function will not exit on
error.</p>
<p>In the problematic code, the hope was that the function (and
therefore the script) would fail if the build and test suite failed.
Instead, the deployment continues even if the tests fail.</p>
<p>This can be fixed by either using
<code>version=$(set -e; deploy)</code> or by enabling
<code>inherit_errexit</code> as in the correct example.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you don't care that the function runs without <code>set -e</code>,
you can <a href="ignore">ignore</a> this warning.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <h1>SC2312 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2312">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="consider-invoking-this-command-separately-to-avoid-masking-its-return-value-or-use--true-to-ignore">Consider
invoking this command separately to avoid masking its return value (or
use '|| true' to ignore).</h2>
<h3 id="optional---check-extra-masked-returns">Optional -
<code>check-extra-masked-returns</code></h3>
<p>This is an <a href="optional">optional</a> rule, which means that it
has a special "long name" and is not enabled by default. See the <a
href="optional">optional</a> page for more details. In short, you have
to enable it with the long name instead of the "SC" code like you would
with a normal rule:</p>
<h4 id="shellcheckrc"><code>.shellcheckrc</code></h4>
<pre><code>enable=check-extra-masked-returns # SC2312</code></pre>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">set</span> <span class="at">-e</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">cd</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="ex">get_chroot_dir</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st">/etc&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">tar</span> xf <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${config}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">set</span> <span class="at">-e</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">dir</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="ex">get_chroot_dir</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">cd</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${dir}</span><span class="st">/etc&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">tar</span> xf <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${config}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code-with-correction">Correct code: (with
correction)</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">set</span> <span class="at">-e</span></span>
<span id="cb4-2"><a href="#cb4-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">dir</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="ex">get_chroot_dir</span><span class="va">)</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-3"><a href="#cb4-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">[[</span> <span class="ot">-d</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${dir}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="kw">]]</span> <span class="kw">||</span> <span class="bu">exit</span> 1</span>
<span id="cb4-4"><a href="#cb4-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">cd</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${dir}</span><span class="st">/etc&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-5"><a href="#cb4-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">tar</span> xf <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">${config}</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>In the problematic example, the exit code for
<code>get_chroot_dir</code> is ignored because it is used in a command
substitution in the argument of another command.</p>
<p>If the command shows <code>error: Can't determine chroot</code> and
exits with failure without outputting a directory, then the command
being run will be <code>cd "/etc"</code> and the script will proceed to
overwrite the host system's configuration.</p>
<p>By assigning it to a variable first, the exit code of the command
will propagate into the exit code of the assignment, so that it can be
checked explicitly with <code>if</code> or implicitly with
<code>set -e</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you don't care about the command's exit status, already handle it
through a side channel like <code>&lt;(cmd; echo $? &gt; status)</code>,
or (in the case of background processes and process substitution) wait
on the result like <code>&lt;(cmd) ; wait $!</code>, then you can either
<a href="ignore">ignore</a> the suggestion with a directive, or use
<code>|| true</code> (or <code>|| :</code>) to suppress it.</p>
<h4 id="handling-process-substitution-failures">Handling process
substitution failures</h4>
<p>Note that you can combine <a
href="https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Redirections.html#Duplicating-File-Descriptors">file
descriptor duplication</a> with <code>wait</code> to reference process
substitution output (or input) while retaining the exit codes of those
processes. For example:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb5"><pre
class="sourceCode bash"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb5-1"><a href="#cb5-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">generate_data()</span> <span class="kw">{</span></span>
<span id="cb5-2"><a href="#cb5-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="bu">declare</span> <span class="va">i</span></span>
<span id="cb5-3"><a href="#cb5-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">for</span> <span class="kw">((</span> <span class="va">i</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="dv">0</span> <span class="kw">;</span> <span class="va">i</span> <span class="op">&lt;</span> <span class="dv">5</span> <span class="kw">;</span> <span class="op">++</span><span class="va">i</span> <span class="kw">))</span></span>
<span id="cb5-4"><a href="#cb5-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb5-5"><a href="#cb5-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>        <span class="fu">date</span> <span class="at">-d</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$RANDOM</span><span class="st"> hours&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb5-6"><a href="#cb5-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">done</span></span>
<span id="cb5-7"><a href="#cb5-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span></span>
<span id="cb5-8"><a href="#cb5-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb5-9"><a href="#cb5-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">consume_data()</span> <span class="kw">{</span></span>
<span id="cb5-10"><a href="#cb5-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="bu">declare</span> <span class="va">line</span></span>
<span id="cb5-11"><a href="#cb5-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">while</span> <span class="va">IFS</span><span class="op">=</span> <span class="bu">read</span> <span class="at">-r</span> <span class="va">line</span></span>
<span id="cb5-12"><a href="#cb5-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">do</span></span>
<span id="cb5-13"><a href="#cb5-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>        <span class="bu">echo</span> Consuming line: <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$line</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb5-14"><a href="#cb5-14" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">done</span></span>
<span id="cb5-15"><a href="#cb5-15" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span></span>
<span id="cb5-16"><a href="#cb5-16" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb5-17"><a href="#cb5-17" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">declare</span> <span class="dt">\</span></span>
<span id="cb5-18"><a href="#cb5-18" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="va">input_file_descriptor</span> <span class="dt">\</span></span>
<span id="cb5-19"><a href="#cb5-19" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="va">process</span></span>
<span id="cb5-20"><a href="#cb5-20" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb5-21"><a href="#cb5-21" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># The following statement</span></span>
<span id="cb5-22"><a href="#cb5-22" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#</span></span>
<span id="cb5-23"><a href="#cb5-23" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># - uses process substitution to allow us to read the output of `generate_data`</span></span>
<span id="cb5-24"><a href="#cb5-24" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#   via a filename and</span></span>
<span id="cb5-25"><a href="#cb5-25" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># - duplicates the file descriptor for that file so that it is not</span></span>
<span id="cb5-26"><a href="#cb5-26" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#   immediately closed</span></span>
<span id="cb5-27"><a href="#cb5-27" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#</span></span>
<span id="cb5-28"><a href="#cb5-28" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Note that process substitution uses either `pipe(2)` or named pipes (FIFOs)</span></span>
<span id="cb5-29"><a href="#cb5-29" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># with `O_RDONLY` or `O_WRONLY`, and so the file descriptor that is duplicated</span></span>
<span id="cb5-30"><a href="#cb5-30" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># via `[N]&lt;&amp;WORD` is only opened for reads</span></span>
<span id="cb5-31"><a href="#cb5-31" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">exec</span> {input_file_descriptor}<span class="op">&lt;</span> <span class="op">&lt;(</span></span>
<span id="cb5-32"><a href="#cb5-32" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="ex">generate_data</span></span>
<span id="cb5-33"><a href="#cb5-33" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">)</span></span>
<span id="cb5-34"><a href="#cb5-34" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">process</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$!</span></span>
<span id="cb5-35"><a href="#cb5-35" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb5-36"><a href="#cb5-36" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Returns non-zero if `consume_data` does</span></span>
<span id="cb5-37"><a href="#cb5-37" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">consume_data</span> <span class="op">&lt;&amp;</span><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$input_file_descriptor</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb5-38"><a href="#cb5-38" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb5-39"><a href="#cb5-39" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Returns non-zero if `generate_data` does</span></span>
<span id="cb5-40"><a href="#cb5-40" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">wait</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$process</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>This can be particularly helpful with <code>readarray</code> for
robust array handling</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2313 – Quote array indices to avoid them expanding as globs.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2313 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2313">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="quote-array-indices-to-avoid-them-expanding-as-globs">Quote
array indices to avoid them expanding as globs.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">read</span> <span class="at">-r</span> <span class="va">foo[</span>index<span class="op">]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">read</span> <span class="at">-r</span> <span class="st">&quot;foo[index]&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found an array element passed to read, where the
<code>[]</code> was not quoted. This means the array index
<code>[index]</code> will be treated as a glob range, and the word may
be replaced or trigger <code>failglob</code>.</p>
<p>In the problematic example, having a directory named
<code>food</code> will cause the command to become
<code>read -r food</code> instead, since <code>food</code> matches the
glob <code>foo[index]</code>. The result is assigning a value to the
wrong variable.</p>
<p>Quote or escape the pattern as shown to ensure it always reads into
the array <code>foo</code> at index <code>index</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2314 – In bats, `!` does not cause a test failure.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2314 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2314">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2 id="in-bats--does-not-cause-a-test-failure">In bats, <code>!</code>
does not cause a test failure.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/usr/bin/env bats</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">@test</span> <span class="st">&quot;test&quot;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="co"># ... code</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="ot">! </span><span class="ex">test_file_exists</span></span>
<span id="cb1-6"><a href="#cb1-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="co"># ... more code</span></span>
<span id="cb1-7"><a href="#cb1-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="er">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/usr/bin/env bats</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">@test</span> <span class="st">&quot;test&quot;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="co"># ... code</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="ex">run</span> ! test_file_exists</span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="co"># ... more code</span></span>
<span id="cb2-7"><a href="#cb2-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="er">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Bats uses <code>set -e</code> and <code>trap ERR</code> to catch test
failures as early as possible. Although the return code of a
<code>!</code> negated command is inverted, they will never trigger
<code>errexit</code>, due to a bash design decision (see <a
href="#related-resources">Related Resources</a>). This means that tests
which use <code>!</code> can never fail.</p>
<p>Starting with bats 1.5.0 you can use <code>!</code> inside
<code>run</code>. If you are still using an older bats version, you can
rewrite <code>! &lt;command&gt;</code> to
<code>&lt;command&gt; &amp;&amp; exit 1</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>The return code of the last command in the test will be the exit code
of the test function. This means that you can use
<code>! &lt;command&gt;</code> on the last line of the test and it will
still fail appropriately. However, you are encouraged to still use
<code>run !</code> in this case for consistency.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li><p><a href="SC2251.md">SC2251: This ! is not on a condition and
skips errexit</a></p></li>
<li><p><a
href="https://stackoverflow.com/a/39582012/760746">Stackoverflow: Why do
I need parenthesis In bash <code>set -e</code> and negated return
code</a></p></li>
<li><p><a href="https://linux.die.net/man/1/bash">bash manpage</a> (look
at <code>trap [-lp] [[arg] sigspec ...]</code>):</p>
<blockquote>
<p>The ERR trap is not executed [...] if the command's return value is
being inverted via !</p>
</blockquote></li>
</ul>
