    <title>ShellCheck: SC2315 – In bats, `!` does not cause a test failure. Fold the `!` into the conditional!</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2315 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2315">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="in-bats--does-not-cause-a-test-failure-fold-the--into-the-conditional">In
bats, <code>!</code> does not cause a test failure. Fold the
<code>!</code> into the conditional!</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/usr/bin/env bats</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">@test</span> <span class="st">&quot;test&quot;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="co"># ... code</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="ot">! </span><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="va">$status</span> <span class="ot">==</span> 0 <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb1-6"><a href="#cb1-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="co"># ... more code</span></span>
<span id="cb1-7"><a href="#cb1-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="er">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/usr/bin/env bats</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">@test</span> <span class="st">&quot;test&quot;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="co"># ... code</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="va">$status</span> <span class="ot">!=</span> 0 <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="co"># ... more code</span></span>
<span id="cb2-7"><a href="#cb2-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="er">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>Bats uses <code>set -e</code> and <code>trap ERR</code> to catch test
failures as early as possible. Although the return code of a
<code>!</code> negated command is inverted, they will never trigger
<code>errexit</code>, due to a bash design decision (see <a
href="#related-resources">Related Resources</a>). This means that tests
which use <code>!</code> can never fail.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>The return code of the last command in the test will be the exit code
of the test function. This means that you can use
<code>! &lt;command&gt;</code> on the last line of the test and it will
still fail appropriately. However, you are encouraged to still transform
the code in this case for consistency.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li><p><a href="SC2314">SC2314: In bats, ! does not cause a test failure
(for non-conditionals)</a></p></li>
<li><p><a href="SC2251.md">SC2251: This ! is not on a condition and
skips errexit</a></p></li>
<li><p><a
href="https://stackoverflow.com/a/39582012/760746">Stackoverflow: Why do
I need parenthesis In bash <code>set -e</code> and negated return
code</a></p></li>
<li><p><a href="https://linux.die.net/man/1/bash">bash manpage</a> (look
at <code>trap [-lp] [[arg] sigspec ...]</code>):</p>
<blockquote>
<p>The ERR trap is not executed [...] if the command's return value is
being inverted via !</p>
</blockquote></li>
</ul>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2316 – This applies local to the variable named readonly, which is probably not what you want. Use a separate command or the appropriate `declare` options instead.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2316 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2316">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="this-applies-local-to-the-variable-named-readonly-which-is-probably-not-what-you-want-use-a-separate-command-or-the-appropriate-declare-options-instead">This
applies local to the variable named readonly, which is probably not what
you want. Use a separate command or the appropriate <code>declare</code>
options instead.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre
class="sourceCode bash"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">local</span> <span class="va">readonly</span> <span class="va">foo</span><span class="op">=</span>3</span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">readonly</span> <span class="va">export</span> <span class="va">bar</span><span class="op">=</span>4</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre
class="sourceCode bash"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">local</span> <span class="va">foo</span><span class="op">=</span>3</span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">readonly</span> <span class="va">foo</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">readonly</span> <span class="va">bar</span><span class="op">=</span>4</span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">export</span> <span class="va">bar</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre
class="sourceCode bash"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">declare</span> <span class="at">-r</span> <span class="va">foo</span><span class="op">=</span>3</span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">declare</span> <span class="at">-rx</span> <span class="va">bar</span><span class="op">=</span>4</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>In most languages, declaration modifiers like
<code>public</code>/<code>static</code>/<code>const</code> are keywords
and you can apply multiple to any declaration.</p>
<p>In shell scripting they are instead command names, and anything after
them is an argument. This means that <code>readonly local foo</code>
will create two readonly variables: <code>local</code>, and
<code>foo</code>. Neither will be local.</p>
<p>Instead, either use multiple commands, or use a single
<code>declare</code> command with appropriate flags
(<code>declare</code> will automatically make a variable local when
invoked in a function, unless <code>-g</code> is passed to explicitly
make it global).</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you want to name your variable <code>local</code>, you can quote
it as in <code>readonly "local"</code> to make your intention clear to
ShellCheck and other humans.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2317 – Command appears to be unreachable. Check usage (or ignore if invoked indirectly).</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2317 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2317">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="command-appears-to-be-unreachable-check-usage-or-ignore-if-invoked-indirectly">Command
appears to be unreachable. Check usage (or ignore if invoked
indirectly).</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">usage()</span> <span class="kw">{</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="op">&gt;&amp;</span><span class="dv">2</span> <span class="st">&quot;Usage: </span><span class="va">$0</span><span class="st"> -i input&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">exit</span> 1</span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span>     </span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$1</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;--help&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb1-6"><a href="#cb1-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-7"><a href="#cb1-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="ex">usage</span></span>
<span id="cb1-8"><a href="#cb1-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">exit</span> 0   <span class="co"># Unreachable</span></span>
<span id="cb1-9"><a href="#cb1-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">usage()</span> <span class="kw">{</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="op">&gt;&amp;</span><span class="dv">2</span> <span class="st">&quot;Usage: </span><span class="va">$0</span><span class="st"> -i input&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span>     </span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$1</span><span class="st">&quot;</span> <span class="ot">=</span> <span class="st">&quot;--help&quot;</span> <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="ex">usage</span></span>
<span id="cb2-7"><a href="#cb2-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">exit</span> 0</span>
<span id="cb2-8"><a href="#cb2-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>The problematic code wanted to exit with success if the user
explicitly asked for <code>--help</code>. However, since the
<code>usage</code> function already had an <code>exit 1</code>, this
statement could never run.</p>
<p>One possible solution is to change <code>usage()</code> to only echo,
and let callers be responsible for exiting.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck may incorrectly believe that code is unreachable if it's
invoked by variable name or in a trap. In such a case, please <a
href="Ignore">Ignore</a> the message.</p>
<p>Note in particular that since unreachable commands may come in
clusters, it's useful to use ShellCheck's filewide or functionwide
ignore directives. A <code>disable</code> directive before a function
ignores the entire function:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/bash</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">...</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># shellcheck disable=SC2317  # Don&#39;t warn about unreachable commands in this function</span></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">start()</span> <span class="kw">{</span></span>
<span id="cb3-5"><a href="#cb3-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> Starting</span>
<span id="cb3-6"><a href="#cb3-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="ex">/etc/init.d/foo</span> start</span>
<span id="cb3-7"><a href="#cb3-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span></span>
<span id="cb3-8"><a href="#cb3-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="st">&quot;</span><span class="va">$1</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-9"><a href="#cb3-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">exit</span> 0</span></code></pre></div>
<p>A disable directive after the shebang, before any commands, will
ignore the entire file:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/bash</span></span>
<span id="cb4-2"><a href="#cb4-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Test script #1</span></span>
<span id="cb4-3"><a href="#cb4-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># shellcheck disable=SC2317  # Don&#39;t warn about unreachable commands in this file</span></span>
<span id="cb4-4"><a href="#cb4-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb4-5"><a href="#cb4-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Temporarily disabled&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-6"><a href="#cb4-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">exit</span> 0</span>
<span id="cb4-7"><a href="#cb4-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb4-8"><a href="#cb4-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">run-test1</span></span>
<span id="cb4-9"><a href="#cb4-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">run-test2</span></span>
<span id="cb4-10"><a href="#cb4-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">run-test3</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Defined functions are assumed to be reachable when the script ends
(not exits) since another file may source and invoke them.</p>
<h3 id="more-problematic-code">More Problematic Code</h3>
<p>You have defined two functions in the same file you are sourcing
whose names are the same but defined differently within their bodies.
Then shellcheck will state that every line of the body of the earlier
seen function definition will be unreachable which is how bash would
operate when sourcing the file. It <strong>unclear</strong> what
shellcheck would output if the earlier definition appeared in a
difference file that was seen first. Apparently doing a quick test. It
does <strong>NOT</strong> notice.</p>

  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2318 – This assignment is used again in this `declare`, but won't have taken effect. Use two `declare`s.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2318 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2318">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="this-assignment-is-used-again-in-this-declare-but-wont-have-taken-effect-use-two-declares">This
assignment is used again in this <code>declare</code>, but won't have
taken effect. Use two <code>declare</code>s.</h2>
<p>(or <code>local</code>, <code>typeset</code>, <code>readonly</code>,
<code>export</code>)</p>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">declare</span> <span class="at">-i</span> <span class="va">first</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$1</span> <span class="va">current</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$first</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">declare</span> <span class="at">-i</span> <span class="va">first</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$1</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">declare</span> <span class="at">-i</span> <span class="va">current</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$first</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>When assigning variables via a command, such as <code>declare</code>,
<code>typeset</code>, <code>local</code> etc, the expansion of all
arguments happen before all assignments. This means that you can't have
a variable assigned and then referenced in the same command.</p>
<p>In the example, if <code>$1</code> is 42, the arguments will first be
expanded in the current environment into
<code>-i first=42 current=</code>. They will then be passed to
<code>declare</code> which will perform the assignments.</p>
<p>To correctly set <code>current=$first</code> so that it uses the new
value of <code>first</code>, use two separate commands as shown.</p>
<p>Note that this only applies when assigning via commands, because
arguments are always expanded before commands are invoked. If assigning
without a command, as in <code>first=$1 current=$first</code>, it will
work as expected.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you want to reference the value as it existed before the command,
e.g. if swapping variables with <code>declare x=$y y=$x</code>, you can
ignore this message. However, consider rewriting it anyways for the
benefit of any humans reading the code.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2319 – This `$?` refers to a condition, not a command. Assign to a variable to avoid it being overwritten.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2319 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2319">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="this--refers-to-a-condition-not-a-command-assign-to-a-variable-to-avoid-it-being-overwritten">This
<code>$?</code> refers to a condition, not a command. Assign to a
variable to avoid it being overwritten.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">mycommand</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="va">$?</span> <span class="ot">-ne</span> 0 <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="va">$?</span> <span class="ot">-ne</span> 14 <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Command failed&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">mycommand</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">[</span> <span class="va">$?</span> <span class="ot">-gt</span> 0 <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="bu">exit</span> <span class="va">$?</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">mycommand</span></span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">ret</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$?</span></span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="va">$ret</span> <span class="ot">-ne</span> 0 <span class="bu">]</span> <span class="kw">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="va">$ret</span> <span class="ot">-ne</span> 14 <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb3-4"><a href="#cb3-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb3-5"><a href="#cb3-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Command failed&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb3-6"><a href="#cb3-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">mycommand</span> <span class="kw">||</span> <span class="bu">exit</span> <span class="va">$?</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a <code>$?</code> that always refers to a condition
like <code>[ .. ]</code>, <code>[[ .. ]]</code>, or
<code>test</code>.</p>
<p>This most commonly happens when trying to inspect <code>$?</code>
before doing something with it, such as inspecting it again or exiting
with it, without realizing that any such inspection will also overwrite
<code>$?</code>.</p>
<p>In the first problematic example, <code>[ $? -ne 14 ]</code> will
never be true because it only runs after <code>[ $? -ne 0 ]</code> has
modified $? to be 0. The solution is to assign <code>$?</code> from
<code>mycommand</code> to a variable so that the variable can be
inspected repeatedly.</p>
<p>In the second problematic example, <code>exit $?</code> will always
<code>exit 0</code>, because it only runs if <code>[ $? -gt 0 ]</code>
returns success and sets <code>$?</code> to 0. The solution could again
be to assign <code>$?</code> to a variable first, or (as shown) use
<code>mycommand || exit $?</code> as there is no condition to overwrite
<code>$?</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None. Note that ShellCheck does not warn if the usage of
<code>$?</code> after <code>[ .. ]</code> is unconditional, as in
<code>[ -d dir ]; return $?</code>.</p>

<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <h2
id="this--refers-to-echoprintf-not-a-previous-command-assign-to-variable-to-avoid-it-being-overwritten">This
<code>$?</code> refers to echo/printf, not a previous command. Assign to
variable to avoid it being overwritten.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">mycommand</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Command exited with </span><span class="va">$?</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="va">$?</span> <span class="ot">-ne</span> 0 <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Failed&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-6"><a href="#cb1-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">mycommand</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">ret</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$?</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Command exited with </span><span class="va">$ret</span><span class="st">&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> <span class="bu">[</span> <span class="va">$ret</span> <span class="ot">-ne</span> 0 <span class="bu">]</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">then</span></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Failed&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-7"><a href="#cb2-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">fi</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a <code>$?</code> that always refers to
<code>echo</code> or <code>printf</code>.</p>
<p>This most commonly happens when trying to show <code>$?</code> before
doing something with it, without realizing that any such action will
also overwrite <code>$?</code>.</p>
<p>In the problematic example,
<code>echo "Command exited with $?"</code> was intended to show the exit
code before acting on it, but the act of showing <code>$?</code> also
overwrote it, so the condition is always false. The solution is to
assign <code>$?</code> to a variable first, so that it can be used
repeatedly.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you intentionally refer to <code>echo</code> to get the result of
a write, you can ignore this message. Alternatively, write it out as in
<code>if echo $$ &gt; "$pidfile"; then status=0; else status=1; fi</code></p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2321 – Array indices are already arithmetic contexts. Prefer removing the `$((` and `))`.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2321 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2321">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="array-indices-are-already-arithmetic-contexts-prefer-removing-the--and-">Array
indices are already arithmetic contexts. Prefer removing the
<code>$((</code> and <code>))</code>.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">values</span><span class="op">[</span><span class="va">$((i</span><span class="op">+</span><span class="dv">1</span><span class="va">))</span><span class="op">]=</span>1</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">values</span><span class="op">[</span>i+1<span class="op">]=</span>1</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>In indexed arrays (but not associative ones), the array index is
already an arithmetic context. There is no point or value in wrapping it
in an additional, explicit <code>$((..))</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If ShellCheck has failed to realize that your array is associative,
or if you for stylistic reasons prefer the redundancy, you can ignore
this message.</p>

    <title>ShellCheck: SC2322 – In arithmetic contexts, `((x))` is the same as `(x)`. Prefer only one layer of parentheses.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2322 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2322">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="in-arithmetic-contexts-x-is-the-same-as-x-prefer-only-one-layer-of-parentheses">In
arithmetic contexts, <code>((x))</code> is the same as <code>(x)</code>.
Prefer only one layer of parentheses.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">value</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$((</span> ((<span class="va">offset</span> <span class="op">+</span> <span class="va">index</span>)) <span class="op">*</span> <span class="dv">512</span> <span class="va">))</span> </span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">value</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$((</span> (<span class="va">offset</span> <span class="op">+</span> <span class="va">index</span>) <span class="op">*</span> <span class="dv">512</span> <span class="va">))</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found doubly nested parentheses in an arithmetic
expression. While the syntax for an arithmetic expansion is
<code>$((..))</code>, this does not imply that parentheses in the
expression should also be doubled. <code>(x)</code>, <code>((x))</code>,
and <code>(((x)))</code> are all identical, so you might as well use
only one layer of parentheses.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>This is a stylistic suggestion. If you prefer keeping both
parentheses, you can <a href="ignore">ignore</a> this message.</p>

    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2323 – `a[(x)]` is the same as `a[x]`. Prefer not wrapping in additional parentheses.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2323 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2323">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="ax-is-the-same-as-ax-prefer-not-wrapping-in-additional-parentheses"><code>a[(x)]</code>
is the same as <code>a[x]</code>. Prefer not wrapping in additional
parentheses.</h2>
<p>Similarly <code>$(( (x) ))</code> is the same as
<code>$(( x ))</code>, <code>(( (x) ))</code> is the same as
<code>(( x ))</code>.</p>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">array</span><span class="op">[</span>(x+1)<span class="op">]=</span>val</span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="va">$((</span> (<span class="va">x</span><span class="op">+</span><span class="dv">1</span>) <span class="va">))</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">array</span><span class="op">[</span>x+1<span class="op">]=</span>val</span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="va">$((x</span><span class="op">+</span><span class="dv">1</span><span class="va">))</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found an entire arithmetic expression wrapped in
parentheses. This does not serve a purpose since the expression is
already clearly delimited by the construct it's in, such as
<code>array[..]=</code> or <code>$((..))</code> in the example.</p>
<p>Note: ShellCheck does <em>not</em> warn about redundant parentheses
in subexpressions, such as <code>(a*b)+c</code>. Feel free to use
parentheses to clarify the order of operations any way you'd like.
ShellCheck only emits this suggestion when the <em>entire</em>
expression is wrapped <em>twice</em>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you prefer having an extra layer of parentheses for stylistic
reasons, you can <a href="ignore">ignore</a> this message.</p>

<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2324 – var+=1 will append, not increment. Use (( var += 1 )), declare -i var, or quote number to silence.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2324 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2324">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="var1-will-append-not-increment-use--var--1--declare--i-var-or-quote-number-to-silence">var+=1
will append, not increment. Use (( var += 1 )), declare -i var, or quote
number to silence.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span>2 <span class="va">n</span><span class="op">=</span>3</span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">+=</span><span class="va">$n</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<p>In bash/ksh, use an <code>(( arithmetic context ))</code></p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">((</span> <span class="va">var</span> <span class="op">+=</span> <span class="va">n</span> <span class="kw">))</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>or declare the variable as an integer type:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">declare</span> <span class="at">-i</span> <span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span>2</span>
<span id="cb3-2"><a href="#cb3-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">n</span><span class="op">=</span>4</span>
<span id="cb3-3"><a href="#cb3-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">+=</span><span class="va">$n</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>For POSIX sh, use an <code>$((arithmetic expansion))</code>:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$((var</span><span class="op">+</span><span class="va">n))</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>The problematic code attempts to add 2 and 3 to get 5.</p>
<p>Instead, <code>+=</code> on a string variable will concatenate, so
the result is 23.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>If you <em>do</em> want to concatenate a number, for example to
append trailing zeroes, you can silence the warning by quoting the
number:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb5"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb5-1"><a href="#cb5-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">+=</span><span class="st">&quot;000&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>

<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2325 – Multiple ! in front of pipelines are a bash/ksh extension. Use only 0 or 1.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2325 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2325">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="multiple--in-front-of-pipelines-are-a-bashksh-extension-use-only-0-or-1">Multiple
! in front of pipelines are a bash/ksh extension. Use only 0 or 1.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/sh</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ot">! ! </span><span class="fu">true</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/sh</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">true</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>POSIX (and Dash) does not allow multiple <code>!</code> pipeline
negations in a row. It's also logically unnecessary.</p>
<p>Use either zero or one <code>!</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>Scripts whose shebang declares it will run with Ksh and Bash will not
trigger this warning.</p>
<p>If you really want to negate multiple times on POSIX or Dash, e.g. to
normalize exit codes to 0 or 1, use <code>cmd || false</code> or a
command group:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ot">! </span><span class="kw">{</span> <span class="ot">! </span><span class="fu">true</span><span class="kw">;</span> <span class="kw">}</span> </span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2326 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2326">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="-is-not-allowed-in-the-middle-of-pipelines-use-command-group-as-in-cmd----cmd--if-necessary">!
is not allowed in the middle of pipelines. Use command group as in
<code>cmd | { ! cmd; }</code> if necessary.</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">cat</span> <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="ot">! </span><span class="fu">tee</span> /dev/full</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<p>Either negate the entire pipeline (this is equivalent unless
<code>pipefail</code> is set):</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ot">! </span><span class="fu">cat</span> <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="fu">tee</span> /dev/full</span></code></pre></div>
<p>Or use a command group to negate a single stage:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb3"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb3-1"><a href="#cb3-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">cat</span> <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="kw">{</span> <span class="ot">! </span><span class="fu">tee</span> /dev/full<span class="kw">;</span> <span class="kw">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p><a
href="https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/utilities/V3_chap02.html#tag_18_09_02">POSIX
specifies</a> that a status negation operator <code>!</code> is only
used to negate the status of an entire pipeline, not individual
stages.</p>
<p>By default the status of a pipeline is that of the last command, so
use <code>!</code> in front of the pipeline to negate as necessary.</p>
<p>If you have set the option <code>pipefail</code> to OR the status of
each stage together, and want to negate the status of only a single
stage, you can use negate inside a
<code>{ ! command group; }</code>.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>Ksh supports <code>!</code> in front of individual pipeline stages.
ShellCheck does not warn when the shebang declares that the script will
run with Ksh.</p>
<h3 id="related-resources">Related resources:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>
    <hr />
    <p style='font-size: 80%'><a href="https://www.shellcheck.net">ShellCheck</a> is a static analysis tool for shell scripts. This page is part of its documentation.</p>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes" />
    <title>ShellCheck: SC2328 – This redirection takes output away from the command substitution.</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css" />
  </head>
  <body style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; max-width: 800px">
    <h1>SC2328 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2328">See this page on GitHub</a>
    <p style="display: none"><a href="index.html">Sitemap</a></p>
    <hr />
    <h2
id="this-redirection-takes-output-away-from-the-command-substitution">This
redirection takes output away from the command substitution.</h2>
<p>(and companion warning "This command substitution will be empty
because the command's output gets redirected away" which points to the
relevant command substitution)</p>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">tr</span> <span class="at">-d</span> <span class="st">&#39;:&#39;</span> <span class="op">&lt;</span> input.txt <span class="op">&gt;</span> output.txt<span class="va">)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># If the output should be captured INSTEAD OF being written to file</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">tr</span> <span class="at">-d</span> <span class="st">&#39;:&#39;</span> <span class="op">&lt;</span> input.txt<span class="va">)</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># If the output should be captured IN ADDITION to being written to file</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="va">var</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="va">$(</span><span class="fu">tr</span> <span class="at">-d</span> <span class="st">&#39;:&#39;</span> <span class="op">&lt;</span> input.txt <span class="kw">|</span> <span class="fu">tee</span> output.txt<span class="va">)</span></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb2-7"><a href="#cb2-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># If the output should NOT BE captured at all</span></span>
<span id="cb2-8"><a href="#cb2-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">tr</span> <span class="at">-d</span> <span class="st">&#39;:&#39;</span> <span class="op">&lt;</span> input.txt <span class="op">&gt;</span> output.txt</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck has found a command substitution (<code>$(..)</code>,
<code>`..`</code>) that appears to never capture any output because the
command's output is being redirected.</p>
<p>Decide whether you want the output to be captured (by removing the
redirection), to go into wherever it's redirected (by not running the
command in a command substitution), or both (by using <code>tee</code>
to copy the output to both file and stdout).</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>None</p>

<ul>
<li>Help by adding links to BashFAQ, StackOverflow, man pages, POSIX,
etc!</li>
</ul>

    <h1>SC2329 – ShellCheck Wiki</h1>
    <a href="https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/SC2329">See this page on GitHub</a>

    <hr />
    <h2
id="this-function-is-never-invoked-check-usage-or-ignored-if-invoked-indirectly">This
function is never invoked. Check usage (or ignored if invoked
indirectly).</h2>
<h3 id="problematic-code">Problematic code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb1"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb1-1"><a href="#cb1-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/sh</span></span>
<span id="cb1-2"><a href="#cb1-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">f()</span> <span class="kw">{</span></span>
<span id="cb1-3"><a href="#cb1-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb1-4"><a href="#cb1-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span></span>
<span id="cb1-5"><a href="#cb1-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">exit</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="correct-code">Correct code:</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb2"><pre class="sourceCode sh"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb2-1"><a href="#cb2-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">#!/bin/sh</span></span>
<span id="cb2-2"><a href="#cb2-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">f()</span> <span class="kw">{</span></span>
<span id="cb2-3"><a href="#cb2-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">echo</span> <span class="st">&quot;Hello World&quot;</span></span>
<span id="cb2-4"><a href="#cb2-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">}</span></span>
<span id="cb2-5"><a href="#cb2-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">f</span></span>
<span id="cb2-6"><a href="#cb2-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">exit</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rationale">Rationale:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck found a function that goes out of scope before it's ever
invoked. Verify that the function is called. It could be misspelled, or
its invocation could also be unreachable (as in
<code>f() { ..; }; exit; f</code>).</p>
<p>Note that if the example script did not end in <code>exit</code>,
this warning would not be emitted. This is because the function could be
invoked by another script that <code>source</code>s it.</p>
<h3 id="exceptions">Exceptions:</h3>
<p>ShellCheck is currently bad at figuring out functions that are
invoked via <code>trap</code>. In such cases, please <a
href="ignore">ignore</a> the message with a directive.</p>
